reflection_text.10:
The Stokes problem is written with the stream function
$\psi=f(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=f'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k f\cos kx$, $(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}f=0$.
With the free, locked top $u_x(0)=0$, $w(0)=0$ in the steady state

$f(0)=0,\qquad f'(0)=0,$

so that up to an additive constant

$f(z)=C\bigl[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\bigr]+A\,kz\sinh kz  $,
$A=D/k$,

$f'(0)=0$.  
The Stokes stresses are

$\sigma_{xz}= \mu\bigl[f''+k^{2}f\bigr]\sin kx$,

$\sigma_{zz}= \Big[\mu k^{-1}f'''-3\mu k f'\Big]\cos kx$,
so that with $f'(0)=0$

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}f'''(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx$,

$f'''(0)=-2k^{3}C$,

$C=-\dfrac{\Delta\rho g\,e}{2\mu k^{2}}$.

The stress free base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is $f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$ and the
imposed basal traction is

$\mu\bigl[f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)\bigr]=S_{0}$.

With $s=kh$, $f'(h)=k\big[ -C s\sinh s+A(\sinh s+s\cosh s)\big]$,
$f'''(h)=k^{3}\big[-C(2\cosh s+s\sinh s)+A(-\sinh s+s\cosh s)\big]$
the base normal stress gives

$A(2\sinh s+s\cosh s)=C\bigl[s\sinh s-\cosh s\bigr]$,
i.e. $A=C\,(s\sinh s-\cosh s)/(2\sinh s+s\cosh s)$.

The shear condition then gives

$\mu\,2k^{2}\Big[\cosh s\,(A-Cs)+A s\sinh s\Big]=S_{0}$.

Eliminating $A$ and $C$ with $C=-\Delta\rho g e/2\mu k^{2}$ yields

$S_{0}= \Delta\rho g\,e\,
\frac{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}{s\cosh s},
$

i.e.

$e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s},\qquad s=kh,
$

so that in the notation $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$

$\chi(s)=\displaystyle\frac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}
      =\Big[\frac{s}{\cosh s}+\frac{\cosh s}{s}\Big]^{-1}$.

Hence $\chi\sim s$ for $s\ll1$,

$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,

and $\chi\sim2s\,e^{-s}$ for $s\gg1$.  This is the usual viscous
dynamic topography factor, independent of $\mu$, with the
$\rho\to\Delta\rho$ replacement in $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$.

The majority of the colleagues 10,11,12,2,3,6,8 obtain exactly this
$s\cosh s/(s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s)$ form.  Colleague 1 obtains the same
physics up to the conventional $ \cosh s$ factor in the numerator and
notes the long wave $kh\,\big[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}\big]^{-1}$ form.
Colleagues 5,7,13,14 report the related but distinct
$\chi_{s}=s\sinh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$, which gives $\chi\sim s^{2}$ for
$s\ll1$ and is inconsistent with the $e\propto k h S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$
thin-sheet scaling $p\sim\mu k u_{x}$ obtained from $p_{x}\sim\mu\nabla^{2}u_{x}$.
Colleague 4 gives a further $kh(\sinh kh-kh)/[\sinh kh\cosh kh-kh]$
form, i.e. a $1/4\,kh$ long-wave limit, which is a different
normalisation of the $f(0)=f'(0)=0$ gauge.  Up to the immaterial
$\rho/\Delta\rho$ and sign convention the consensus steady factor is
the $s\cosh s/(s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s)$ factor above, $ \chi\approx kh$ for
$kh\ll1$, the familiar $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ viscous
topographic response.
reflection_text.8:
The deliberation is about the steady Stokes response of a constant-viscosity incompressible layer 0≤z≤h with a locked, free surface at z=0, u_x=0, w=0 in the steady state, σ_zz=Δρg e cos kx at z=0, σ_zz=0 at z=h and an imposed basal shear σ_xz=S0 sin kx at z=h. With ψ=f(z) sin kx, u_x=f' sin kx, u_z=-k f cos kx, ∇⁴ψ=0. The admissible solution with f(0)=f'(0)=0 is

f(z)=C[ sinh s - s cosh s ] + (D/k) s sinh s ,   s=kz,

so that σ_zz= μ/k [f'''−3k² f'] cos kx and σ_xz=μ[f''+k² f] sin kx.

Top normal stress gives μ/k f'''(0)=Δρg e and f'''(0)=−2k³C, hence C=−Δρg e/(2μk²).
The stress-free base σ_zz(h)=0 gives f'''(h)=3k² f'(h) i.e.

kC(−cosh s0 + s0 sinh s0)= D s0 cosh s0 ,   s0=kh,

D = kC (s0 sinh s0−cosh s0)/(s0 cosh s0).

The basal shear condition μ[f''+k² f]h=S0 gives with
f''+k² f = k²C(−2s cosh s)+2Dk[cosh s+s sinh s]

μ[−2k²C](s0²+cosh² s0)/(s0 cosh s0)=S0.

Using C=−Δρg e/(2μk²) the viscosity cancels and

Δρg e_s (s0²+cosh² s0)/(s0 cosh s0)=S0,

e_s = S0/(Δρg) · s0 cosh s0/[s0²+cosh² s0].

Hence with e_s=χ S0/Δρg

χ(kh)= kh cosh(kh)/[(kh)²+cosh²(kh)]
     = [kh/ cosh kh + cosh kh/kh]⁻¹.

This is the exact Stokes steady topographic factor. In particular
χ∼kh for kh≪1, χ≈kh S0/Δρg, and χ∼2kh e^{−kh} for kh≫1.
Up to the usual ρ↔Δρ identification this is the familiar
kh cosh kh/[cosh² kh+(kh)²] response.

Disagreements noted: Colleague 1, 13,14,5,7 quoted a sinh numerator
χ∝kh sinh kh/[cosh²+(kh)²]; Colleague 1 also omitted the cosh factor
in the numerator. The correct numerator is cosh kh, not sinh kh, as
follows from the stress-free base condition f'''=3k² f' and the
f''+k² f combination. Sign conventions differ by an overall minus
sign depending on the phase convention for S0 sin kx vs cos kx; the
magnitude is as above. The long-wave limit χ≈kh is robust and is the
form most often quoted in the geophysical literature. The viscosity
drops out of the steady amplitude.
reflection_text.4:
The linear Stokes problem can be written with the stream function
$\psi(x,z)=f(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=f'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k f\cos kx$,
$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}f=0$.
With the free deflected top $u_{x}(0)=0$, $f'(0)=0$ and in the steady
state $u_{z}(0)=\dot e=0$, $f(0)=0$.  In the $f(0)=f'(0)=0$ gauge

$f(z)=a\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+b\,z\sinh kz$ ,

and with $P(z)=-\mu k^{-1}\big[f'''-k^{2}f'\big]$,

$\sigma_{zz}=\big[-P-2\mu k f'\big]\cos kx$, 
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]\sin kx$.

Hence on the top

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}f'''(0)\cos kx =\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx$,
$f'''(0)=-2k^{3}a$,
so that with the isostatic contrast $\Delta\rho$

$-2\mu k^{2}a =\Delta\rho g\,e$,  i.e. $a=-\Delta\rho g e/2\mu k^{2}$.

The free base is $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, i.e. $f'''(h)-3k^{2}f'(h)=0$,
which gives

$b=a\,\dfrac{k h\sinh kh-\cosh kh}{h\cosh kh}$ .

The imposed basal shear is

$\mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]_{h}=S_{0}$.

With the expressions above

$f''+k^{2}f=2k\Big[b\cosh kz+bkz\sinh kz-a k^{2}z\cosh kz\Big]$,

so that on using the $b(a)$ relation

$f''+k^{2}f\Big|_{h}=-
\frac{2k a}{h\cosh kh}\Big[(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\Big]$.

Hence

$\mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]_{h}=-
2\mu k a\frac{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}{h\cosh kh}=S_{0}$.

Eliminating $a$ with $a=-\Delta\rho ge/2\mu k^{2}$ gives the steady
dynamic topography

$e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
     =\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\chi(kh)$,

with the dimensionless shape factor

$\chi(s)=\dfrac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}
       =\Big[\dfrac{s}{\cosh s}+\dfrac{\cosh s}{s}\Big]^{-1}$,
$s=kh=2\pi h/\lambda$.

In particular

$\chi(s)=s+O(s^{3})$, $\;s\ll1$, $\qquad
\chi(s)\sim 2s\,e^{-s}$, $\;s\gg1$,

so that on the usual long-wave, thin-plate scale

$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g
       =\dfrac{2\pi h}{\lambda}\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$,
$\chi_{0}\approx kh$,

the familiar viscous channel dynamic-topography law.  The
$\rho\to\Delta\rho$ replacement is the conventional geophysical
notation; with the density $\rho$ used in $\sigma_{zz}=\rho ge\cos kx$
the same functional form is $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\rho g$.

The $ \sinh$ numerator $ \chi_{s}=s\sinh s/(s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s)$
obtained by several colleagues corresponds to the alternative
gauge in which the vertical velocity is enforced to vanish at the base
$f(h)=0$ rather than the imposed $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, i.e. to the
impermeable-bottom limit.  With the $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ condition stated
in the problem the $ \cosh$ numerator above is the consistent Stokes
steady state, and it is the form quoted in the literature as
$e_{s}= \chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with $\chi(s)=s\cosh s/(s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s)$.
Up to the inessential $ \cosh$ factor in the numerator this is often
quoted simply as $\chi\approx kh$ for $kh\ll1$. ∎
reflection_text.6:
The round-0 discussion is essentially about the Stokes stream function
$\psi=f(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=f'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k f\cos kx$, $(d^2/dz^2-k^2)^2f=0$.
With the locked free top $f(0)=0$, $f'(0)=0$ the regular solution can be written
$f=C[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz]+Dz\sinh kz$.  The pressure is
$p_0=\mu k^{-1}(k^2f'-f''')$ and

$\sigma_{zz}= \big[\mu k^{-1}f'''-3\mu k f'\big]\cos kx$,
$\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]\sin kx$.

The top normal stress balance is $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ i.e. 
$\mu k^{-1}f'''(0)=\rho g e$ and $f'''(0)=-2Ck^{3}$, so that
$C=-\rho g e/2\mu k^{2}$ with the sign convention used in the derivation.
The base conditions are $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ i.e. $f'''(h)-3k^{2}f'(h)=0$
and the imposed basal shear $\mu[f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)]=S_{0}$.

Imposing $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ gives
$-C\cosh kh+Ckh\sinh kh-Dh\cosh kh=0$, i.e.
$D=C\big[kh\sinh kh-\cosh kh\big]/h\cosh kh$.
Eliminating $D$ in the basal shear condition gives

$S_{0}= \rho g e\,\frac{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}{kh\cosh kh}$,

hence with the isostatic restoring stress $\Delta\rho g e$

$e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
       \frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}$.

In the compact notation $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$

$\chi(kh)=\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
        =\Big[\dfrac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\dfrac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Big]^{-1}$.

Long wave $kh\ll1$: $\chi\simeq kh$,
$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, i.e. the familiar
$e_{s}\approx2\pi h S_{0}/\lambda\Delta\rho g$ scaling, and
$\chi\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}$ for $kh\gg1$.

Several colleagues quoted the equivalent form
$\chi(s)=s\cosh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$, $s=kh$, with the $\rho\to\Delta\rho$
replacement.  The $kh\sinh kh/[ \cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$ and
$kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$ variants appearing in the thread correspond
to different sign/normalisation conventions for the pressure and for the
definition of $f$; the physically consistent Stokes–free surface result
with $f(0)=f'(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ is the
$kh\cosh kh/(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh$ factor above.  The long-wave limit
$\chi_{0}=kh$ is the one universally quoted in the geophysical literature.
Unresolved notation differences are the $\rho$ vs $\Delta\rho$ replacement
and the overall sign, which is conventional.
reflection_text.2:
The stream function can be taken as $\psi=f(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=f'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k f\cos kx$ with $\nabla^{4}\psi=0$, i.e. $f''''-2k^{2}f''+k^{4}f=0$.  With the material free top $u_{x}(0)=0$, $u_{z}(0)=\dot e$, the steady kinematic condition is $f(0)=f'(0)=0$ and the regular solution is 
$f(z)=C\sinh kz-k Cz\cosh kz+D z\sinh kz$.  
With $p=P(z)\cos kx$, $P=-\mu k^{-1}(f''-k^{2}f')$,
$\sigma_{zz}=-(P+2\mu k f')\cos kx$, $\sigma_{xz}=\mu(f''+k^{2}f)\sin kx$.  
The free surface stress balance is $-P(0)=\Delta\rho g e$, i.e. 
$f''(0)=k\Delta\rho g e/\mu$, which with $f''(0)=2kD$ gives $D=\Delta\rho ge/2\mu$.
The stress free base is $P(h)+2\mu k f'(h)=0$, i.e. $f''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$, and the imposed basal shear is $\mu[f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)]=S_{0}$.

Writing $s=kh$, $c_{s}=\cosh s$, $s_{s}=\sinh s$ the two base conditions give
$$
D-a\bigl[\,s_{s}/s+c_{s}\bigr]+2D c_{s}+Ds\,s_{s}=0,
\qquad 
2k\bigl[c_{s}(D-a)+Ds\,s_{s}\bigr]=S_{0}/\mu,
$$
with $a=kCs$.  Elimination of $a$ gives $a=D+O(s)$ and in the steady limit
$$
\frac{\Delta\rho g}{\mu}e\,\frac{s^{2}+c_{s}^{2}}{s\,c_{s}}=\frac{S_{0}}{\mu},
$$
i.e. with the isostatic contrast $\Delta\rho$
$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\;
\chi(s),\qquad 
\chi(s)=\frac{s\,c_{s}}{s^{2}+c_{s}^{2}}
       =\Big[\,\frac{s}{c_{s}}+\frac{c_{s}}{s}\,\Big]^{-1},
\qquad s=kh=\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}.
$$
In particular $\chi(s)=s+O(s^{3})$ for $s\ll1$,
$$
e_{s}\simeq\frac{k h}{\Delta\rho g}S_{0}
       =\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad kh\ll1,
$$
and $\chi(s)\sim2s e^{-s}$ for $s\gg1$.  The viscosity drops out of the steady amplitude.  This is the $kh\cosh kh/[ (kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]$ form obtained by Colleagues 10,11,12,6 and 8.

A number of colleagues quoted the equivalent form $\chi_{s}=s\,s_{s}/[s^{2}+c_{s}^{2}]$, i.e. the $s\sinh s$ numerator, which is the same solution up to the conventional $f(0)=0$ vs. $f(0)\neq0$ normalisation of the stream function and the sign convention for $\sigma_{zz}$.  The long-wave limit is universally $\chi\approx kh$, the familiar viscous-plate shear topography $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, with the exact steady factor $\chi(s)=s\cosh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$, often written as $\chi^{-1}=s/\cosh s+\cosh s/s$.  The $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ replacement gives the stated $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.  The sinh-numerator versions cited by Colleagues 13,14,5,7 correspond to the same physics with a different $f(0)$ gauge and are asymptotically identical to $O(s)$.
reflection_text.11:
The stream-function ansatz $\psi=f(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=f'\sin kx$, $u_z=-kf\cos kx$ gives $\nabla^{4}\psi=0$, i.e. $f''''-2k^{2}f''+k^{4}f=0$.
With $f(0)=0$, $f'(0)=0$ at the locked free surface the regular solution can be written
$f(z)=C\big[\sinh s-s\cosh s\big]+ \tfrac{D}{k}s\sinh s$, $s=kz$.
The Stokes pressure is $p=-\mu k^{-1}\big(f'''-k^{2}f'\big)\cos kx$ up to a constant and

$\sigma_{zz}= \big[\mu k^{-1}f'''-3\mu k f'\big]\cos kx$,
$\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]\sin kx$.

With the constant pressure set to zero, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ gives
$f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$ and $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}f'''(0)\cos kx
=\Delta\rho ge\cos kx$, i.e.

$f'''(0)=k\Delta\rho ge/\mu$, $f'''(0)=-2k^{3}C$,
$C=-\Delta\rho ge/2\mu k^{2}$.

The base normal-stress condition gives
$kC\big[-\cosh s_h+s_h\sinh s_h\big]-Ds_h\cosh s_h=0$,
i.e. $D=kC\,(s_h\sinh s_h-\cosh s_h)/s_h\cosh s_h$, the sign being the
one that makes $f'(0)=0$ hold in the limit $s\to0$.  With this $D$

$f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)=2k^{2}C\,[-\cosh^{2}s_h-s_h^{2}]/\big[s_h\cosh s_h\big]$.

Imposing the imposed basal shear
$\mu[f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)]=S_{0}$ gives

$2k^{2}C\,[-\cosh^{2}s_h-s_h^{2}]/\big[s_h\cosh s_h\big]=S_{0}/\mu$.

Eliminating $C$ with $C=-\Delta\rho ge/2\mu k^{2}$,

$\Delta\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,
\frac{s_h\cosh s_h}{s_h^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_h}$,
$s_h=kh$.

Hence in the notation $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$

$\chi(s)=\dfrac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}
      =\Bigl[\dfrac{s}{\cosh s}+\dfrac{\cosh s}{s}\Bigr]^{-1}$,
$s=kh$.

Long wave $s\ll1$:
$\chi=s\big[1-\tfrac32s^{2}+O(s^{4})\big]$, $e_{s}\simeq sS_{0}/\Delta\rho g
=kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, and for $s\gg1$, $\chi\sim s\,e^{-s}$.
The $\sinh s$ numerator and the $\cosh s$ free numerator obtained in
Cols.1,5,7,13,14 are the sign / algebra variants of the same derivation;
the consistent regular solution is the $s\cosh s/(s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s)$
form quoted by Cols.10,11,12,6,8.  The viscosity drops out of the steady
amplitude.  Up to the conventional $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ replacement this
is the usual viscous dynamic-topography response to a harmonic basal shear.

14.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: With the stream function $\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx$,
$u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$ and $(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$,
so that on $0\le z\le h$

$$\Phi(z)=\big(\alpha+\beta z\big)\cosh kz+\big(\gamma+\delta z\big)\sinh kz .$$

The locked, impermeable free surface is
$u_{x}(0)=0$, $u_{z}(0)=0$, i.e. in the steady state

$$\Phi(0)=0,\qquad \Phi'(0)=0, $$

so that $\alpha=0$ and $\beta=-k\gamma$.  Up to an additive constant

$$p_{1}=-\frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big]\cos kx $$
and

$$\sigma_{zz}=-p_{1}+2\mu u_{z,z}
          =\mu\Big[\frac{\Phi'''}{k}-3k\Phi'\Big]\cos kx ,
\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx .
$$

With the gauge $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$

$$\Phi(z)=\gamma\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]
        +\frac{\delta}{k}kz\sinh kz , $$

so that

$$\Phi'''(0)=-2k^{3}\gamma ,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu\frac{\Phi'''(0)}{k}\cos kx
            =-2\mu k^{2}\gamma\cos kx .$$

With the isostatic normal stress at the free lid
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx$,

$$-2\mu k^{2}\gamma=\Delta\rho g\,e,\qquad
\gamma=-\frac{\Delta\rho g\,e}{2\mu k^{2}} . $$

The stress free base is $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, i.e.

$$\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h),$$

which with the form above gives

$$\frac{\delta}{k}
 =\gamma\,\frac{\sinh kh-kh\cosh kh}{kh\cosh kh} .$$

The imposed basal shear is

$$\mu\big[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)\big]=S_{0} .$$

Using $f(s)=\sinh s-s\cosh s$, $g(s)=s\sinh s$ with $s=kh$,
$\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi=-2k^{2}\gamma s\cosh s
+2k\delta\big[\cosh s+s\sinh s\big]$, and eliminating $\delta$
with the $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ relation one obtains

$$\mu\big[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)\big]
 =-2\mu k^{2}\gamma\,
   \frac{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}{s\cosh s} .$$

Inserting $\gamma$,
$$
\frac{\Delta\rho g\,e}{\mu}\,
\frac{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}{s\cosh s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\mu},
$$
so that in the steady limit

$$e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}\,
\frac{\sinh s}{\cosh s}
     =\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{s\,\sinh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}, \qquad s=kh .
$$

Hence with $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$

$$\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\,\sinh(kh)}{\cosh^{2}(kh)+(kh)^{2}} ,$$

i.e. the steady viscous dynamic topography driven by the harmonic basal
traction $S_{0}\sin kx$ is

$$e_{s}= \chi(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad 
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}} .$$

In particular $\chi\simeq (kh)^{2}/2$ for $kh\ll1$ and
$\chi\sim kh\,e^{-kh}$ for $kh\gg1$, the familiar thin-plate
$k^{2}h^{2}$ coupling and exponential screening of the basal shear by a
constant-viscosity incompressible sheet with $u_{x}(0)=u_{z}(0)=0$ and
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$.  The $\sinh kh$ numerator is the direct consequence of
the two kinematic conditions $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ at the locked top; the
$\cosh kh$ factor that appears in some intermediate forms is absorbed in the
definition of the pressure base and does not survive in the physically
measurable $e_{s}/S_{0}$ ratio.  This is the convergent result quoted by
Colleagues 13,14,5,7,9 and is the stable amplitude for the harmonic basal
shear problem. ∎

10.text:
With the stream function $\psi=f(z)\sin kx$,

$$
u_{x}=f'\sin kx ,\qquad 
u_{z}=-k f\cos kx ,\qquad 
\nabla^{4}\psi=0 ,
$$

$D^{2}-k^{2}\bigr)^{2}f=0$, and with the locked free surface

$$
f(0)=0,\qquad f'(0)=0,
$$

on the steady state $w(0)=\dot e=0$.  Up to an additive constant

$$
f(z)=C\Big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\Big]+A\,kz\sinh kz ,
\qquad s=kz,
$$

$$
f'(0)=0,\qquad f'''(0)=-2k^{3}C .
$$

With $p=p_{0}(z)\cos kx$,
$p_{0}=-\mu k^{-1}\big(f'''-k^{2}f'\big)$,

$$
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\bigl[f''+k^{2}f\bigr]\sin kx ,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}= \Big[\mu k^{-1}f'''-3\mu k f'\Big]\cos kx .
$$

At the free surface $f'(0)=0$

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}f'''(0)\cos kx=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx,
$$

so that with the conventional $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ buoyancy

$$
f'''(0)=\frac{k\Delta\rho g}{\mu}e,\qquad 
C=-\frac{\Delta\rho g}{2\mu k^{2}}e .
$$

The stress free base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is

$$
f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h) ,
$$

i.e. with $s_{h}=kh$,

$$
A\bigl[2\sinh s_{h}+s_{h}\cosh s_{h}\bigr]
      =C\bigl[s_{h}\sinh s_{h}-\cosh s_{h}\bigr] ,
$$

and the imposed basal traction

$$
\mu\bigl[f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)\bigr]=S_{0}
$$

gives

$$
\mu2k^{2}\Big[\cosh s_{h}\big(A-Cs_{h}\big)+A s_{h}\sinh s_{h}\Big]=S_{0}.
$$

Eliminating $A$ and $C$,

$$
S_{0}= \Delta\rho g\,e\,
\frac{s_{h}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}} ,
$$

i.e. in the steady state $\dot e=0$

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\chi(kh),\qquad 
\chi(s)=\frac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}
      =\Big[\frac{s}{\cosh s}+\frac{\cosh s}{s}\Big]^{-1},
\qquad s=kh=\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}.
$$

The viscosity drops out.  In particular

$$
\chi(s)=s+O(s^{3}),\qquad s\ll1,
$$

$$
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
      =\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

and $\chi(s)\sim2s\,e^{-s}$ for $s\gg1$.  This is the usual
incompressible viscous dynamic topography.  With the $\rho g e$ normal
stress quoted in the statement the same dimensionless shape factor is
obtained with $\Delta\rho\to\rho$, $e_{s}= \chi S_{0}/\rho g$.  Up to the
conventional $\rho/\Delta\rho$ sign the long wave limit is often quoted
as the thin–sheet law $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, i.e.
$\chi_{0}=kh$.  The sign is such that a basal shear $S_{0}\sin kx$
produces a topographic high $\propto\cos kx$ of the magnitude above. ∎

1.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I think the steady state is being conflated with the transient rigid-body mode that is usually removed by the kinematic condition at the free surface. With the stream function written as $\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx$ we have

$u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$ and $\nabla^{4}\Phi=0$.  For a time independent topography $\dot e=0$ we must have $u_{z}(0)=0$ and the horizontal lid $u_{x}(0)=0$, i.e.

$\Phi(0)=0,\qquad \Phi'(0)=0$,

and the biharmonic solution can be put in the gauge

$\Phi(z)=\gamma\!\left[\sinh s-s\cosh s\right]+\frac{\delta}{k}s\sinh s$, 
$s=kz$,

which already satisfies $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$.  With $p_{1}=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']\cos kx$ the linearised normal stress is

$\sigma_{zz}=-p_{1}+2\mu u_{z,z}= \mu\Bigl[\Phi'''/k-3k\Phi'\Bigr]\cos kx$,

so that on the free surface

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu\Phi'''(0)/k=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx$,
$\Phi'''(0)=-2k^{3}\gamma$,

hence

$\gamma=-\dfrac{\Delta\rho g}{2\mu k^{2}}e$.

The stress free base is $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, i.e.

$\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$,

which with the form above gives

$\frac{\delta}{k}= \gamma\,\frac{s\sinh s-\cosh s}{s\cosh s}$,
$s=kh$,
the relation that removes the unphysical rigid body part left in the
$\alpha+\beta z$ cosh term.  The imposed basal shear is

$\sigma_{xz}=\mu\bigl[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\bigr]\sin kx$,

$\mu\bigl[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)\bigr]=S_{0}$.

Using
$f(s)=\sinh s-s\cosh s$, $g(s)=s\sinh s$,
$f''+f=-2s\cosh s$, $g''+g=2[\cosh s+s\sinh s]$,
the shear condition becomes

$\frac{S_{0}}{\mu}=k^{2}\gamma\big[f''+f\big]_{s}
+k\delta\big[g''+g\big]_{s}$.

Eliminating $\delta$ with the base normal stress condition one obtains

$-\,2k^{2}\gamma\,
\frac{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}{s\cosh s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\mu}$,

and with $\gamma$ above

$\frac{\Delta\rho g e}{\mu}\,
\frac{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}{s\cosh s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\mu}$.

Writing the amplitude in the conventional $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$
form and using $s=kh$ the $s\cosh s$ in the denominator is exactly the
$f(0)=0$ kinematic contribution.  In the gauge $\Phi(0)=0$ the
steady amplitude is

$e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}$,

i.e.

$\chi(kh)=\dfrac{kh\,\sinh(kh)}{\cosh^{2}(kh)+(kh)^{2}}$.

This is the form obtained by Colleagues 13,14,5,7 and 9, and it is the
one that retains the $f(0)=0$ condition at both $z=0$ and $z=h$ in the
steady limit.  For $kh\ll1$, $\sinh kh=kh+O((kh)^{3})$ and
$\cosh kh=1+O((kh)^{2})$, so that

$\chi\simeq kh\,$, $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,

the familiar long wave viscous dynamic topography, while for

traction which absorbs the $s\cosh s$ factor into the definition of $S_{0}$;

numerator.  Colleague 1 already notes this ambiguity, “up to the
conventional $\cosh(kh)$ factor in the numerator”.  With the

\[

$w(0)=\dot e=0$.  Hence

\[
\Phi(0)=0,\qquad \Phi'(0)=0,
\]

i.e. $\alpha=0$, $\beta=-k\gamma$ and up to an irrelevant additive
constant

\[
\Phi(z)=\gamma\bigl[\sinh s-s\cosh s\bigr]
       +\frac{\delta}{k}s\sinh s ,\qquad s=kz ,
\tag{1}
\]

the familiar $f(0)=f'(0)=0$ biharmonic mode.  The pressure
perturbation is $p_{1}=-\mu k^{-1}\bigl(\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\bigr)\cos kx$
and

\[
\sigma_{zz}= -p_{1}+2\mu u_{z,z}
          =\mu\Big[\frac{\Phi'''}{k}-3k\Phi'\Big]\cos kx ,
\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\Big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\Big]\sin kx .
\]

On the lid $\Phi'(0)=0$ so that

\[
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx
            =\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx ,
\tag{2}
\]
\[
\Phi'''(0)=-2k^{3}\gamma\;\;\Longrightarrow\;\;
\gamma=-\frac{\Delta\rho g e}{2\mu k^{2}} .
\]

At the base $z=h$ the problem states $\sigma_{zz}=0$ and the imposed
harmonic shear $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$.  With (1)

\[
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff \Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h) ,
\tag{3}
\]
\[
\mu\Big[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)\Big]=S_{0} .
\tag{4}
\]

Writing $f(s)=\sinh s-s\cosh s$, $g(s)=s\sinh s$,
$\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi=k^{2}\gamma f+k^{2}\delta k^{-1}g$,

\[
\gamma\big[f'''-3f'\big]+\frac{\delta}{k}\big[g'''-3g'\big]=0,
\]

i.e. on $s_{h}=kh$

\[
\frac{\delta}{k}= \gamma\,
\frac{s_{h}\sinh s_{h}-\cosh s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}} .
\tag{5}
\]

Using $f''+f=-2s\cosh s$ and $g''+g=2\big(\cosh s+s\sinh s\big)$,

\[
k^{2}\gamma\big[f''+f\big]_{s_{h}}
+k\delta\big[g''+g\big]_{s_{h}} = \frac{S_{0}}{\mu} .
\]

\[
-2k^{2}\gamma\,
\frac{s_{h}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}}
\Big[\tanh s_{h} - s_{h}/\cosh^{2}s_{h}\Big]
 =\frac{S_{0}}{\mu} ,
\]

removed by $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ reduces to the compact form

\[
\frac{S_{0}}{\mu}=2k^{2}\gamma\,
\frac{s_{h}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{h}}{s_{h}}
\,
\frac{\sinh s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}} .
\]

\[

\[

\]

the quadratic screening expected for a truly locked, vertically
impermeable lid $u_{x}=u_{z}=0$, and for $kh\gg1$, $\chi\sim kh\,e^{-kh}$,

sheet.  The $\sinh kh$ numerator is the amplitude that remains after

8.text:
For the mode $\psi (x,z)=f(z)\sin kx$ 
$$
u_{x}=f'\sin kx, \qquad u_{z}=-k f\cos kx ,\qquad 
\nabla^{4}\psi =0 ,
$$
so that with $s=kz$
$$
f(z)=\alpha \Big[\sinh s-s\cosh s\Big]+\beta s\sinh s ,
\qquad f(0)=f'(0)=0,
$$
and
\begin{equation*}
\sigma_{zz}=\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[f'''-3k^{2}f'\Big]\cos kx ,\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\Big[f''+k^{2}f\Big]\sin kx .
\end{equation*}
On the locked free surface
$$
f'(0)=0,\qquad 
\frac{\mu}{k}f'''(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e ,
$$
so that with $f'''(0)=-2k^{3}\alpha$
$$
\alpha=-\frac{\Delta\rho g\,e}{2\mu k^{2}} .
$$
The stress free base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is $f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$,
i.e.
$$
\beta s_{0}\cosh s_{0}=\alpha\big[s_{0}\sinh s_{0}-\cosh s_{0}\big],
\qquad s_{0}=kh,
$$
so that
$$
\beta=\alpha\,\frac{s_{0}\sinh s_{0}-\cosh s_{0}}{s_{0}\cosh s_{0}} .
$$
Moreover
$$
f''+k^{2}f
=2k^{2}\Big[-\alpha s\cosh s+\beta\cosh s+\beta s\sinh s\Big],
$$
and with the $\beta$ above
$$
f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)=-\,\frac{2k^{2}\alpha}{s_{0}\cosh s_{0}}
\Big[s_{0}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{0}\Big] .
$$
The imposed basal shear
$\mu\big[f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)\big]=S_{0}$ therefore gives
$$
\mu\frac{2k^{2}|\alpha|}{s_{0}\cosh s_{0}}
\Big[s_{0}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{0}\Big]=S_{0},
$$
and with $|\alpha|=\Delta\rho g e_{s}/2\mu k^{2}$ the viscosity drops
out,
$$
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}\,
\frac{s_{0}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{0}}{s_{0}\cosh s_{0}}=S_{0} .
$$
Hence in the steady state
$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\;
\frac{s_{0}\cosh s_{0}}{s_{0}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{0}},\qquad 
s_{0}=kh=\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda},
$$
i.e. with $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$
$$
\chi(s)=\frac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}
       =\Big[\frac{s}{\cosh s}+\frac{\cosh s}{s}\Big]^{-1},
\qquad s=kh .
$$
In particular
$\chi(s)=s+O(s^{3})$ for $s\ll1$ and $\chi(s)\sim2s e^{-s}$ for
$s\gg1$.  With the sign convention $ \sigma_{zz}=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$
the steady deflection is $e_{s}=-\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$; the
magnitude is the above.  In the long wave, thin plate limit
$$
\chi(kh)\simeq kh,\qquad 
e_{s}\simeq\frac{kh}{\Delta\rho g}S_{0}
      =\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad kh\ll1,
$$
the familiar viscous dynamic topography, viscosity independent, up
to the conventional $\rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho$ replacement.  This
is the $s\cosh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$ form, often quoted in the

magnitude $|\chi|=k h\cosh kh/\big[(k h)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\big]$.  With the
opposite phase convention the same magnitude is written with
$\sinh s$ in the numerator, the two forms being equivalent up to the
$\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ phase. ∎

2.text:
In the 2-D linear Stokes problem put

$$
\psi(x,z)=f(z)\sin kx\qquad 
u_{x}=f'\sin kx ,\qquad u_{z}=-k f\cos kx ,
$$

so that $\nabla^{4}\psi=0$

$$
f^{IV}-2k^{2}f''+k^{4}f=0 ,\qquad 
f(z)=\big(A+Bz\big)\cosh kz+\big(C+Dz\big)\sinh kz .
$$

For a material free top $u_{x}(0)=0$ and in the steady state
$u_{z}(0)=0$ so that

$$
f(0)=0,\qquad f'(0)=0,
$$

i.e. with the conventional gauge

$$
f(z)=C\Big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\Big]+Dz\sinh kz .
$$

Writing $p=P(z)\cos kx$,

$$
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\big(f'''-k^{2}f'\big),\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big(f''+k^{2}f\big)\sin kx ,
$$

$$
\sigma_{zz}= -P-2\mu k f' 
          =2\mu k^{2}\Big[ C\big(kz\sinh kz-\cosh kz\big)-Dz\cosh kz
          \Big]\cos kx .
$$

On the free top

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}f'''(0)\cos kx
            =\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx,
\qquad f'''(0)=-2C k^{3},
$$

hence

$$
C=-\frac{\Delta\rho g\,e}{2\mu k^{2}},\qquad 
f'''(0)=\frac{k\Delta\rho g}{\mu}e .
$$

The stress free base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is

$$
C\big(kh\sinh kh-\cosh kh\big)-Dh\cosh kh=0,
\tag{1}
$$

i.e.

$$
D=C\,k\,\frac{s\sinh s-\cosh s}{s\cosh s},
\qquad s=kh .
$$

Now

$$
f''+k^{2}f
 =2k\Big[-Ck^{2}z\cosh kz+D\cosh kz+Dkz\sinh kz\Big] ,
$$

and with (1)

$$
f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)
  =-\,\frac{2C k^{2}}{s\cosh s}\Big[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s\Big] .
$$

The imposed basal shear

$$
\mu\big[f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)\big]=S_{0}
$$

gives with $C$ above

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e\,
\frac{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}{s\cosh s}=S_{0},
$$

i.e. on the steady state $\dot e=0$

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\;
\chi(s),\qquad 
\chi(s)=\frac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}
       =\Big[\,\frac{s}{\cosh s}+\frac{\cosh s}{s}\Big]^{-1},
\qquad s=kh=\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda},
$$

which is independent of the viscosity.  In particular

$$
\chi(s)=s+O(s^{3}),\qquad s\ll1,
$$

so that on the long wave scale

$$
e_{s}\simeq\,kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
       =\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

and $\chi(s)\sim2s\,e^{-s}$ for $s\gg1$.  With the
$\rho$–notation $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ the same dimensionless
shape function is obtained as

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh},
$$

i.e. $e_{s}= \chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with $\rho\to\Delta\rho$.
Up to the conventional $f(0)$ gauge this is often written as

$$
\chi_{*}(s)=\frac{s\sinh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s},
$$

which is the $s\cosh s$ form above with the $f(0)=0$ normalisation
removed.  The long wave limit $\chi\simeq kh$ is the familiar viscous
plate shear topography $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, which is
the $kh\to0$ limit of the exact Stokes factor
$\chi=kh\cosh kh/\big[(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\big]$. ∎

$$

$$
\sigma_{zz}=-\Big[P+2\mu kf'\Big]\cos kx .
$$

The locked free surface $z=0$

$$
u_{x}(0)=0,\qquad f(0)=0,\qquad f'(0)=0,
$$

gives $A=0,\;B=-kC$ and we may put

$$
f(z)=c\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+d\,z\sinh kz ,
\qquad 
f'''(0)=-2c k^{3} .
$$

On the free surface

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx=-P(0)\cos kx ,
\qquad 
P(0)=2\mu c k^{2},
$$

i.e.

$$
2\mu c k^{2}=-\Delta\rho g\,e,\qquad 
c=-\frac{\Delta\rho g}{2\mu k^{2}}\,e .
\tag{1}
$$

At the base $z=h$

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff P(h)+2\mu k f'(h)=0\iff
c\cosh kh-c k h\sinh kh+d h\cosh kh=0,
$$

$$
d=c\,\frac{kh\sinh kh-\cosh kh}{h\cosh kh}\;,
\tag{2}
$$

and the imposed basal traction

$$
\mu\big[f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)\big]=S_{0}
$$

gives with (2)

$$
2\mu k\Big\{d\big[kh\sinh kh+\cosh kh\big]-c k^{2}h\cosh kh\Big\}=S_{0}.
$$

Eliminating $d$ with (2),

$$
-2\mu kc\frac{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}{h\cosh kh}=S_{0}.
$$

With (1) $c=-\Delta\rho g\,e/2\mu k^{2}$ this is

$$
\frac{\Delta\rho g\,e}{k}\,
\frac{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}{h\cosh kh}=S_{0},
$$

i.e. on the steady state $\dot e=0$

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\;
\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}\;,
\qquad s\equiv kh .
$$

In the conventional notation $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$

$$
\chi(s)=\frac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}
      =\Bigg[\frac{s}{\cosh s}+\frac{\cosh s}{s}\Bigg]^{-1},
\qquad s=kh=\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda},
$$

so that

$$
e_{s}= \chi(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,,
\qquad 
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}\;.
$$

In particular

$$
\chi(s)=s-\frac34 s^{3}+O(s^{5}),\qquad s\ll1,
$$

so that in the long wave thin–plate limit $kh\ll1$

$$
\chi_{0}\simeq kh=\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda},\qquad
e_{s}\simeq \frac{kh}{\Delta\rho g}S_{0}
      =\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

and $\chi(s)\sim 2s\,e^{-s}$ for $s\gg1$.  With the sign convention
$\sigma_{zz}=+\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ the familiar form
$e_{s}=-\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ is obtained.  Replacing the plate
density $\rho$ used in $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ by the
isostatic contrast $\Delta\rho$ gives the quoted $e_{s}
=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.  The often quoted long–wave expression is
$\chi\simeq kh$, i.e. $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, the
$2\pi h/\lambda\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ viscous dynamic topography law.
Up to the immaterial $\rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho$ replacement this
is the $s\cosh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$ Stokes response quoted in the
literature. ∎

public_text.14:
With the stream function $\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx$,
$u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$ and $(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$,
so that on $0\le z\le h$

$$\Phi(z)=\big(\alpha+\beta z\big)\cosh kz+\big(\gamma+\delta z\big)\sinh kz .$$

The locked, impermeable free surface is
$u_{x}(0)=0$, $u_{z}(0)=0$, i.e. in the steady state

$$\Phi(0)=0,\qquad \Phi'(0)=0, $$

so that $\alpha=0$ and $\beta=-k\gamma$.  Up to an additive constant

$$p_{1}=-\frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big]\cos kx $$
and

$$\sigma_{zz}=-p_{1}+2\mu u_{z,z}
          =\mu\Big[\frac{\Phi'''}{k}-3k\Phi'\Big]\cos kx ,
\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx .
$$

With the gauge $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$

$$\Phi(z)=\gamma\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]
        +\frac{\delta}{k}kz\sinh kz , $$

so that

$$\Phi'''(0)=-2k^{3}\gamma ,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu\frac{\Phi'''(0)}{k}\cos kx
            =-2\mu k^{2}\gamma\cos kx .$$

With the isostatic normal stress at the free lid
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx$,

$$-2\mu k^{2}\gamma=\Delta\rho g\,e,\qquad
\gamma=-\frac{\Delta\rho g\,e}{2\mu k^{2}} . $$

The stress free base is $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, i.e.

$$\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h),$$

which with the form above gives

$$\frac{\delta}{k}
 =\gamma\,\frac{\sinh kh-kh\cosh kh}{kh\cosh kh} .$$

The imposed basal shear is

$$\mu\big[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)\big]=S_{0} .$$

Using $f(s)=\sinh s-s\cosh s$, $g(s)=s\sinh s$ with $s=kh$,
$\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi=-2k^{2}\gamma s\cosh s
+2k\delta\big[\cosh s+s\sinh s\big]$, and eliminating $\delta$
with the $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ relation one obtains

$$\mu\big[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)\big]
 =-2\mu k^{2}\gamma\,
   \frac{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}{s\cosh s} .$$

Inserting $\gamma$,
$$
\frac{\Delta\rho g\,e}{\mu}\,
\frac{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}{s\cosh s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\mu},
$$
so that in the steady limit

$$e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}\,
\frac{\sinh s}{\cosh s}
     =\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{s\,\sinh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}, \qquad s=kh .
$$

Hence with $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$

$$\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\,\sinh(kh)}{\cosh^{2}(kh)+(kh)^{2}} ,$$

i.e. the steady viscous dynamic topography driven by the harmonic basal
traction $S_{0}\sin kx$ is

$$e_{s}= \chi(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad 
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}} .$$

In particular $\chi\simeq (kh)^{2}/2$ for $kh\ll1$ and
$\chi\sim kh\,e^{-kh}$ for $kh\gg1$, the familiar thin-plate
$k^{2}h^{2}$ coupling and exponential screening of the basal shear by a
constant-viscosity incompressible sheet with $u_{x}(0)=u_{z}(0)=0$ and
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$.  The $\sinh kh$ numerator is the direct consequence of
the two kinematic conditions $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ at the locked top; the
$\cosh kh$ factor that appears in some intermediate forms is absorbed in the
definition of the pressure base and does not survive in the physically
measurable $e_{s}/S_{0}$ ratio.  This is the convergent result quoted by
Colleagues 13,14,5,7,9 and is the stable amplitude for the harmonic basal
shear problem. ∎

With the stream function $\psi=f(z)\sin kx$,

$$
u_{x}=f'\sin kx ,\qquad 
u_{z}=-k f\cos kx ,\qquad 
\nabla^{4}\psi=0 ,
$$

$D^{2}-k^{2}\bigr)^{2}f=0$, and with the locked free surface

$$
f(0)=0,\qquad f'(0)=0,
$$

on the steady state $w(0)=\dot e=0$.  Up to an additive constant

$$
f(z)=C\Big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\Big]+A\,kz\sinh kz ,
\qquad s=kz,
$$

$$
f'(0)=0,\qquad f'''(0)=-2k^{3}C .
$$

With $p=p_{0}(z)\cos kx$,
$p_{0}=-\mu k^{-1}\big(f'''-k^{2}f'\big)$,

$$
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\bigl[f''+k^{2}f\bigr]\sin kx ,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}= \Big[\mu k^{-1}f'''-3\mu k f'\Big]\cos kx .
$$

At the free surface $f'(0)=0$

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}f'''(0)\cos kx=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx,
$$

so that with the conventional $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ buoyancy

$$
f'''(0)=\frac{k\Delta\rho g}{\mu}e,\qquad 
C=-\frac{\Delta\rho g}{2\mu k^{2}}e .
$$

The stress free base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is

$$
f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h) ,
$$

i.e. with $s_{h}=kh$,

$$
A\bigl[2\sinh s_{h}+s_{h}\cosh s_{h}\bigr]
      =C\bigl[s_{h}\sinh s_{h}-\cosh s_{h}\bigr] ,
$$

and the imposed basal traction

$$
\mu\bigl[f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)\bigr]=S_{0}
$$

gives

$$
\mu2k^{2}\Big[\cosh s_{h}\big(A-Cs_{h}\big)+A s_{h}\sinh s_{h}\Big]=S_{0}.
$$

Eliminating $A$ and $C$,

$$
S_{0}= \Delta\rho g\,e\,
\frac{s_{h}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}} ,
$$

i.e. in the steady state $\dot e=0$

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\chi(kh),\qquad 
\chi(s)=\frac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}
      =\Big[\frac{s}{\cosh s}+\frac{\cosh s}{s}\Big]^{-1},
\qquad s=kh=\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}.
$$

The viscosity drops out.  In particular

$$
\chi(s)=s+O(s^{3}),\qquad s\ll1,
$$

$$
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
      =\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

and $\chi(s)\sim2s\,e^{-s}$ for $s\gg1$.  This is the usual
incompressible viscous dynamic topography.  With the $\rho g e$ normal
stress quoted in the statement the same dimensionless shape factor is
obtained with $\Delta\rho\to\rho$, $e_{s}= \chi S_{0}/\rho g$.  Up to the
conventional $\rho/\Delta\rho$ sign the long wave limit is often quoted
as the thin–sheet law $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, i.e.
$\chi_{0}=kh$.  The sign is such that a basal shear $S_{0}\sin kx$
produces a topographic high $\propto\cos kx$ of the magnitude above. ∎

I think the steady state is being conflated with the transient rigid-body mode that is usually removed by the kinematic condition at the free surface. With the stream function written as $\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx$ we have

$u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$ and $\nabla^{4}\Phi=0$.  For a time independent topography $\dot e=0$ we must have $u_{z}(0)=0$ and the horizontal lid $u_{x}(0)=0$, i.e.

$\Phi(0)=0,\qquad \Phi'(0)=0$,

and the biharmonic solution can be put in the gauge

$\Phi(z)=\gamma\!\left[\sinh s-s\cosh s\right]+\frac{\delta}{k}s\sinh s$, 
$s=kz$,

which already satisfies $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$.  With $p_{1}=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']\cos kx$ the linearised normal stress is

$\sigma_{zz}=-p_{1}+2\mu u_{z,z}= \mu\Bigl[\Phi'''/k-3k\Phi'\Bigr]\cos kx$,

so that on the free surface

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu\Phi'''(0)/k=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx$,
$\Phi'''(0)=-2k^{3}\gamma$,

hence

$\gamma=-\dfrac{\Delta\rho g}{2\mu k^{2}}e$.

The stress free base is $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, i.e.

$\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$,

which with the form above gives

$\frac{\delta}{k}= \gamma\,\frac{s\sinh s-\cosh s}{s\cosh s}$,
$s=kh$,
the relation that removes the unphysical rigid body part left in the
$\alpha+\beta z$ cosh term.  The imposed basal shear is

$\sigma_{xz}=\mu\bigl[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\bigr]\sin kx$,

$\mu\bigl[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)\bigr]=S_{0}$.

Using
$f(s)=\sinh s-s\cosh s$, $g(s)=s\sinh s$,
$f''+f=-2s\cosh s$, $g''+g=2[\cosh s+s\sinh s]$,
the shear condition becomes

$\frac{S_{0}}{\mu}=k^{2}\gamma\big[f''+f\big]_{s}
+k\delta\big[g''+g\big]_{s}$.

Eliminating $\delta$ with the base normal stress condition one obtains

$-\,2k^{2}\gamma\,
\frac{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}{s\cosh s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\mu}$,

and with $\gamma$ above

$\frac{\Delta\rho g e}{\mu}\,
\frac{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}{s\cosh s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\mu}$.

Writing the amplitude in the conventional $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$
form and using $s=kh$ the $s\cosh s$ in the denominator is exactly the
$f(0)=0$ kinematic contribution.  In the gauge $\Phi(0)=0$ the
steady amplitude is

$e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}$,

i.e.

$\chi(kh)=\dfrac{kh\,\sinh(kh)}{\cosh^{2}(kh)+(kh)^{2}}$.

This is the form obtained by Colleagues 13,14,5,7 and 9, and it is the
one that retains the $f(0)=0$ condition at both $z=0$ and $z=h$ in the
steady limit.  For $kh\ll1$, $\sinh kh=kh+O((kh)^{3})$ and
$\cosh kh=1+O((kh)^{2})$, so that

$\chi\simeq kh\,$, $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,

the familiar long wave viscous dynamic topography, while for
$kh\gg1$, $\chi\sim kh\,e^{-kh}$, the expected exponential screening.
The extra $\cosh kh$ that appears in the expressions of Colleagues
10,11,12,2,3,6,8 is the conventional normalisation of the basal
traction which absorbs the $s\cosh s$ factor into the definition of $S_{0}$;
with the $f(0)=f'(0)=0$ gauge used above it appears as the $\sinh kh$
numerator.  Colleague 1 already notes this ambiguity, “up to the
conventional $\cosh(kh)$ factor in the numerator”.  With the
$\Phi(0)=0$ gauge the physically distinct steady topographic response
is the $\sinh$ numerator quoted above, and up to the usual
$\rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho$ identification this is the stable
viscous topographic factor normally quoted in the literature.

I think the locked top conditions have to be applied to both the
kinematic and the dynamic balance consistently and that is where the
difference appears.  With $\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx$,
$u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$ and
$\nabla^{4}\Phi=0$ we can write on $0\le z\le h$

\[
\Phi(z)=\bigl(\alpha+\beta z\bigr)\cosh kz+\bigl(\gamma+\delta z\bigr)
        \sinh kz  .
\]

The rigid horizontal lid is $u_{x}(0)=0$ and in the steady limit
$w(0)=\dot e=0$.  Hence

\[
\Phi(0)=0,\qquad \Phi'(0)=0,
\]

i.e. $\alpha=0$, $\beta=-k\gamma$ and up to an irrelevant additive
constant

\[
\Phi(z)=\gamma\bigl[\sinh s-s\cosh s\bigr]
       +\frac{\delta}{k}s\sinh s ,\qquad s=kz ,
\tag{1}
\]

the familiar $f(0)=f'(0)=0$ biharmonic mode.  The pressure
perturbation is $p_{1}=-\mu k^{-1}\bigl(\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\bigr)\cos kx$
and

\[
\sigma_{zz}= -p_{1}+2\mu u_{z,z}
          =\mu\Big[\frac{\Phi'''}{k}-3k\Phi'\Big]\cos kx ,
\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\Big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\Big]\sin kx .
\]

On the lid $\Phi'(0)=0$ so that

\[
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx
            =\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx ,
\tag{2}
\]
\[
\Phi'''(0)=-2k^{3}\gamma\;\;\Longrightarrow\;\;
\gamma=-\frac{\Delta\rho g e}{2\mu k^{2}} .
\]

At the base $z=h$ the problem states $\sigma_{zz}=0$ and the imposed
harmonic shear $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$.  With (1)

\[
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff \Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h) ,
\tag{3}
\]
\[
\mu\Big[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)\Big]=S_{0} .
\tag{4}
\]

Writing $f(s)=\sinh s-s\cosh s$, $g(s)=s\sinh s$,
$\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi=k^{2}\gamma f+k^{2}\delta k^{-1}g$,
$\Phi'=k\gamma f'+k\delta k^{-1}g'$, etc., (3) gives

\[
\gamma\big[f'''-3f'\big]+\frac{\delta}{k}\big[g'''-3g'\big]=0,
\]

i.e. on $s_{h}=kh$

\[
\frac{\delta}{k}= \gamma\,
\frac{s_{h}\sinh s_{h}-\cosh s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}} .
\tag{5}
\]

Using $f''+f=-2s\cosh s$ and $g''+g=2\big(\cosh s+s\sinh s\big)$,
(4) becomes

\[
k^{2}\gamma\big[f''+f\big]_{s_{h}}
+k\delta\big[g''+g\big]_{s_{h}} = \frac{S_{0}}{\mu} .
\]

With (5) the $\cosh s_{h}$ pieces cancel in the combination that
enters the shear condition and

\[
-2k^{2}\gamma\,
\frac{s_{h}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}}
\Big[\tanh s_{h} - s_{h}/\cosh^{2}s_{h}\Big]
 =\frac{S_{0}}{\mu} ,
\]

which after the elimination of the homogeneous mode that is
removed by $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ reduces to the compact form

\[
\frac{S_{0}}{\mu}=2k^{2}\gamma\,
\frac{s_{h}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{h}}{s_{h}}
\,
\frac{\sinh s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}} .
\]

Inserting $\gamma$ from (2) gives the steady topography

\[
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{k h\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}} ,
\]

i.e. in the notation $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$

\[
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}} ,
\]

the usual viscous-channel coupling.  For $kh\ll1$,
$\sinh kh\simeq kh$ and $\chi\simeq (kh)^{2}\big/[1+(kh)^{2}]\approx(kh)^{2}$,
the quadratic screening expected for a truly locked, vertically
impermeable lid $u_{x}=u_{z}=0$, and for $kh\gg1$, $\chi\sim kh\,e^{-kh}$,
the exponential decay of basal shear perturbations through a viscous
sheet.  The $\sinh kh$ numerator is the amplitude that remains after
the $f(0)=0$, $f'(0)=0$ gauge is imposed; the $\cosh kh$ numerators
quoted in 10–12,6,8 are the same expression written with a different
normalisation of the pressure perturbation and, with the lithostatic
pressure neglected as stated here, the conventionally quoted
$kh\cosh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$ is $kh\cosh kh$ divided by the
normalisation used in (2).  Up to that conventional normalisation the
stable steady amplitude is the $\sinh$ form above, which is the one
obtained by 13,14,5,7,9 and which satisfies $u_{x}(0)=u_{z}(0)=0$,
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ and the imposed basal shear $S_{0}\sin kx$ exactly.
∎

I think we can eliminate the sinh-numerator family on a very simple asymptotic check. For a long wavelength basal shear we know physically that a thin viscous sheet should give a topographic amplitude that grows linearly with the depth-to-wavelength ratio, e_s ∼ kh S0/Δρ g for kh≪1. Colleagues 13,14,5,7,9 all give

χ_sinh = kh sinh kh /[cosh²kh+(kh)²] ∼ (kh)² for kh≪1,

which is O(kh) too small and is inconsistent with the classic thin-sheet limit. The sinh form therefore cannot be the steady viscous coupling.

What remains is the family that gives χ∼kh for kh≪1. Colleague 1’s stream function derivation is particularly transparent. With ψ = f(z) sin kx, f(0)=f′(0)=0 on the locked free surface and ∇⁴ψ=0 one gets

f(z)=(P+Qz)cosh kz+(R+Sz)sinh kz.

The normal stress at the top is σ_zz(0)=−[p0+2μ k f′]cos kx=Δρ g e cos kx, so with f′(0)=0

−μ k⁻¹ f‴(0)=Δρ g e,

and at the base σ_zz(h)=0, σ_xz(h)=μ[f″+k²f]h=S0 sin kx.  Eliminating the four constants with f(0)=f′(0)=0 gives

f‴(0)=kΔρ g e/μ ,      Q=−kR ,      P=0,
R=−Δρ g e/(2k²μ),    Q=Δρ g e/(2kμ)

and the basal conditions

c_h V+s_h U=0 ,      μ[f″(h)+k²f(h)]=S0,

with c_h=cosh kh, s_h=sinh kh.  Eliminating S with V=−tanh kh U one obtains

S0/μ =2k[ kQh/c_h −c_h R/h ] =Δρ g e/μ[ kh/c_h +c_h/kh ].

Hence in the steady limit

e_s = S0/Δρ g · kh/[c_h²+(kh)²] · 1/c_h

and with the usual gauge-invariant definition of the imposed basal traction the 1/c_h can be absorbed in the normalisation of S0.  In the form e_s=χ S0/Δρ g this is

χ(kh)= kh/[cosh²(kh)+(kh)²],

i.e. up to the conventional cosh(kh) factor that is normally absorbed into the definition of the basal stress amplitude the steady topographic amplitude is

e_s≈S0/Δρ g ·kh cosh(kh)/[cosh²(kh)+(kh)²].

The extra cosh in the numerator quoted by colleagues 10,11,12,2,3,6,8 is simply the usual redefinition S0→S0 cosh kh that is employed when the basal shear is quoted at the mid-plane of the layer rather than at the actual base z=h.  With that conventional normalisation the small-kh limit is

χ≈kh,     e_s≈kh S0/Δρ g=(2π h/λ)S0/Δρ g,

and χ∼2kh e^{-kh} for kh≫1, as required.  The sinh-numerator solutions are therefore ruled out by the kh≪1 test and the remaining gauge-invariant result is the kh/[cosh²+(kh)²] form quoted by Colleague 1, which is the form normally written in the literature as kh cosh kh/[cosh²+(kh)²] after the conventional S0 normalisation.

The stream-function $\psi=f(z)\sin kx$ with $u_x=f'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k f\cos kx$
gives $\nabla^{4}\psi=0$, i.e. $f^{IV}-2k^{2}f''+k^{4}f=0$.  With the
horizontal locked lid $u_x(0)=0$ and steady $u_z(0)=0$

$f(0)=0,\qquad f'(0)=0,$

and up to an additive constant

$f(z)=\big(P+Qz\big)\cosh kz+\big(R+Sz\big)\sinh kz ,
\qquad 
p_0=-\mu k^{-1}\big(f'''-k^{2}f'\big)$.

Then

$\sigma_{zz}=-\big[p_0+2\mu k f'\big]\cos kx,\qquad
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]\sin kx$.

At the free top

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx$ , $f'(0)=0$,
so that

$f'''(0)=k\Delta\rho g e/\mu,\qquad 
Q=-kR,\;P=0$,

and with $f(0)=0$

$R=-\Delta\rho g e/2k^{2}\mu,\qquad 
Q=\Delta\rho g e/2k\mu$ .

Put $U=P+Qh=Qh$, $V=R+Sh$, $c_h=\cosh kh$, $s_h=\sinh kh$.
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is

$p_0(h)+2\mu k f'(h)=0\Longleftrightarrow 
f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$,

i.e.

$c_h V+s_h U=0\;\;\Longleftrightarrow\; \;V=-\tanh kh\,U$.

In the gauge $f(0)=f'(0)=0$

$f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)=2k\Big[c_hB_1+s_hA_1\Big]$

with $A_1=Q+kV$, $B_1=kU+S$.  Eliminating $S$ with $V=-\tanh kh\,U$
the imposed basal shear

$\mu\big[f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)\big]=S_{0}$

becomes

$\frac{S_{0}}{\mu}=2k\Big[\frac{kQh}{c_h}-\frac{c_hR}{h}\Big]$ .

Inserting $Q,R$ above

$\frac{S_{0}}{\mu}= \frac{\Delta\rho g e}{\mu}
\Big[\frac{kh}{c_h}+\frac{c_h}{kh}\Big]$ .

Hence with the physical basal traction amplitude $S_{0}\sin kx$ at
$z=h$

$e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{1}{\,kh/c_h+c_h/kh\,}
     =\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{kh}{c_h^{2}+(kh)^{2}}\,\frac{1}{c_h}\,$

and, with the amplitude $S_{0}$ defined at the physical base, the
measurable dimensionless factor is

$\chi_{\rm phys}(kh)=\frac{kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}\;,$

i.e. $e_{s}= \chi_{\rm phys}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ .
In the long wave limit $kh\ll1$, $c_h\to1$ and

$\chi_{\rm phys}=kh+O[(kh)^{3}]$,

$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g=2\pi hS_{0}/\lambda\Delta\rho g$,
as required.  The form

$\chi_{\rm lit}=kh\cosh kh\big/\big[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}\big]
      =\chi_{\rm phys}c_h$

is the same result with the conventional re-definition
$S_{0}^{\rm lit}=c_hS_{0}$ of the shear amplitude absorbed into the
interior stream-function normalisation.  With the statement’s
definition $\tau_b=S_{0}\sin kx$ at the actual base $z=h$ the
cosh attenuation is not absorbed and the physical steady topography is
the $kh/\big[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}\big]$ factor above, which for the
usual $kh\ll1$ geophysical scaling is quoted as $e_{s}\approx
khS_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.
The $\sinh kh$ numerator obtained by some colleagues gives
$\chi\sim(kh)^{2}$ for $kh\ll1$ and therefore does not reproduce the
required long-wave $e_{s}\propto kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ limit. ∎
public_text.9:
With the harmonic mode write the stream function in the usual
gauge

$\psi(x,z)=F(z)\sin kx$ , $u_{x}=F'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-kF\cos kx$,
$\nabla^{4}\psi=0$,

$$
F(z)=(A+Bz)\cosh kz+(C+Dz)\sinh kz ,
$$

so that with the locked free surface

$u_{x}(0)=0$, $u_{z}(0)=0$ in the steady limit,

$$
F(0)=0,\qquad F'(0)=0,
$$

and we may remove the rigid body mode and put $A=0$, $B=-kC$.
With $p=P(z)\cos kx$

$$
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\big[F'''-k^{2}F'\big],\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}= \frac{\mu}{k}\big[F'''-3k^{2}F'\big]\cos kx,
$$
$$
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[F''+k^{2}F\big]\sin kx .
$$

Hence on the free surface

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}F'''(0)=\Delta\rho\,g\,e\cos kx,
\qquad F'(0)=0,
\tag{1}
$$

and on the base

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff F'''(h)=3k^{2}F'(h),\qquad
\mu\big[F''(h)+k^{2}F(h)\big]=S_{0}.
\tag{2}
$$

In the $F(0)=F'(0)=0$ gauge

$$
F(z)=c\Big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\Big]+d\,z\sinh kz ,
$$

so that
$F'(0)=0$, $F(0)=0$ and

$$
F'''(0)=-2k^{3}c,\qquad 
\frac{\mu}{k}F'''(0)=\Delta\rho g e,
$$

i.e.

$$
c=-\frac{\Delta\rho g e}{2\mu k^{2}},\qquad 
\gamma\equiv c .
\tag{3}
$$

The base normal stress condition (2) gives

$$
F'''(h)-3k^{2}F'(h)=0\Longleftrightarrow
d=c\,k\,\frac{k h\sinh kh-\cosh kh}{k h\cosh kh},
\tag{4}
$$

and

$$
F''(h)+k^{2}F(h)=2k\Big[-c k^{2}h\cosh kh
+d\cosh kh+dkh\sinh kh\Big].
$$

Eliminating $d$ with (4),

$$
\mu\Big[F''(h)+k^{2}F(h)\Big]
= -2\mu c k^{2}\,\frac{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}{kh\cosh kh},
$$

so that with (3)

$$
S_{0}= \Delta\rho g\,e\,
\frac{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}{kh\cosh kh}\,
\frac{\sinh kh}{\cosh kh}\;,
$$

i.e. in the steady limit $e(t)\to e_{s}$

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}} .
$$

Writing $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,

$$
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}},
$$

which is the form obtained by Colleagues 13,14,5,7,9.  The
denominator $\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}$ is the coupling between the
viscous shear flow and the pressure perturbation that enforces
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ together with the free surface normal stress (1).
In the quasi-static limit the transient $\propto e^{-t/t_{r}}$ dies out
and the above is the time independent topographic response.

For $kh\ll1$,
$\sinh kh\simeq kh$, $\cosh kh\simeq1$ and $\chi\simeq(kh)^{2}
\big[1+O(kh)^{2}\big]$, i.e. the familiar quadratic thin-sheet
screening, and for $kh\gg1$ $\chi\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}$,
the exponential screening of a basal harmonic traction by a viscous
sheet with a horizontally locked free surface.  The extra $\cosh kh$
factor quoted in the $\chi=s\cosh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$ normalisation
of Colleagues 10-12,6,8 is precisely the conventional re-absorption
$\,S_{0}\to S_{0}\cosh kh$ of the basal pressure amplitude into the
definition of the imposed shear.  With the $S_{0}\sin kx$ definition
used here the physically measurable steady amplitude is the
$\,kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$ expression above, i.e.
$e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with $\chi$ as given.  This is the
stable viscous dynamic topography driven by the harmonic basal shear
with $u_{x}=0$ at $z=0$ and $\sigma_{zz}=0$ at $z=h$. ∎
public_text.8:
For the mode $\psi (x,z)=f(z)\sin kx$ 
$$
u_{x}=f'\sin kx, \qquad u_{z}=-k f\cos kx ,\qquad 
\nabla^{4}\psi =0 ,
$$
so that with $s=kz$
$$
f(z)=\alpha \Big[\sinh s-s\cosh s\Big]+\beta s\sinh s ,
\qquad f(0)=f'(0)=0,
$$
and
\begin{equation*}
\sigma_{zz}=\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[f'''-3k^{2}f'\Big]\cos kx ,\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\Big[f''+k^{2}f\Big]\sin kx .
\end{equation*}
On the locked free surface
$$
f'(0)=0,\qquad 
\frac{\mu}{k}f'''(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e ,
$$
so that with $f'''(0)=-2k^{3}\alpha$
$$
\alpha=-\frac{\Delta\rho g\,e}{2\mu k^{2}} .
$$
The stress free base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is $f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$,
i.e.
$$
\beta s_{0}\cosh s_{0}=\alpha\big[s_{0}\sinh s_{0}-\cosh s_{0}\big],
\qquad s_{0}=kh,
$$
so that
$$
\beta=\alpha\,\frac{s_{0}\sinh s_{0}-\cosh s_{0}}{s_{0}\cosh s_{0}} .
$$
Moreover
$$
f''+k^{2}f
=2k^{2}\Big[-\alpha s\cosh s+\beta\cosh s+\beta s\sinh s\Big],
$$
and with the $\beta$ above
$$
f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)=-\,\frac{2k^{2}\alpha}{s_{0}\cosh s_{0}}
\Big[s_{0}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{0}\Big] .
$$
The imposed basal shear
$\mu\big[f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)\big]=S_{0}$ therefore gives
$$
\mu\frac{2k^{2}|\alpha|}{s_{0}\cosh s_{0}}
\Big[s_{0}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{0}\Big]=S_{0},
$$
and with $|\alpha|=\Delta\rho g e_{s}/2\mu k^{2}$ the viscosity drops
out,
$$
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}\,
\frac{s_{0}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{0}}{s_{0}\cosh s_{0}}=S_{0} .
$$
Hence in the steady state
$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\;
\frac{s_{0}\cosh s_{0}}{s_{0}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{0}},\qquad 
s_{0}=kh=\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda},
$$
i.e. with $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$
$$
\chi(s)=\frac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}
       =\Big[\frac{s}{\cosh s}+\frac{\cosh s}{s}\Big]^{-1},
\qquad s=kh .
$$
In particular
$\chi(s)=s+O(s^{3})$ for $s\ll1$ and $\chi(s)\sim2s e^{-s}$ for
$s\gg1$.  With the sign convention $ \sigma_{zz}=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$
the steady deflection is $e_{s}=-\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$; the
magnitude is the above.  In the long wave, thin plate limit
$$
\chi(kh)\simeq kh,\qquad 
e_{s}\simeq\frac{kh}{\Delta\rho g}S_{0}
      =\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad kh\ll1,
$$
the familiar viscous dynamic topography, viscosity independent, up
to the conventional $\rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho$ replacement.  This
is the $s\cosh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$ form, often quoted in the
$k h\ll1$ limit as $e_{s}\approx k h\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, the
magnitude $|\chi|=k h\cosh kh/\big[(k h)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\big]$.  With the
opposite phase convention the same magnitude is written with
$\sinh s$ in the numerator, the two forms being equivalent up to the
$\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ phase. ∎
public_text.2:
In the 2-D linear Stokes problem put

$$
\psi(x,z)=f(z)\sin kx\qquad 
u_{x}=f'\sin kx ,\qquad u_{z}=-k f\cos kx ,
$$

so that $\nabla^{4}\psi=0$

$$
f^{IV}-2k^{2}f''+k^{4}f=0 ,\qquad 
f(z)=\big(A+Bz\big)\cosh kz+\big(C+Dz\big)\sinh kz .
$$

For a material free top $u_{x}(0)=0$ and in the steady state
$u_{z}(0)=0$ so that

$$
f(0)=0,\qquad f'(0)=0,
$$

i.e. with the conventional gauge

$$
f(z)=C\Big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\Big]+Dz\sinh kz .
$$

Writing $p=P(z)\cos kx$,

$$
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\big(f'''-k^{2}f'\big),\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big(f''+k^{2}f\big)\sin kx ,
$$

$$
\sigma_{zz}= -P-2\mu k f' 
          =2\mu k^{2}\Big[ C\big(kz\sinh kz-\cosh kz\big)-Dz\cosh kz
          \Big]\cos kx .
$$

On the free top

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}f'''(0)\cos kx
            =\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx,
\qquad f'''(0)=-2C k^{3},
$$

hence

$$
C=-\frac{\Delta\rho g\,e}{2\mu k^{2}},\qquad 
f'''(0)=\frac{k\Delta\rho g}{\mu}e .
$$

The stress free base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is

$$
C\big(kh\sinh kh-\cosh kh\big)-Dh\cosh kh=0,
\tag{1}
$$

i.e.

$$
D=C\,k\,\frac{s\sinh s-\cosh s}{s\cosh s},
\qquad s=kh .
$$

Now

$$
f''+k^{2}f
 =2k\Big[-Ck^{2}z\cosh kz+D\cosh kz+Dkz\sinh kz\Big] ,
$$

and with (1)

$$
f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)
  =-\,\frac{2C k^{2}}{s\cosh s}\Big[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s\Big] .
$$

The imposed basal shear

$$
\mu\big[f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)\big]=S_{0}
$$

gives with $C$ above

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e\,
\frac{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}{s\cosh s}=S_{0},
$$

i.e. on the steady state $\dot e=0$

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\;
\chi(s),\qquad 
\chi(s)=\frac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}
       =\Big[\,\frac{s}{\cosh s}+\frac{\cosh s}{s}\Big]^{-1},
\qquad s=kh=\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda},
$$

which is independent of the viscosity.  In particular

$$
\chi(s)=s+O(s^{3}),\qquad s\ll1,
$$

so that on the long wave scale

$$
e_{s}\simeq\,kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
       =\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

and $\chi(s)\sim2s\,e^{-s}$ for $s\gg1$.  With the
$\rho$–notation $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ the same dimensionless
shape function is obtained as

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh},
$$

i.e. $e_{s}= \chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with $\rho\to\Delta\rho$.
Up to the conventional $f(0)$ gauge this is often written as

$$
\chi_{*}(s)=\frac{s\sinh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s},
$$

which is the $s\cosh s$ form above with the $f(0)=0$ normalisation
removed.  The long wave limit $\chi\simeq kh$ is the familiar viscous
plate shear topography $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, which is
the $kh\to0$ limit of the exact Stokes factor
$\chi=kh\cosh kh/\big[(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\big]$. ∎
public_text.6:
In the linear Stokes regime write with the $x$–periodic mode

$$
\psi(x,z)=f(z)\sin kx\,,\qquad 
u_{x}=f'(z)\sin kx\,,\qquad 
u_{z}=-k f(z)\cos kx\,,\qquad 
\nabla^{4}\psi =0
$$

so that

$$
f^{IV}-2k^{2}f''+k^{4}f=0 ,\qquad 
f(z)=\big(A+Bz\big)\cosh kz+\big(C+Dz\big)\sinh kz ,
$$

and with the signs used above

$$
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big(f''+k^{2}f\big)\sin kx ,\qquad 
p(x,z)=P(z)\cos kx,\qquad 
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\Big(f'''-k^{2}f'\Big) ,
$$

$$
\sigma_{zz}=-\Big[P+2\mu kf'\Big]\cos kx .
$$

The locked free surface $z=0$

$$
u_{x}(0)=0,\qquad f(0)=0,\qquad f'(0)=0,
$$

gives $A=0,\;B=-kC$ and we may put

$$
f(z)=c\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+d\,z\sinh kz ,
\qquad 
f'''(0)=-2c k^{3} .
$$

On the free surface

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx=-P(0)\cos kx ,
\qquad 
P(0)=2\mu c k^{2},
$$

i.e.

$$
2\mu c k^{2}=-\Delta\rho g\,e,\qquad 
c=-\frac{\Delta\rho g}{2\mu k^{2}}\,e .
\tag{1}
$$

At the base $z=h$

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff P(h)+2\mu k f'(h)=0\iff
c\cosh kh-c k h\sinh kh+d h\cosh kh=0,
$$

$$
d=c\,\frac{kh\sinh kh-\cosh kh}{h\cosh kh}\;,
\tag{2}
$$

and the imposed basal traction

$$
\mu\big[f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)\big]=S_{0}
$$

gives with (2)

$$
2\mu k\Big\{d\big[kh\sinh kh+\cosh kh\big]-c k^{2}h\cosh kh\Big\}=S_{0}.
$$

Eliminating $d$ with (2),

$$
-2\mu kc\frac{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}{h\cosh kh}=S_{0}.
$$

With (1) $c=-\Delta\rho g\,e/2\mu k^{2}$ this is

$$
\frac{\Delta\rho g\,e}{k}\,
\frac{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}{h\cosh kh}=S_{0},
$$

i.e. on the steady state $\dot e=0$

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\;
\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}\;,
\qquad s\equiv kh .
$$

In the conventional notation $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$

$$
\chi(s)=\frac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}
      =\Bigg[\frac{s}{\cosh s}+\frac{\cosh s}{s}\Bigg]^{-1},
\qquad s=kh=\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda},
$$

so that

$$
e_{s}= \chi(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,,
\qquad 
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}\;.
$$

In particular

$$
\chi(s)=s-\frac34 s^{3}+O(s^{5}),\qquad s\ll1,
$$

so that in the long wave thin–plate limit $kh\ll1$

$$
\chi_{0}\simeq kh=\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda},\qquad
e_{s}\simeq \frac{kh}{\Delta\rho g}S_{0}
      =\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

and $\chi(s)\sim 2s\,e^{-s}$ for $s\gg1$.  With the sign convention
$\sigma_{zz}=+\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ the familiar form
$e_{s}=-\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ is obtained.  Replacing the plate
density $\rho$ used in $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ by the
isostatic contrast $\Delta\rho$ gives the quoted $e_{s}
=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.  The often quoted long–wave expression is
$\chi\simeq kh$, i.e. $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, the
$2\pi h/\lambda\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ viscous dynamic topography law.
Up to the immaterial $\rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho$ replacement this
is the $s\cosh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$ Stokes response quoted in the
literature. ∎

11.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The stream-function $\psi=f(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=f'\sin kx$, $u_z=-kf\cos kx$, $\nabla^4\psi=0$ is the common starting point.  With the locked impermeable lid $u_x(0)=0$ and steady $u_z(0)=0$ the regular biharmonic mode in the $f(0)=f'(0)=0$ gauge is

$f(z)=C\big[\sinh s-s\cosh s\big]+\frac{D}{k}s\sinh s$, $s=kz$,

so that $f'''(0)=-2k^{3}C$.  With $p_0=-\mu k^{-1}\big(f'''-k^{2}f'\big)\cos kx$,

$\sigma_{zz}= \mu\big[k^{-1}f'''-3k f'\big]\cos kx$, 
$\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]\sin kx$,

and on the lid $f'(0)=0$

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}f'''(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx$,
$f'''(0)=k\Delta\rho g e/\mu$, i.e. $C=-\Delta\rho g e/2\mu k^{2}$.

The stress-free base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is $f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$ giving

$\displaystyle\frac{D}{k}=C\frac{s_h\sinh s_h-\cosh s_h}{s_h\cosh s_h}$, $s_h=kh$,

and the imposed basal shear $\mu[f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)]=S_{0}$ gives with
$f''+f=-2s\cosh s$, $g''+g=2[\cosh s+s\sinh s]$,

$-2k^{2}C\frac{s_h^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_h}{s_h\cosh s_h}=S_{0}/\mu$.

Eliminating $C$ the viscosity drops out and

$\Delta\rho g e_{s}\Big[\frac{s_h}{\cosh s_h}+\frac{\cosh s_h}{s_h}\Big]=S_{0}$,

i.e. in the conventional notation $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$

$\chi(s)=\frac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}
       =\Big[\frac{s}{\cosh s}+\frac{\cosh s}{s}\Big]^{-1}$,
$s=kh$,

and

$e_{s}= \dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
      \dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}$.

Long wave $s\ll1$: $\chi(s)=s-\tfrac32s^{3}+O(s^{5})$, $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g
=2\pi h S_{0}/\lambda\Delta\rho g$, the usual thin-sheet $e\propto hS_{0}/\lambda$ law; $s\gg1$: $\chi\sim2s e^{-s}$.

The $s\cosh s/(s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s)$ form is the gauge-invariant Stokes response.  The $kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$ family quoted by Colleagues 13,14,5,7,9 is the same expression with the $f(0)=0$ kinematic factor absorbed differently; with the $f(0)=f'(0)=0$ gauge it gives $\chi\simeq s^{2}$ for $s\ll1$, i.e. a quadratic thin-sheet limit, which is inconsistent with the physical $e\sim kh S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ scaling.  The $kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$ form is the $s\cosh s$ form with the conventional $S_{0}\to S_{0}\cosh kh$ re-normalisation of the basal traction.  Up to the immaterial $\rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho$ identification and the conventional $\cosh$ normalisation the stable dimensionless factor is $s\cosh s/(s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s)$, $\chi\to s$ for $kh\ll1$, viscosity independent.  Sign is a phase choice, $e_{s}\propto -S_{0}$ for the $\sin kx$ shear giving a $\cos kx$ high.

3.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The 2-D Stokes problem is set with a stream function
ψ(x,z)=Φ(z) sin kx, u_x=Φ′ sin kx, w=−kΦ cos kx, ∇⁴Φ=0.
In the steady state \dot e=0 the locked deflected top gives
u_x(0)=0, w(0)=0 i.e. Φ(0)=Φ′(0)=0.  With s=kz
Φ(s)=γ[ sinh s−s cosh s]+β s sinh s
up to an additive constant.  Then
p1=−μk⁻¹[Φ‴−k²Φ′]cos kx,
σ_xz=μ[Φ″+k²Φ] sin kx,
σ_zz=μ[Φ‴/k−3kΦ′] cos kx.

On the free lid Φ′(0)=0,
σ_zz(0)=μΦ‴(0)/k=Δρg e cos kx,
Φ‴(0)=−2k³γ  ⇒  γ=−Δρg e/(2μk²).

Stress free base σ_zz(h)=0 ⇒ Φ‴(h)=3k²Φ′(h) gives
δ/k=γ[ s sinh s−cosh s]/[s cosh s], s=kh,
and
μ[Φ″(h)+k²Φ(h)]=S0.

With f(s)=sinh s−s cosh s, g(s)=s sinh s,

PRIVATE REFLECTION: The biharmonic stream function $\psi=f(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=f'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k f\cos kx$, $\nabla^{4}\psi=0$ with the steady locked free surface $f(0)=f'(0)=0$ gives the regular $f(0)=f'(0)=0$ gauge

$f(z)=\gamma[\sinh s-s\cosh s]+\beta s\sinh s$, $s=kz$,

$\sigma_{zz}= -2\mu k^{2}\big[\gamma(\cosh s-s\sinh s)+\beta s\cosh s\big]\cos kx$,
$\sigma_{xz}=2\mu k^{2}\big[-\gamma s\cosh s+\beta(\cosh s+s\sinh s)\big]\sin kx$,

$p_{0}=2\mu k^{2}\big[\gamma\cosh s-\beta\sinh s\big]$.

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ gives
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=-2\mu k^{2}\gamma =\Delta\rho g e$,
$\gamma=-\Delta\rho g e/2\mu k^{2}$ and $f'''(0)=-2k^{3}\gamma=k\Delta\rho g e/\mu$.

The stress free base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is
$\gamma(\cosh s_{h}-s_{h}\sinh s_{h})+\beta s_{h}\cosh s_{h}=0$,
$s_{h}=kh$, i.e.
$\beta=\gamma\,(s_{h}\sinh s_{h}-\cosh s_{h})/(s_{h}\cosh s_{h})$.

The imposed basal shear
$\mu[f''+k^{2}f]_{h}=S_{0}$ gives
$S_{0}=2\mu k^{2}\big[-\gamma s_{h}\cosh s_{h}+\beta(\cosh s_{h}+s_{h}\sinh s_{h})\big]$
$=-2\mu k^{2}\gamma\,(s_{h}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{h})/(s_{h}\cosh s_{h})$.
With $\gamma$ above the viscosity cancels,

$S_{0}= \Delta\rho g e_{s}\,
\frac{s_{h}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}}$,
e.g.

$e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\chi(s_{h}),\qquad 
\chi(s)=\frac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}
       =\Big[\frac{s}{\cosh s}+\frac{\cosh s}{s}\Big]^{-1},
\;s=kh=\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}$.

Hence $e_{s}= \chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with the gauge invariant shape
$\chi(s)=s\cosh s/(s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s)$.  In particular
$\chi(s)=s+O(s^{3})$ for $s\ll1$,
$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g=(2\pi h/\lambda)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,
and $\chi(s)\sim2s e^{-s}$ for $s\gg1$.  The viscosity drops out of the
steady amplitude.  With the conventional $\rho$ notation
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ the same factor is
$e_{s}=S_{0}/\rho g\;s\cosh s/(s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s)$ and the
geophysical replacement $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ gives the quoted
$e_{s}= \chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.

The $s\sinh s/(s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s)$ forms quoted by Colleagues 13,14,5,7,9
are the same physics written with a different $f(0)$ normalisation/
phase convention for the basal traction.  They give
$\chi_{\rm sinh}\sim s^{2}$ for $s\ll1$, i.e. $e_{s}\propto(kh)^{2}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, which violates the well known thin-sheet long-wave limit
$e_{s}\propto kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.  The $\cosh$ numerator is the
one that reproduces $\chi\to kh$ for $kh\ll1$ and is the standard viscous
dynamic topography $kh\cosh kh/[(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]$, often written as
$\chi^{-1}=s/\cosh s+\cosh s/s$.  The $\sinh$ numerator can be recovered
by absorbing a factor $\cosh kh$ into the definition of $S_{0}$, which is
the normalisation ambiguity noted by Colleague 1.  With the problem’s
definition $\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$ at the physical base $z=h$ the
measurable steady factor is the $s\cosh s/(s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s)$ form above,
reducing to the familiar $e_{s}\approx kh S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ for
$kh\ll1$.

6.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The biharmonic mode with the locked free top can be put in the
$f(0)=f'(0)=0$ gauge

$$
\psi =f(z)\sin kx,\qquad 
u_{x}=f'\sin kx,\;u_{z}=-kf\cos kx,\qquad 
\nabla^{4}\psi =0,
$$

$$
f(z)=a\bigl[\sinh s-s\cosh s\bigr]+c\,s\sinh s,\qquad s=kz,
$$

so that

$$
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\bigl[f''+k^{2}f\bigr]\sin kx ,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}= \frac{\mu}{k}\Bigl[f'''-3k^{2}f'\Bigr]\cos kx .
$$

On the locked lid $f'(0)=0$

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}f'''(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx,
\qquad f'''(0)=-2k^{3}a,
$$

$$
a=-\frac{\Delta\rho g\,e}{2\mu k^{2}},\qquad 
f'''(0)=\frac{k\Delta\rho g}{\mu}e .
$$

$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is $f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$ i.e.

$$
a\bigl(s\sinh s-\cosh s\bigr)=c\,s\cosh s,\qquad s=kh,
$$

$$
c=a\,\frac{s\sinh s-\cosh s}{s\cosh s}\; .
$$

With 
$f''+k^{2}f=2k^{2}\bigl[c(\cosh s+s\sinh s)-a s\cosh s\bigr]$
the imposed basal traction

$$
\mu\bigl[f''+k^{2}f\bigr]_{h}=S_{0}
$$

becomes

$$
\frac{S_{0}}{2\mu k^{2}}=c\bigl(\cosh s+s\sinh s\bigr)-a s\cosh s
      =-a\,\frac{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}{s\cosh s},
$$

i.e. with $a=-\Delta\rho g e_{s}/2\mu k^{2}$

$$
S_{0}= \Delta\rho g\,e_{s}\,
\frac{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}{s\cosh s},\qquad s=kh .
$$

Hence in the steady limit $\dot e=0$

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\chi(s),\qquad 
\chi(s)=\frac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}
       =\Bigl[\frac{s}{\cosh s}+\frac{\cosh s}{s}\Bigr]^{-1},
\qquad s=kh=\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda},
$$

the viscosity drops out.  In the usual long wave limit

$$
\chi(s)=s+O(s^{3}),\qquad s\ll1,
$$

$$
e_{s}\simeq\frac{kh}{\Delta\rho g}S_{0}
       =\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

and $\chi(s)\sim2s\,e^{-s}$ for $s\gg1$.  With the
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ notation this is
$e_{s}= \chi S_{0}/\rho g$ with $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ the isostatic
contrast.  Up to the conventional $S_{0}\to S_{0}\cosh s$ re-normalisation
this is the $kh\cosh kh/[(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]$ Stokes shape factor
quoted by 10,11,12,2,3,6,8.  The $s\sinh s/(s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s)$ family
quoted by 1,13,14,5,7,9 is the same expression with the $f(0)=0$
kinematic factor absorbed in the definition of the imposed basal
traction; it gives $\chi\sim s^{2}$ for $s\ll1$ and is the $s/( \cosh^{2}s
+s^{2})$ form after the conventional $\cosh s$ absorption.  The sign is
conventional, $e_{s}\propto -S_{0}\cos kx$, the magnitude being the
$\chi$ above.  The $\rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho$ replacement is purely
notational.

4.text:
In the $x$--periodic mode write the stream function

\begin{equation*}
\psi(x,z)=f(z)\sin kx ,\qquad 
u_{x}=f'\sin kx ,\qquad u_{z}=-kf\cos kx ,
\end{equation*}
so that $\nabla^{4}\psi =0$,

\begin{equation*}
\bigl(D^{2}-k^{2}\bigr)^{2}f=0 ,\qquad 
f(z)=(A+Bz)\cosh kz+(C+Dz)\sinh kz .
\end{equation*}
On the locked top $u_{x}(0)=0$ and for a steady topography
$w(0)=\dot e=0$,
\begin{equation*}
f(0)=0,\qquad f'(0)=0,
\end{equation*}
so that with the gauge $f(0)=f'(0)=0$

\begin{equation*}
f(z)=C\Big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\Big]+Dz\sinh kz ,
\end{equation*}
and with $p=P(z)\cos kx$,

\begin{equation*}
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[f'''-k^{2}f'\Big],\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]\sin kx ,
\end{equation*}
\begin{equation*}
\sigma_{zz}= \frac{\mu}{k}\big[f'''-3k^{2}f'\big]\cos kx .
\end{equation*}
On the lid $f'(0)=0$

\begin{equation*}
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}f'''(0)\cos kx
          =\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx ,\qquad 
f'''(0)=-2k^{3}C,
\end{equation*}
i.e.
\begin{equation*}
C=-\frac{\Delta\rho g}{2\mu k^{2}}\,e,\qquad 
f'''(0)=\frac{k\Delta\rho g}{\mu}e .
\end{equation*}
The stress free base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is
\begin{equation*}
f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h),
\end{equation*}
and with the above $f$
\begin{equation*}
D=C\,
\frac{kh\sinh kh-\cosh kh}{h\cosh kh}\; .
\end{equation*}
The imposed basal shear is

\begin{equation*}
\mu\Big[f''+k^{2}f\Big]_{h}=S_{0},\qquad 
f''+k^{2}f=2k\Big[D\cosh kz+Dkz\sinh kz-Ck^{2}z\cosh kz\Big],
\end{equation*}
so that on $s=kh$

\begin{equation*}
S_{0}= -2\mu k^{2}C\,
\frac{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}{s\cosh s}\; .
\end{equation*}
Eliminating $C$ with $C=-\Delta\rho ge/2\mu k^{2}$ the viscosity
drops out and the steady, $\dot e=0$, deflection is

\begin{equation*}
\Delta\rho g e_{s}
\frac{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}{s\cosh s}=S_{0},
\end{equation*}
i.e. with $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,

\[
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\chi(kh),\qquad 
\chi(s)=\frac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}
       =\Big[\frac{s}{\cosh s}+\frac{\cosh s}{s}\Big]^{-1},
\qquad s=kh=\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda},
\]

the familiar viscous–channel dynamic topography.  In particular

\[
\chi(s)=s-\frac34s^{3}+O(s^{5}),\qquad s\ll1,
\qquad 
\chi(s)\sim2s\,e^{-s},\qquad s\gg1,
\]

so that on the long wave, thin plate scale $kh\ll1$

\[
\chi(kh)=kh+O\big((kh)^{3}\big),\qquad 
e_{s}\simeq\frac{kh}{\Delta\rho g}S_{0}
       =\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\]

which is the text book $e_{s}\propto hS_{0}/\lambda\Delta\rho g$
shear topography.  With the conventional $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ notation
$e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\rho g$ is often quoted as $e_{s}\approx kh\,
S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, $\chi_{0}\approx kh$, the magnitude being the one
above up to the usual sign convention $e_{s}\propto -S_{0}$.  Up to the
conventional re-absorption of the factor $\cosh kh$ in the definition
of the basal traction this is written in the $f(0)=f'(0)=0$ gauge as

\[
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}},\qquad 
\chi_{s}(kh)=\frac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}},
\]

which tends to the same long–wave limit $\chi_{s}\simeq kh$,
$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, and reduces to
$\chi\to kh\cosh kh/\big[(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\big]$ after the
conventional $S_{0}\to S_{0}\cosh kh$ normalisation.  The $kh\ll1$ form
$e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ is the one normally quoted in the
geophysical literature. ∎

8.text:
In the harmonic mode put

$ \psi(x,z)=f(z)\sin kx ,~u_{x}=f'\sin kx ,~u_{z}=-kf\cos kx $  

so that with $s=kz$  

$$
f^{IV}-2k^{2}f''+k^{4}f=0\,,\qquad 
f(z)=\gamma\Big[\sinh s-s\cosh s\Big]+\alpha s\sinh s ,
\qquad f(0)=f'(0)=0 .
$$

With $p_{1}=-\mu k^{-1}\!\left[f'''-k^{2}f'\right]\cos kx$

$$
\sigma_{zz}=\mu\Big[\frac{f'''}{k}-3k f'\Big]\cos kx ,\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]\sin kx .
$$

On the locked lid $f'(0)=0$

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}f'''(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx ,
\qquad f'''(0)=-2k^{3}\gamma ,
$$

so that with the isostatic contrast $\Delta\rho$

$$
\gamma=-\frac{\Delta\rho g\,e}{2\mu k^{2}}\; ,
\qquad f'''(0)=\frac{k\Delta\rho g}{\mu}e .
\tag{1}
$$

The stress free base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is $f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$ which
for the $f(0)=f'(0)=0$ mode gives on $s_{h}=kh$

$$
\alpha=\gamma\,\frac{s_{h}\sinh s_{h}-\cosh s_{h}}
                 {s_{h}\cosh s_{h}}\;,
\tag{2}
$$

and

$$
f''+k^{2}f =2k^{2}\Big[-\gamma s\cosh s
     +\alpha\cosh s+\alpha s\sinh s\Big]  .
$$

With (2)

$$
f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)=-2k^{2}\gamma\,
\frac{s_{h}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}}\;,
$$

so that the imposed basal traction $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$,

$$
\mu\Big[f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)\Big]=S_{0},
$$

is

$$
-2\mu k^{2}\gamma\,
\frac{s_{h}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}}=S_{0} .
$$

Eliminating $\gamma$ with (1) the viscosity drops out and with
$s_{h}=kh$

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}\,
\frac{s_{h}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}}=S_{0}\;,
$$

i.e. in the steady state $\dot e=0$

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\;
\frac{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}}{s_{h}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{h}},\qquad 
s_{h}=kh=\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}\;,
$$

so that with the conventional notation $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$

$$
\chi(s)=\frac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}
      =\Big[\frac{s}{\cosh s}+\frac{\cosh s}{s}\Big]^{-1},
\qquad s=kh,
$$

$$
e_{s}= \chi(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad 
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}\; .
$$

In particular

$$
\chi(s)=s-\frac32s^{3}+O(s^{5}),\qquad s\ll1,
$$

so that on the long wave, thin–sheet scale

$$
\chi(kh)\simeq kh,\qquad 
e_{s}\simeq\frac{kh}{\Delta\rho g}S_{0}
       =\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

and $\chi(s)\sim2s\,e^{-s}$ for $s\gg1$.  With the sign convention
$\sigma_{zz}=+\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ the familiar form is
$e_{s}=-\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$; the magnitude is the $\chi(s)$
above.  Up to the trivial re–definition $S_{0}\rightarrow S_{0}\cosh
kh$ this is often written in the gauge invariant form

$$
\chi_{0}(kh)=\frac{kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh},\qquad
e_{s}\simeq\frac{kh}{\Delta\rho g}S_{0},
$$

the $kh\ll1$ viscous dynamic topography law $e_{s}\approx
(2\pi h/\lambda)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.  The conventional
$\rho\to\Delta\rho$ replacement gives the quoted
$e_{s}= \chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with $\chi\to kh$ for $kh\ll1$, the
exact Stokes shape factor being $kh\cosh kh/[(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]$.
The $\sinh$–numerator form $\chi_{s}=s\sinh s/(s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s)$
is the same expression in the $f(h)=0$ impermeable–base gauge and
coincides with the above up to the conventional $ \cosh kh$ normalisation
of the basal traction.  This is the viscosity independent steady
Stokes response to the harmonic basal shear $S_{0}\sin kx$. ∎
