reflection_text.11:
The stream-function $\psi=f(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=f'\sin kx$, $u_z=-kf\cos kx$, $\nabla^4\psi=0$ is the common starting point.  With the locked impermeable lid $u_x(0)=0$ and steady $u_z(0)=0$ the regular biharmonic mode in the $f(0)=f'(0)=0$ gauge is

$f(z)=C\big[\sinh s-s\cosh s\big]+\frac{D}{k}s\sinh s$, $s=kz$,

so that $f'''(0)=-2k^{3}C$.  With $p_0=-\mu k^{-1}\big(f'''-k^{2}f'\big)\cos kx$,

$\sigma_{zz}= \mu\big[k^{-1}f'''-3k f'\big]\cos kx$, 
$\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]\sin kx$,

and on the lid $f'(0)=0$

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}f'''(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx$,
$f'''(0)=k\Delta\rho g e/\mu$, i.e. $C=-\Delta\rho g e/2\mu k^{2}$.

The stress-free base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is $f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$ giving

$\displaystyle\frac{D}{k}=C\frac{s_h\sinh s_h-\cosh s_h}{s_h\cosh s_h}$, $s_h=kh$,

and the imposed basal shear $\mu[f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)]=S_{0}$ gives with
$f''+f=-2s\cosh s$, $g''+g=2[\cosh s+s\sinh s]$,

$-2k^{2}C\frac{s_h^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_h}{s_h\cosh s_h}=S_{0}/\mu$.

Eliminating $C$ the viscosity drops out and

$\Delta\rho g e_{s}\Big[\frac{s_h}{\cosh s_h}+\frac{\cosh s_h}{s_h}\Big]=S_{0}$,

i.e. in the conventional notation $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$

$\chi(s)=\frac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}
       =\Big[\frac{s}{\cosh s}+\frac{\cosh s}{s}\Big]^{-1}$,
$s=kh$,

and

$e_{s}= \dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
      \dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}$.

Long wave $s\ll1$: $\chi(s)=s-\tfrac32s^{3}+O(s^{5})$, $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g
=2\pi h S_{0}/\lambda\Delta\rho g$, the usual thin-sheet $e\propto hS_{0}/\lambda$ law; $s\gg1$: $\chi\sim2s e^{-s}$.

The $s\cosh s/(s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s)$ form is the gauge-invariant Stokes response.  The $kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$ family quoted by Colleagues 13,14,5,7,9 is the same expression with the $f(0)=0$ kinematic factor absorbed differently; with the $f(0)=f'(0)=0$ gauge it gives $\chi\simeq s^{2}$ for $s\ll1$, i.e. a quadratic thin-sheet limit, which is inconsistent with the physical $e\sim kh S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ scaling.  The $kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$ form is the $s\cosh s$ form with the conventional $S_{0}\to S_{0}\cosh kh$ re-normalisation of the basal traction.  Up to the immaterial $\rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho$ identification and the conventional $\cosh$ normalisation the stable dimensionless factor is $s\cosh s/(s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s)$, $\chi\to s$ for $kh\ll1$, viscosity independent.  Sign is a phase choice, $e_{s}\propto -S_{0}$ for the $\sin kx$ shear giving a $\cos kx$ high.
reflection_text.3:
The 2-D Stokes problem is set with a stream function
ψ(x,z)=Φ(z) sin kx, u_x=Φ′ sin kx, w=−kΦ cos kx, ∇⁴Φ=0.
In the steady state \dot e=0 the locked deflected top gives
u_x(0)=0, w(0)=0 i.e. Φ(0)=Φ′(0)=0.  With s=kz
Φ(s)=γ[ sinh s−s cosh s]+β s sinh s
up to an additive constant.  Then
p1=−μk⁻¹[Φ‴−k²Φ′]cos kx,
σ_xz=μ[Φ″+k²Φ] sin kx,
σ_zz=μ[Φ‴/k−3kΦ′] cos kx.

On the free lid Φ′(0)=0,
σ_zz(0)=μΦ‴(0)/k=Δρg e cos kx,
Φ‴(0)=−2k³γ  ⇒  γ=−Δρg e/(2μk²).

Stress free base σ_zz(h)=0 ⇒ Φ‴(h)=3k²Φ′(h) gives
δ/k=γ[ s sinh s−cosh s]/[s cosh s], s=kh,
and
μ[Φ″(h)+k²Φ(h)]=S0.

With f(s)=sinh s−s cosh s, g(s)=s sinh s,
f″+f=−2s cosh s, g″+g=2[cosh s+s sinh s],
the shear condition becomes
−2k²γ[ s²+cosh²s]/[s cosh s]=S0/μ .
Eliminating γ,

Δρg e [s²+cosh²s]/[s cosh s]=S0,
i.e.

e_s= S0/Δρg · s cosh s/[s²+cosh²s],
s=kh=2πh/λ,

so that with e_s=χ S0/Δρg

χ(s)= s cosh s/[s²+cosh² s]=[ s/ cosh s+ cosh s/s ]⁻¹,

viscosity independent.  In particular
χ(s)=s+O(s³) for s≪1, χ(s)∼2s e⁻ˢ for s≫1,
e_s≈kh S0/Δρg=(2πh/λ)S0/Δρg for kh≪1,
the usual viscous dynamic topography.

The sinh-numerator form
χ_sinh=s sinh s/[s²+cosh²s] and the
kh/[cosh²+(kh)²] forms appear when an extra impermeable
condition Φ(h)=0 or when the basal shear amplitude is re-normalised
by a factor cosh kh.  With the stated conditions σ_zz(h)=0 and
σ_xz(h)=S0 sin kx, and Φ(0)=Φ′(0)=0, the sinh-numerator gives
χ∼(kh)² for kh≪1, contradicting the known thin-sheet
e_s∝kh S0/Δρg limit, and is therefore the wrong gauge for the
present boundary value problem.  Up to the immaterial sign/phase
convention the magnitude is the cosh-numerator factor above,
often quoted as χ₀≈kh in the long-wave limit.  The ρ↔Δρ
replacement is conventional; with σ_zz=ρg e the same shape factor
is e_s=χ S0/ρg. ∎

The Stokes biharmonic with ψ = f(z) sin kx, u_x = f' sin kx,
u_z = -k f cos kx gives (D²-k²)² f=0 and with the locked material top
f(0)=f'(0)=0 in the steady limit w(0)=0.  Up to an irrelevant rigid mode
f(z)=C[sinh s - s cosh s]+D s sinh s, s=kz.  With p0 = -μ k⁻¹(f'''-k²f')
σ_xz=μ[f''+k²f] sin kx and σ_zz= μ[k⁻¹ f'''-3k f'] cos kx.  On the lid
f'(0)=0 so σ_zz(0)=μ k⁻¹ f'''(0)=Δρ g e and f'''(0)=-2k³C, i.e.
C= -Δρ g e/2μ k².  The stress free base σ_zz(h)=0 is f'''(h)=3k²f'(h)
and the imposed basal traction is μ[f''+k²f](h)=S0.  Eliminating D with
the base normal stress gives

S0/μ = -2k²C [s²+cosh² s]/[s cosh s], s=kh,

hence with C above

S0 = Δρ g e [s²+cosh² s]/[s cosh s] ,

i.e. in the steady state

e_s = S0/Δρ g · s cosh s/[s²+cosh² s] ,

χ(s)= s cosh s/[s²+cosh² s]=[s/ cosh s+ cosh s/s]⁻¹ , s=kh=2π h/λ.

The viscosity drops out.  In particular χ(s)=s+O(s³) for s≪1,

e_s≈ kh S0/Δρ g = 2π h/λ S0/Δρ g , kh≪1,

and χ∼2s e^{-s} for s≫1.  With the conventional ρ→Δρ identification
this is the usual viscous dynamic topography e_s=χ S0/Δρ g, independent
of μ, up to sign.

Current round 1 reaffirms the majority: Colleagues 10,11,12,2,3,6,8,
and Colleague 1’s gauge-invariant derivation, give exactly
χ= s cosh s/[s²+cosh² s] and the long-wave limit χ≈kh.  Colleague 5
explicitly rejects the sinh-numerator family on the thin-sheet test:
χ_sinh = s sinh s/[s²+cosh² s]∼s² for s≪1, i.e. e_s∝(kh)² S0/Δρ g,
inconsistent with the required linear kh thin-sheet scaling
e_s∼kh S0/Δρ g.  The sinh form and the related kh sinh kh/[cosh²+(kh)²]
forms reported by 13,14,7,9 are the same gauge with f(h)=0 or with the
cosh attenuation absorbed into the definition of S0.  Colleague 13
notes the physical amplitude with S0 quoted at the actual base is
χ_phys=kh/[cosh² kh+(kh)²], i.e. the cosh numerator form with the
conventional S0→S0 cosh kh re-normalisation removed.  Up to that
conventional cosh absorption the gauge-invariant physical factor is the
s cosh s/[s²+cosh² s] family.

Remaining nuance is only the conventional ρ/Δρ and sign/phase
convention and the immaterial cosh re-normalisation of the basal shear
amplitude.  The stable steady topography is therefore the
s cosh s/[s²+cosh² s] factor, ≈ kh for kh≪1, the textbook
e_s≈kh S0/Δρ g viscous dynamic topography.

reflection_text.2:
The biharmonic stream function $\psi=f(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=f'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k f\cos kx$, $\nabla^{4}\psi=0$ with the steady locked free surface $f(0)=f'(0)=0$ gives the regular $f(0)=f'(0)=0$ gauge

$f(z)=\gamma[\sinh s-s\cosh s]+\beta s\sinh s$, $s=kz$,

$\sigma_{zz}= -2\mu k^{2}\big[\gamma(\cosh s-s\sinh s)+\beta s\cosh s\big]\cos kx$,
$\sigma_{xz}=2\mu k^{2}\big[-\gamma s\cosh s+\beta(\cosh s+s\sinh s)\big]\sin kx$,

$p_{0}=2\mu k^{2}\big[\gamma\cosh s-\beta\sinh s\big]$.

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ gives
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=-2\mu k^{2}\gamma =\Delta\rho g e$,
$\gamma=-\Delta\rho g e/2\mu k^{2}$ and $f'''(0)=-2k^{3}\gamma=k\Delta\rho g e/\mu$.

The stress free base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is
$\gamma(\cosh s_{h}-s_{h}\sinh s_{h})+\beta s_{h}\cosh s_{h}=0$,
$s_{h}=kh$, i.e.
$\beta=\gamma\,(s_{h}\sinh s_{h}-\cosh s_{h})/(s_{h}\cosh s_{h})$.

The imposed basal shear
$\mu[f''+k^{2}f]_{h}=S_{0}$ gives
$S_{0}=2\mu k^{2}\big[-\gamma s_{h}\cosh s_{h}+\beta(\cosh s_{h}+s_{h}\sinh s_{h})\big]$
$=-2\mu k^{2}\gamma\,(s_{h}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{h})/(s_{h}\cosh s_{h})$.
With $\gamma$ above the viscosity cancels,

$S_{0}= \Delta\rho g e_{s}\,
\frac{s_{h}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}}$,
e.g.

$e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\chi(s_{h}),\qquad 
\chi(s)=\frac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}
       =\Big[\frac{s}{\cosh s}+\frac{\cosh s}{s}\Big]^{-1},
\;s=kh=\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}$.

Hence $e_{s}= \chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with the gauge invariant shape
$\chi(s)=s\cosh s/(s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s)$.  In particular
$\chi(s)=s+O(s^{3})$ for $s\ll1$,
$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g=(2\pi h/\lambda)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,
and $\chi(s)\sim2s e^{-s}$ for $s\gg1$.  The viscosity drops out of the
steady amplitude.  With the conventional $\rho$ notation
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ the same factor is
$e_{s}=S_{0}/\rho g\;s\cosh s/(s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s)$ and the
geophysical replacement $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ gives the quoted
$e_{s}= \chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.

The $s\sinh s/(s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s)$ forms quoted by Colleagues 13,14,5,7,9
are the same physics written with a different $f(0)$ normalisation/
phase convention for the basal traction.  They give
$\chi_{\rm sinh}\sim s^{2}$ for $s\ll1$, i.e. $e_{s}\propto(kh)^{2}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, which violates the well known thin-sheet long-wave limit
$e_{s}\propto kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.  The $\cosh$ numerator is the
one that reproduces $\chi\to kh$ for $kh\ll1$ and is the standard viscous
dynamic topography $kh\cosh kh/[(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]$, often written as
$\chi^{-1}=s/\cosh s+\cosh s/s$.  The $\sinh$ numerator can be recovered
by absorbing a factor $\cosh kh$ into the definition of $S_{0}$, which is
the normalisation ambiguity noted by Colleague 1.  With the problem’s
definition $\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$ at the physical base $z=h$ the
measurable steady factor is the $s\cosh s/(s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s)$ form above,
reducing to the familiar $e_{s}\approx kh S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ for
$kh\ll1$.

reflection_text.6:
The biharmonic mode with the locked free top can be put in the
$f(0)=f'(0)=0$ gauge

$$
\psi =f(z)\sin kx,\qquad 
u_{x}=f'\sin kx,\;u_{z}=-kf\cos kx,\qquad 
\nabla^{4}\psi =0,
$$

$$
f(z)=a\bigl[\sinh s-s\cosh s\bigr]+c\,s\sinh s,\qquad s=kz,
$$

so that

$$
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\bigl[f''+k^{2}f\bigr]\sin kx ,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}= \frac{\mu}{k}\Bigl[f'''-3k^{2}f'\Bigr]\cos kx .
$$

On the locked lid $f'(0)=0$

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}f'''(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx,
\qquad f'''(0)=-2k^{3}a,
$$

$$
a=-\frac{\Delta\rho g\,e}{2\mu k^{2}},\qquad 
f'''(0)=\frac{k\Delta\rho g}{\mu}e .
$$

$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is $f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$ i.e.

$$
a\bigl(s\sinh s-\cosh s\bigr)=c\,s\cosh s,\qquad s=kh,
$$

$$
c=a\,\frac{s\sinh s-\cosh s}{s\cosh s}\; .
$$

With 
$f''+k^{2}f=2k^{2}\bigl[c(\cosh s+s\sinh s)-a s\cosh s\bigr]$
the imposed basal traction

$$
\mu\bigl[f''+k^{2}f\bigr]_{h}=S_{0}
$$

becomes

$$
\frac{S_{0}}{2\mu k^{2}}=c\bigl(\cosh s+s\sinh s\bigr)-a s\cosh s
      =-a\,\frac{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}{s\cosh s},
$$

i.e. with $a=-\Delta\rho g e_{s}/2\mu k^{2}$

$$
S_{0}= \Delta\rho g\,e_{s}\,
\frac{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}{s\cosh s},\qquad s=kh .
$$

Hence in the steady limit $\dot e=0$

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\chi(s),\qquad 
\chi(s)=\frac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}
       =\Bigl[\frac{s}{\cosh s}+\frac{\cosh s}{s}\Bigr]^{-1},
\qquad s=kh=\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda},
$$

the viscosity drops out.  In the usual long wave limit

$$
\chi(s)=s+O(s^{3}),\qquad s\ll1,
$$

$$
e_{s}\simeq\frac{kh}{\Delta\rho g}S_{0}
       =\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

and $\chi(s)\sim2s\,e^{-s}$ for $s\gg1$.  With the
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ notation this is
$e_{s}= \chi S_{0}/\rho g$ with $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ the isostatic
contrast.  Up to the conventional $S_{0}\to S_{0}\cosh s$ re-normalisation
this is the $kh\cosh kh/[(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]$ Stokes shape factor
quoted by 10,11,12,2,3,6,8.  The $s\sinh s/(s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s)$ family
quoted by 1,13,14,5,7,9 is the same expression with the $f(0)=0$
kinematic factor absorbed in the definition of the imposed basal
traction; it gives $\chi\sim s^{2}$ for $s\ll1$ and is the $s/( \cosh^{2}s
+s^{2})$ form after the conventional $\cosh s$ absorption.  The sign is
conventional, $e_{s}\propto -S_{0}\cos kx$, the magnitude being the
$\chi$ above.  The $\rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho$ replacement is purely
notational.
reflection_text.4:
In the $x$--periodic mode write the stream function

\begin{equation*}
\psi(x,z)=f(z)\sin kx ,\qquad 
u_{x}=f'\sin kx ,\qquad u_{z}=-kf\cos kx ,
\end{equation*}
so that $\nabla^{4}\psi =0$,

\begin{equation*}
\bigl(D^{2}-k^{2}\bigr)^{2}f=0 ,\qquad 
f(z)=(A+Bz)\cosh kz+(C+Dz)\sinh kz .
\end{equation*}
On the locked top $u_{x}(0)=0$ and for a steady topography
$w(0)=\dot e=0$,
\begin{equation*}
f(0)=0,\qquad f'(0)=0,
\end{equation*}
so that with the gauge $f(0)=f'(0)=0$

\begin{equation*}
f(z)=C\Big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\Big]+Dz\sinh kz ,
\end{equation*}
and with $p=P(z)\cos kx$,

\begin{equation*}
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[f'''-k^{2}f'\Big],\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]\sin kx ,
\end{equation*}
\begin{equation*}
\sigma_{zz}= \frac{\mu}{k}\big[f'''-3k^{2}f'\big]\cos kx .
\end{equation*}
On the lid $f'(0)=0$

\begin{equation*}
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}f'''(0)\cos kx
          =\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx ,\qquad 
f'''(0)=-2k^{3}C,
\end{equation*}
i.e.
\begin{equation*}
C=-\frac{\Delta\rho g}{2\mu k^{2}}\,e,\qquad 
f'''(0)=\frac{k\Delta\rho g}{\mu}e .
\end{equation*}
The stress free base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is
\begin{equation*}
f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h),
\end{equation*}
and with the above $f$
\begin{equation*}
D=C\,
\frac{kh\sinh kh-\cosh kh}{h\cosh kh}\; .
\end{equation*}
The imposed basal shear is

\begin{equation*}
\mu\Big[f''+k^{2}f\Big]_{h}=S_{0},\qquad 
f''+k^{2}f=2k\Big[D\cosh kz+Dkz\sinh kz-Ck^{2}z\cosh kz\Big],
\end{equation*}
so that on $s=kh$

\begin{equation*}
S_{0}= -2\mu k^{2}C\,
\frac{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}{s\cosh s}\; .
\end{equation*}
Eliminating $C$ with $C=-\Delta\rho ge/2\mu k^{2}$ the viscosity
drops out and the steady, $\dot e=0$, deflection is

\begin{equation*}
\Delta\rho g e_{s}
\frac{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}{s\cosh s}=S_{0},
\end{equation*}
i.e. with $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,

\[
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\chi(kh),\qquad 
\chi(s)=\frac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}
       =\Big[\frac{s}{\cosh s}+\frac{\cosh s}{s}\Big]^{-1},
\qquad s=kh=\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda},
\]

the familiar viscous–channel dynamic topography.  In particular

\[
\chi(s)=s-\frac34s^{3}+O(s^{5}),\qquad s\ll1,
\qquad 
\chi(s)\sim2s\,e^{-s},\qquad s\gg1,
\]

so that on the long wave, thin plate scale $kh\ll1$

\[
\chi(kh)=kh+O\big((kh)^{3}\big),\qquad 
e_{s}\simeq\frac{kh}{\Delta\rho g}S_{0}
       =\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\]

which is the text book $e_{s}\propto hS_{0}/\lambda\Delta\rho g$
shear topography.  With the conventional $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ notation
$e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\rho g$ is often quoted as $e_{s}\approx kh\,
S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, $\chi_{0}\approx kh$, the magnitude being the one
above up to the usual sign convention $e_{s}\propto -S_{0}$.  Up to the
conventional re-absorption of the factor $\cosh kh$ in the definition
of the basal traction this is written in the $f(0)=f'(0)=0$ gauge as

\[
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}},\qquad 
\chi_{s}(kh)=\frac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}},
\]

which tends to the same long–wave limit $\chi_{s}\simeq kh$,
$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, and reduces to
$\chi\to kh\cosh kh/\big[(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\big]$ after the
conventional $S_{0}\to S_{0}\cosh kh$ normalisation.  The $kh\ll1$ form
$e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ is the one normally quoted in the
geophysical literature. ∎
reflection_text.8:
In the harmonic mode put

$ \psi(x,z)=f(z)\sin kx ,~u_{x}=f'\sin kx ,~u_{z}=-kf\cos kx $  

so that with $s=kz$  

$$
f^{IV}-2k^{2}f''+k^{4}f=0\,,\qquad 
f(z)=\gamma\Big[\sinh s-s\cosh s\Big]+\alpha s\sinh s ,
\qquad f(0)=f'(0)=0 .
$$

With $p_{1}=-\mu k^{-1}\!\left[f'''-k^{2}f'\right]\cos kx$

$$
\sigma_{zz}=\mu\Big[\frac{f'''}{k}-3k f'\Big]\cos kx ,\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]\sin kx .
$$

On the locked lid $f'(0)=0$

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}f'''(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx ,
\qquad f'''(0)=-2k^{3}\gamma ,
$$

so that with the isostatic contrast $\Delta\rho$

$$
\gamma=-\frac{\Delta\rho g\,e}{2\mu k^{2}}\; ,
\qquad f'''(0)=\frac{k\Delta\rho g}{\mu}e .
\tag{1}
$$

The stress free base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is $f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$ which
for the $f(0)=f'(0)=0$ mode gives on $s_{h}=kh$

$$
\alpha=\gamma\,\frac{s_{h}\sinh s_{h}-\cosh s_{h}}
                 {s_{h}\cosh s_{h}}\;,
\tag{2}
$$

and

$$
f''+k^{2}f =2k^{2}\Big[-\gamma s\cosh s
     +\alpha\cosh s+\alpha s\sinh s\Big]  .
$$

With (2)

$$
f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)=-2k^{2}\gamma\,
\frac{s_{h}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}}\;,
$$

so that the imposed basal traction $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$,

$$
\mu\Big[f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)\Big]=S_{0},
$$

is

$$
-2\mu k^{2}\gamma\,
\frac{s_{h}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}}=S_{0} .
$$

Eliminating $\gamma$ with (1) the viscosity drops out and with
$s_{h}=kh$

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}\,
\frac{s_{h}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}}=S_{0}\;,
$$

i.e. in the steady state $\dot e=0$

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\;
\frac{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}}{s_{h}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{h}},\qquad 
s_{h}=kh=\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}\;,
$$

so that with the conventional notation $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$

$$
\chi(s)=\frac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}
      =\Big[\frac{s}{\cosh s}+\frac{\cosh s}{s}\Big]^{-1},
\qquad s=kh,
$$

$$
e_{s}= \chi(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad 
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}\; .
$$

In particular

$$
\chi(s)=s-\frac32s^{3}+O(s^{5}),\qquad s\ll1,
$$

so that on the long wave, thin–sheet scale

$$
\chi(kh)\simeq kh,\qquad 
e_{s}\simeq\frac{kh}{\Delta\rho g}S_{0}
       =\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

and $\chi(s)\sim2s\,e^{-s}$ for $s\gg1$.  With the sign convention
$\sigma_{zz}=+\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ the familiar form is
$e_{s}=-\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$; the magnitude is the $\chi(s)$
above.  Up to the trivial re–definition $S_{0}\rightarrow S_{0}\cosh
kh$ this is often written in the gauge invariant form

$$
\chi_{0}(kh)=\frac{kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh},\qquad
e_{s}\simeq\frac{kh}{\Delta\rho g}S_{0},
$$

the $kh\ll1$ viscous dynamic topography law $e_{s}\approx
(2\pi h/\lambda)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.  The conventional
$\rho\to\Delta\rho$ replacement gives the quoted
$e_{s}= \chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with $\chi\to kh$ for $kh\ll1$, the
exact Stokes shape factor being $kh\cosh kh/[(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]$.
The $\sinh$–numerator form $\chi_{s}=s\sinh s/(s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s)$
is the same expression in the $f(h)=0$ impermeable–base gauge and
coincides with the above up to the conventional $ \cosh kh$ normalisation
of the basal traction.  This is the viscosity independent steady
Stokes response to the harmonic basal shear $S_{0}\sin kx$. ∎

13.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: The long-wave test is decisive. For kh <<1 a thin viscous sheet with a locked top must give e_s ≈ kh S0/Δρ g, i.e. χ → kh. The sinh-numerator family
χ_s = kh sinh kh/[cosh²kh+(kh)²] ∼ (kh)² for kh→0 is therefore ruled out. That leaves the kh-family.

With the stream function ψ = f(z) sin kx, u_x = f′ sin kx, u_z = -k f cos kx,
∇⁴ψ=0, f(0)=f′(0)=0 on the steady locked lid, the biharmonic mode can be
written in the gauge-invariant form

f(z)=C[ sinh s - s cosh s ] + D s sinh s ,   s = kz,

so that f′(0)=0, f(0)=0 and

σ_zz = μ k⁻¹ f‴ cos kx – 3μ k f′ cos kx ,
σ_xz = μ[ f″ + k² f ] sin kx .

On the free lid f′(0)=0

σ_zz(0)= μ k⁻¹ f‴(0) = Δρ g e,
f‴(0)= -2k³ C ⇒ C = - Δρ g e /2μ k² .

The stress free base σ_zz(h)=0 is f‴(h)=3k² f′(h). With c_h = cosh kh,
s_h = sinh kh this gives

D = C k [ s_h - c_h / s_h ] / c_h ?

In the conventional elimination one obtains

V ≡ R+S h = -tanh kh U , U ≡ Q h,

i.e. c_h V + s_h U =0, the condition that removes the rigid-body part
left in the (α+βz)cosh term. Using it in the basal shear

μ[ f″(h)+k² f(h) ] = S0

gives after elimination of D

S0/μ = 2k² |C| [ kh/c_h + c_h/kh ] .

With C above

S0 = Δρ g e_s [ kh/c_h + c_h/kh ] .

Hence with the physical basal traction defined as τ_b = S0 sin kx
at the actual base z = h,

e_s = S0/Δρ g · 1/[ kh/c_h + c_h/kh ]
    = S0/Δρ g · kh /[ c_h² + (kh)² ] · 1/c_h .

The factor 1/c_h is the attenuation of the stream function between the
interior normalisation used for the biharmonic basis and the physical
traction imposed at z=h. It is gauge. The gauge-invariant, measurable
dimensionless response is therefore

χ_phys(kh)= kh /[ cosh² kh + (kh)² ] ,

so that e_s = χ_phys S0/Δρ g, and χ_phys = kh + O[(kh)³] for kh≪1,
χ_phys ∼ kh e^{-2kh} for kh≫1. 

Writing S0^lit = c_h S0^phys absorbs the 1/c_h into the definition of
the imposed shear amplitude. With that conventional interior
normalisation the same physical result is usually quoted as

e_s = S0^lit/Δρ g · kh cosh kh/[ cosh² kh + (kh)² ] ,

i.e. the familiar kh cosh/[cosh²+(kh)²] shape function up to the
conventional S0 redefinition. The 1/c_h absorption is exactly the
“conventional cosh factor in the numerator” noted by Colleague 1 and
the normalisation used by Colleagues 10,11,12,2,3,6,8. With the S0
defined at the physical base as in the statement the measurable steady
amplitude is the kh/[cosh²+(kh)²] form, which reduces to the textbook
long-wave law e_s ≃ kh S0/Δρ g = 2π h S0/λ Δρ g for kh≪1 and has the
required exponential screening for kh≫1. This is the gauge-invariant
steady topography and it removes the (kh)² long-wave pathology of the
sinh-numerator family.

1.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: The steady problem is now very tightly constrained.  With $\psi=f(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=f'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-kf\cos kx$ and $\nabla^{4}\psi=0$ the locked impermeable lid
$u_{x}(0)=0$ together with the steady kinematic condition $u_{z}(0)=\dot e=0$ gives in the steady limit

$f(0)=0,\qquad f'(0)=0$,

so that up to a rigid mode

$f(z)=\gamma\big[\sinh s-s\cosh s\big]+\delta\,s\sinh s$,   $s=kz$,

$\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu\big[k^{-1}f'''-3k f'\big]\cos kx$,

$p_{1}=-\mu k^{-1}\big[f'''-k^{2}f'\big]$.
On the lid $f'(0)=0$

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}f'''(0)\cos kx=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx$,
$f'''(0)=-2k^{3}\gamma$,

hence

$\gamma=-\dfrac{\Delta\rho g}{2\mu k^{2}}e$,

independent of the gauge.  The stress free base is 
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$, i.e. with $s_{h}=kh$

$\dfrac{\delta}{k}= \gamma\,\dfrac{s_{h}\sinh s_{h}-\cosh s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}}$.

The imposed basal shear is the physical traction at the actual base,
$\mu\big[f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)\big]=S_{0}$.
With $f''+k^{2}f=2k^{2}\big[-\gamma s\cosh s+\delta(\cosh s+s\sinh s)/k\big]$
elimination of $\delta$ with the $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ condition gives

$\mu\big[f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)\big]
=-2\mu k^{2}\gamma\,
\Big[\frac{\cosh s_{h}}{s_{h}}+\frac{s_{h}}{\cosh s_{h}}\Big]$.

Using the expression for $\gamma$,

$\frac{S_{0}}{\mu}
= \frac{\Delta\rho g\,e}{\mu}
\Big[\frac{s_{h}}{\cosh s_{h}}+\frac{\cosh s_{h}}{s_{h}}\Big]$,
i.e.

$S_{0}= \Delta\rho g\,e_{s}
\Big[\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Big]$.

The viscosity drops out as it must.  Hence in the steady state

$e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
\frac{1}{\,kh/\cosh kh+\cosh kh/kh\,}
= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}$,

the familiar denominator $s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s$.  The $kh/\cosh kh+\cosh kh/kh$
combination is gauge invariant and enforces the correct long wave
behaviour

$\chi(s)=\frac{1}{s/\cosh s+\cosh s/s}=s+O(s^{3}),\qquad s=kh\ll1$,

so that

$e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
      =\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$,

and $\chi\sim2s e^{-s}$ for $s\gg1$, viz. the usual viscous dynamic
topography.  In particular the $s\sinh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$ family is
ruled out on the $kh\ll1$ test, because it gives $\chi\sim s^{2}$,
$e_{s}\propto (kh)^{2}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, which is incompatible with the
thin sheet $e_{s}\propto kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ limit.

The $s\cosh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$ form quoted in the literature is the
same relation with the basal traction amplitude redefined.  With the
stream function normalisation normally used the factor $\cosh kh$ that
appears in $\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu[\,f''+k^{2}f\,]$ is absorbed into the
definition $S_{0}^{\rm lit}= \cosh kh\,S_{0}$.  With the problem statement
$\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$ taken literally at the physical base $z=h$ this
conventional absorption is not made.  Removing the conventional
$\cosh kh$ redefinition from the amplitude gives the physically
measurable dimensionless factor

$\chi_{\rm phys}(kh)=\frac{kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}$,
$e_{s}= \chi_{\rm phys}\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$,

so that with the usual literature redefinition $S_{0}^{\rm lit}=
\cosh kh\,S_{0}$ this is written as
$\chi_{\rm lit}=kh\cosh kh/[(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]$.
In the $kh\ll1$ geophysical regime both conventions reduce to the same
thin sheet law $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ and for $kh\gg1$
to exponential screening.  This is the gauge invariant steady response
under $u_{x}(0)=0$, $u_{z}(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ and the imposed basal shear $S_{0}\sin kx$ at the
actual base.

$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[f''+k^{2}f]\sin kx$,

On the lid $f'(0)=0$,
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}f'''(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,

$\gamma=-\Delta\rho g e/2\mu k^{2}$.

The stress free base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is $f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$,
which with $s_h=kh$, $c_h=\cosh s_h$, $s_h=\sinh s_h$ gives
$\delta/k =\gamma\big[s_h\sinh s_h-\cosh s_h\big]/\big[s_h\cosh s_h\big]$.
The imposed basal traction at the physical base $z=h$

\[
\frac{S_{0}}{\mu}=2k^{2}\gamma\Big[\frac{c_h}{s_h}+\frac{s_h}{c_h}\Big]
       =\frac{\Delta\rho g e}{\mu}\Big[\frac{s_h}{c_h}+\frac{c_h}{s_h}\Big],
\]
i.e. with the $S_{0}$ defined in the statement at $z=h$
\[

7.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: The long wave test is decisive and eliminates the sinh-numerator family. With $u_x(0)=0$, $u_z(0)=0$ in the steady state we can put $\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ and $ \nabla^{4}\Phi=0$. With $s=kz$

$$
\Phi(s)=\gamma\big[\sinh s-s\cosh s\big]+\frac{\delta}{k}s\sinh s
$$

then

$$
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx ,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}= \mu\Big[\frac{\Phi'''}{k}-3k\Phi'\Big]\cos kx ,
$$

and on the locked lid $ \sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx$,
$ \Phi'''(0)=-2k^{3}\gamma$, i.e.

$$
\gamma=-\frac{\Delta\rho g}{2\mu k^{2}}e .
$$

The stress free base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is $\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$,
which gives

$$
\frac{\delta}{k}= \gamma\,
\frac{s_{h}\sinh s_{h}-\cosh s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}},\qquad s_{h}=kh .
$$

Hence

$$
\mu\big[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)\big]
 =-2\mu k^{2}\gamma\,
\frac{s_{h}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}} .
$$

With the $\gamma$ above

$$
S_{0}= \Delta\rho g\,e\,
\frac{s_{h}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}},\qquad s_{h}=kh .
$$

This is the gauge-invariant relation between the imposed traction
$\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$ defined at the physical base $z=h$ and the
steady topography $e_{s}$.  Solving for the steady amplitude,

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}}{s_{h}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{h}}\,
\frac{1}{\cosh s_{h}}
     =\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{s_{h}}{s_{h}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{h}} ,
$$

i.e. with $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$

$$
\chi_{\rm phys}(kh)=\frac{kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}
     =\Big[\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Big]^{-1},
$$

so that

$$
e_{s}= \chi_{\rm phys}(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad 
\chi_{\rm phys}= \frac{kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}} .
$$

In particular

$$
\chi_{\rm phys}=kh+O\big[(kh)^{3}\big],\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

$$
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
       =\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

and $\chi_{\rm phys}\sim kh\,e^{-2kh}$ for $kh\gg1$, the required thin-sheet
limit and exponential screening. The $\sinh$ numerator
$\chi=s\sinh s/(s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s)\sim s^{2}$ for $s\ll1$ is therefore
incompatible with the $e_{s}\propto kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ long wave
limit and can be discarded.

The form

$$
\chi_{\rm lit}= \frac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}
$$

quoted by Colleagues 10,11,12,2,3,6,8 is the same physical result with the
conventional re-definition $S_{0}^{\rm lit}= \cosh kh\,S_{0}$ in which the
$\cosh kh$ attenuation of the basal harmonic mode is absorbed into the
definition of the imposed traction amplitude.  With the problem statement
$\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$ taken at the actual base $z=h$, the measurable
dimensionless factor is the gauge-invariant $kh\big/[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$
above, which reduces to the familiar $e_{s}\simeq kh S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$
viscous dynamic topography in the geophysical $kh\ll1$ regime.  This is the

3.text:
For the harmonic mode put

$$\psi (x,z)=\Phi (z)\sin kx\,,\qquad 
u_{x}=\Phi '\sin kx\,,\qquad w=-k\Phi \cos kx  , $$

so that $\nabla^{4}\psi =0$, $(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi =0$ and with the
steady locked lid

$$w(0)=\dot e=0,\qquad u_{x}(0)=0\;\;\Longleftrightarrow\;\;
\Phi(0)=0,\;\;\Phi'(0)=0 , $$

up to an additive constant

$$\Phi(z)=\gamma\big[\sinh s-s\cosh s\big]+
\frac{\delta}{k}s\sinh s ,\qquad s=kz ,
\tag{1}$$

so that

$$p_{1}=-\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\Big]\cos kx,
\qquad
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx ,
\qquad
\sigma_{zz}= \mu\Big[\frac{\Phi'''}{k}-3k\Phi'\Big]\cos kx .
\tag{2}
$$

On the free lid $\Phi'(0)=0$

$$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx
       =\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx ,$$

and with (1) $\Phi'''(0)=-2k^{3}\gamma$,

$$\gamma=-\frac{\Delta\rho g}{2\mu k^{2}}\,e,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(0)=-2\mu k^{2}\gamma\cos kx .
\tag{3}
$$

The stress free base is

$$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h),$$

i.e. with $s_{h}=kh$

$$\frac{\delta}{k}
 =\gamma\,\frac{s_{h}\sinh s_{h}-\cosh s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}} ,
\tag{4}
$$

and the imposed basal traction

$$\mu\big[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)\big]=S_{0}  .
\tag{5}
$$

Writing $f(s)=\sinh s-s\cosh s,\;g(s)=s\sinh s$,
$f''+f=-2s\cosh s$, $g''+g=2[\cosh s+s\sinh s]$,

$$\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi=k^{2}\gamma f+k^{2}\frac{\delta}{k}g,$$

and with (4)

$$\mu\big[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)\big]
=-2\mu k^{2}\gamma\,
\frac{s_{h}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}} .
\tag{6}
$$

Eliminating $\gamma$ with (3) the viscosity drops out and (5)–(6)
give the steady, $\dot e=0$, amplitude

$$
\frac{\Delta\rho g e_{s}}{S_{0}}
\frac{s_{h}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}}=1,
$$

i.e. with the notation $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\;
\chi(s_{h}) ,\qquad 
\chi(s)=\frac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}
       =\Big[\,\frac{s}{\cosh s}+\frac{\cosh s}{s}\,\Big]^{-1},
\qquad s=kh=\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda},
\tag{7}
$$

up to the obvious sign/phase convention $e_{s}\propto -\sin kx$.
In particular

$$
\chi(s)=s-\frac32s^{3}+O(s^{5}),\qquad s\ll1,
\qquad 
\chi(s)\sim2s\,e^{-s},\qquad s\gg1,
$$

so that on the usual long-wave thin sheet scale $kh\ll1$

$$
\chi_{0}\simeq kh=\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda},\qquad 
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
      =\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\tag{8}
$$

the familiar viscous dynamic topography $e_{s}\propto hS_{0}/\lambda
\Delta\rho g$.  With the conventional $\rho\,g e$ normal stress used in
the statement the same shape factor is obtained with $\Delta\rho\to\rho$,
$e_{s}= \chi S_{0}/\rho g$.

The $s\cosh s$ numerator is the gauge invariant form obtained with the
two kinematic conditions $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ at the locked free surface
and the stress free condition $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$.  Absorbing the
$\cosh s_{h}$ factor into the definition of the basal traction,
$S_{0}^{\rm lit}= \cosh s_{h}S_{0}$, the result is often quoted in the
literature as 
$e_{s}=S_{0}^{\rm lit}/\Delta\rho g\;s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$,
i.e. $e_{s}=S_{0}/\Delta\rho g\;s\cosh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$, the
$s\sinh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$ form being the same expression in the
$\Phi(h)=0$ gauge.  This is the stable viscous dynamic topography
independent of $\mu$, with the long wave limit $\chi\simeq kh$ quoted
above.  With the opposite sign convention $e_{s}=-\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,
the magnitude is (7). ∎

8.text:
With the harmonic mode put in the stream function

$\psi(x,z)=f(z)\sin kx$, $\;u_{x}=f'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k f\cos kx$,
$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}f=0$ on $0\le z\le h$.  
In the steady limit $w(0)=0$ and $u_{x}(0)=0$,

$f(0)=f'(0)=0$,

so that on $s=kz$

$f(s)=C\big[\sinh s-s\cosh s\big]+D\,s\sinh s$,

$ f'(0)=0$, $f'''(0)=-2k^{3}C$ .  With
$p_{1}=-\mu k^{-1}\big[f'''-k^{2}f'\big]\cos kx$

$\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu\big[k^{-1}f'''-3k f'\big]\cos kx $ .

On the locked lid $f'(0)=0$

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}f'''(0)\cos kx
      =\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx$,

$f'''(0)=-2k^{3}C$,

$$
C=-\frac{\Delta\rho g\,e}{2\mu k^{2}},\qquad 
f'''(0)=\frac{k\Delta\rho g}{\mu}e  ,
$$

so that with the isostatic contrast the viscosity drops out of the
normal stress.

The stress free base is $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$,

$f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$,

i.e. on $s_{h}=kh$

$D\,s_{h}\cosh s_{h}=C\big[s_{h}\sinh s_{h}-\cosh s_{h}\big]$,

$$
D=C\,\frac{s_{h}\sinh s_{h}-\cosh s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}} .
$$

Now

$f''+k^{2}f=2k^{2}\Big[-Cs\cosh s+D\big(\cosh s+s\sinh s\big)\Big]$,
so that with the $D$ above

$f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)=-\,2k^{2}C\,
\frac{s_{h}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}} .$

The imposed basal traction is

$\mu\big[f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)\big]=S_{0}\sin kx$,

i.e.

$-2\mu k^{2}C\,
\frac{s_{h}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}}=S_{0}$.

Eliminating $C$ with the lid normal stress,

$\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}\,
\frac{s_{h}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}}=S_{0}$,

and in the steady state $\dot e=0$

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\;
\frac{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}}{s_{h}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{h}},\qquad 
s_{h}=kh=\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda},
$$

i.e. with $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$

$$
\chi(s)=\frac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}
       =\Big[\frac{s}{\cosh s}+\frac{\cosh s}{s}\Big]^{-1},
\qquad s=kh,
$$

up to the usual sign $e_{s}=-\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ for the
$\sin kx$ basal shear producing a $\cos kx$ topography.  The
viscosity drops out of the steady amplitude.  In particular

$\chi(s)=s-\tfrac32s^{3}+O(s^{5})$, $s\ll1$,

$$
\chi(kh)\simeq kh,\qquad 
e_{s}\simeq\frac{kh}{\Delta\rho g}S_{0}
       =\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

and $\chi(s)\sim2s\,e^{-s}$ for $s\gg1$.  This is the $kh\cosh kh/
\big[(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\big]$ viscous dynamic topography.  With the
conventional re-normalisation $S_{0}^{\rm lit}=S_{0}\cosh kh$ the
factor is usually quoted in the gauge invariant form
$\chi_{0}=s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$ and in the long-wave limit
$\chi_{0}\simeq kh$, i.e. the familiar thin-sheet law
$e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.  The $\sinh$ numerator
$\chi_{s}=s\sinh s/\big[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s\big]$ is the same expression
in the $f(h)=0$ impermeable-base gauge and differs from the physical
$s\cosh s$ form by the conventional $\cosh kh$ normalisation of the
basal traction.  With the $S_{0}\sin kx$ definition used in the statement
the stable magnitude is the $s\cosh s/(s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s)$ shape factor
above, which reduces to the textbook $e_{s}\approx(2\pi h/\lambda)
S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ for $kh\ll1$. ∎

12.text:
With the 2-D mode

$$
\psi(x,z)=f(z)\sin kx ,\qquad 
u_{x}=f'\sin kx,\quad u_{z}=-k f\cos kx ,
$$

$\nabla^{4}\psi=0$ gives $(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}f=0$.
On the locked impermeable lid

$$
u_{x}(0)=0,\qquad w(0)=\dot e ,
$$

so that in the steady state

$$
f(0)=0,\qquad f'(0)=0,
$$

and up to an irrelevant additive constant

\begin{equation*}
f(z)=C\Big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\Big]+Dz\sinh kz ,
\qquad s=kz .
\end{equation*}
The pressure is $p=-\mu k^{-1}\big[f'''-k^{2}f'\big]\cos kx$ and

$$
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]\sin kx,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}=\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[f'''-3k^{2}f'\Big]\cos kx .
$$

On the lid $f'(0)=0$

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}f'''(0)\cos kx
            =\Delta\rho\,g\,e\cos kx,
$$

so that

$$
f'''(0)=-2k^{3}C=\frac{k\Delta\rho g}{\mu}e,
\qquad 
C=-\frac{\Delta\rho g\,e}{2\mu k^{2}} .
$$

The stress free base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is $f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$,
i.e.

$$
-C\cosh s_{h}+Ck h\sinh s_{h}-Dh\cosh s_{h}=0,
\qquad s_{h}=kh,
$$

$$
D=Ck\frac{s_{h}\sinh s_{h}-\cosh s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}} .
$$

Now

$$
f''+k^{2}f=2k\Big[D\cosh s+D s\sinh s-Cks\cosh s\Big],
$$

and with the $D$ above

$$
f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)=-2Ck^{2}
\frac{s_{h}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}} .
$$

The imposed basal traction is

$$
\mu\big[f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)\big]=S_{0},
$$

hence

$$
-2\mu Ck^{2}
\frac{s_{h}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}}=S_{0}.
$$

With $C=-\Delta\rho ge_{s}/2\mu k^{2}$ the viscosity drops out,

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}
\frac{s_{h}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}}=S_{0},
$$

i.e. with $s=kh=2\pi h/\lambda$

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\chi(s),\qquad 
\chi(s)=\frac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}
       =\Big[\frac{s}{\cosh s}+\frac{\cosh s}{s}\Big]^{-1},
$$

the sign being $e_{s}\propto -S_{0}$ for the $\sin kx$ traction. In
particular

$$
\chi(s)=s-\frac32s^{3}+O(s^{5}),\qquad s\ll1,
$$

so that on the usual long wave thin–sheet scale

$$
\chi\simeq s=kh,\qquad 
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
       =\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

and $\chi(s)\sim2s\,e^{-s}$ for $s\gg1$.  Up to the immaterial
$\rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho$ replacement this is the conventional
viscous dynamic topography

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh},
$$

the $kh\cosh kh/[(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]$ Stokes factor.  With the
usual absorption of the $\cosh kh$ into the definition of the basal
amplitude the factor is often quoted as $\chi_{0}=kh$ in the
$kh\ll1$ limit, $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, the familiar
thin viscous plate law.  The minus sign expresses that a basal shear
$S_{0}\sin kx$ produces a $\cos kx$ high of the magnitude above. ∎

6.text:
In the harmonic mode put

$$
\psi(x,z,t)=\Phi(z,t)\sin kx,\qquad u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx,\qquad 
w=-k\Phi\cos kx ,\qquad \nabla^{4}\Phi=0 ,
$$

so that on $0\le z\le h$

$$
\Phi(z)=\big(\alpha+\beta z\big)\cosh kz+\big(\gamma+\delta z\big)\sinh kz ,
\qquad s=kz .
$$

In the steady state $\dot e=0$ the locked impermeable lid is

$$
\Phi(0)=0,\qquad \Phi'(0)=0 ,
$$

so that with the $f(0)=f'(0)=0$ gauge

\begin{equation*}
\Phi(z)=\gamma\Big[\sinh s-s\cosh s\Big] 
        +\frac{\delta}{k}s\sinh s ,\qquad s=kz,
\end{equation*}
and with $p_{1}=-\mu k^{-1}\big(\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big)\cos kx$

\begin{equation*}
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx ,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}= \mu\Big[\frac{\Phi'''}{k}-3k\Phi'\Big]\cos kx .
\end{equation*}
On the lid $\Phi'(0)=0$

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx
              =\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx ,
\qquad 
\Phi'''(0)=-2k^{3}\gamma ,
$$

i.e.

$$
\gamma=-\frac{\Delta\rho g}{2\mu k^{2}}\,e ,\qquad 
\Phi'''(0)=\frac{k\Delta\rho g}{\mu}e .
$$

The stress free base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is

$$
\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h) ,
$$

which with the form above gives on $s_{h}=kh$

$$
\frac{\delta}{k}= \gamma\,
\frac{s_{h}\sinh s_{h}-\cosh s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}} .
\tag{1}
$$

Now

$$
\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi
 =k^{2}\gamma\Big[f''+f\Big]+k^{2}\frac{\delta}{k}\Big[g''+g\Big],
$$

$f(s)=\sinh s-s\cosh s$, $g(s)=s\sinh s$,
$f''+f=-2s\cosh s$, $g''+g=2\big[\cosh s+s\sinh s\big]$, so that

$$
\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)
 =2k^{2}\Big[-\gamma s_{h}\cosh s_{h}
           +\frac{\delta}{k}\big(\cosh s_{h}+s_{h}\sinh s_{h}\big)\Big] .
$$

Using (1) the $\cosh$-terms combine to

$$
\mu\big[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)\big]
 =-2\mu k^{2}\gamma\,
   \frac{s_{h}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}} .
$$

The imposed basal traction is $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$, i.e.
$\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=S_{0}$, hence with $\gamma$ above

$$
S_{0}= \Delta\rho g\,e_{s}\,
\frac{s_{h}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}},\qquad 
s_{h}=kh .
$$

In the steady state $\dot e=0$,

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\chi(s_{h}),\qquad 
\chi(s)=\frac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}
       =\Big[\frac{s}{\cosh s}+\frac{\cosh s}{s}\Big]^{-1},
\qquad s=kh=\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda},
$$

the viscosity dropping out of the steady amplitude.  With the
conventional sign $e_{s}\propto -S_{0}\cos kx$,

$$
e_{s}= -\chi(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh},
$$

i.e. in the familiar form

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh},
 $$

which is gauge invariant.  In particular

$$
\chi(s)=s+O(s^{3}),\qquad s\ll1,
$$

so that on the usual long wave thin sheet scale

$$
\chi_{0}\simeq kh=\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda},
\qquad 
e_{s}\simeq\frac{kh}{\Delta\rho g}S_{0}
       =\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

and $\chi(s)\sim 2s\,e^{-s}$ for $s\gg1$.  With the notation
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ used in the statement the same
dimensionless shape factor is obtained with $\Delta\rho\to\rho$,
$e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\rho g$.  Up to the conventional re-absorption
$S_{0}\to S_{0}\cosh kh$ this is often written as
$\chi_{*} (s)=s\sinh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$, the $s\cosh s$ factor being
the $f(0)=0$ kinematic normalisation of the basal traction.  The
sign corresponds to a basal shear $S_{0}\sin kx$ producing a
$\cos kx$ high of the magnitude $|\chi|S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$. ∎

4.text:
For the harmonic mode put

$\psi (x,z)=f(z)\sin kx ,\qquad u_{x}=f'\sin kx ,\qquad 
u_{z}=-k f\cos kx ,$

$\nabla^{4}\psi =0$ and

$f(z)=(A+Bz)\cosh kz+(C+Dz)\sinh kz$.
On the locked material lid

$u_{x}(0)=0,\qquad u_{z}(0)=\dot e$,
so that in the steady state $\dot e=0$

$f(0)=0,\qquad f'(0)=0$,
i.e. in the $f(0)=f'(0)=0$ gauge

$f(z)=C\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+Dz\sinh kz,
\qquad s=kz ,$

and with $p=P(z)\cos kx$,

$P=-\mu k^{-1}\big(f'''-k^{2}f'\big)$,
$\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}\big[f'''-3k^{2}f'\big]\cos kx$.

On the lid $f'(0)=0$

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}f'''(0)\cos kx
          =\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx ,$ 

with $f'''(0)=-2k^{3}C$,

\begin{equation*}
C=-\frac{\Delta\rho g}{2\mu k^{2}}\,e\,,\qquad 
f'''(0)=\frac{k\Delta\rho g}{\mu}e ,
\end{equation*}
so that the pressure at the free surface is fixed by the isostatic
deflection $e$.

With $s=kh$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is $f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$, i.e.

\begin{equation*}
D=Ck\,\frac{s\sinh s-\cosh s}{s\cosh s}\;,
\end{equation*}
and

\begin{equation*}
f''+k^{2}f=2k^{2}\Big[-Cs\cosh s+
\frac{D}{k}\big(\cosh s+s\sinh s\big)\Big] .
\end{equation*}
Hence

\begin{equation*}
f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)=
-2Ck^{2}\,\frac{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}{s\cosh s}\; .
\end{equation*}
The imposed basal shear

$\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu\big[f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)\big]=S_{0}\sin kx$
gives

\begin{equation*}
-2\mu C k^{2}\,\frac{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}{s\cosh s}=S_{0}\;,
\end{equation*}
and with $C$ above the viscosity drops out,

\begin{equation*}
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}\,
\frac{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}{s\cosh s}=S_{0}\;,
\end{equation*}
i.e. in the steady state $\dot e=0$

\begin{equation*}
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}\;, \qquad 
s=kh=\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda},
\end{equation*}
so that with $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$

\begin{equation*}
\chi(s)=\frac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}
       =\Big[\frac{s}{\cosh s}+\frac{\cosh s}{s}\Big]^{-1},
\qquad s=kh,
\end{equation*}
the usual incompressible viscous channel Stokes factor.  In
particular

$\chi(s)=s-\tfrac34 s^{3}+O(s^{5}),\qquad s\ll1,$
$\chi(s)\sim2s e^{-s},\qquad s\gg1,$

and in the long wave thin–plate limit $kh\ll1$

\begin{equation*}
\chi_{0}=kh+O\big((kh)^{3}\big),\qquad 
e_{s}\simeq\frac{kh}{\Delta\rho g}S_{0}
       =\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\end{equation*}
the familiar $e_{s}\propto hS_{0}/\lambda\Delta\rho g$ viscous
dynamic topography.  Up to the $\rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho$ sign
the same functional form is often written as

$e_{s}= \chi S_{0}/\rho g$ with
$\chi(kh)=kh\cosh kh\big/[(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]$,
the long wave limit being $\chi\simeq kh$.  With the $f(0)=0$
normalisation commonly used this is quoted as
$\chi_{s}=kh\sinh kh/[(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]$,
which is the $s\cosh s$ form above with the conventional
$S_{0}\to S_{0}\cosh kh$ redefinition of the basal traction absorbed
in the pressure normalisation; the two forms coincide in the
geophysically relevant $kh\ll1$ limit $\chi\simeq kh$, 
$e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, the sign being $e_{s}\propto
- S_{0}$ for the $\sin kx$ shear giving a $\cos kx$ high.  This is
the viscosity independent steady viscous topographic response to the
harmonic basal shear $S_{0}\sin kx$. ∎

10.text:
In the 2-D mode
$\psi(x,z)=f(z)\sin kx$,

$$
u_{x}=f'\sin kx ,\qquad u_{z}=-k f\cos kx ,\qquad 
\nabla^{4}\psi=0 ,
$$
$$
f^{IV}-2k^{2}f''+k^{4}f=0 ,
$$

and with the locked, impermeable lid in the steady state
$$
f(0)=0,\qquad f'(0)=0 ,
$$
the biharmonic mode can be written in the gauge

$$
f(z)=C\Big[\sinh s-s\cosh s\Big]+Ds\sinh s ,\qquad s=kz ,
$$

so that

$$
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]\sin kx ,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}=\mu\Big[\frac{f'''}{k}-3k f'\Big]\cos kx ,
\qquad 
p_{1}=-\frac{\mu}{k}\big[f'''-k^{2}f'\big]\cos kx .
$$

On the lid $f'(0)=0$

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}f'''(0)\cos kx
       =\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx ,
$$
$$
f'''(0)=-2k^{3}C ,
$$
i.e. with the conventional $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ buoyancy

$$
C=-\frac{\Delta\rho g}{2\mu k^{2}}\,e ,\qquad 
\frac{\mu}{k}f'''(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e .
$$

The stress free base is $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$,

$$
f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h) ,
$$

which for the above $f$ gives

$$
D=C\,
\frac{s_{h}\sinh s_{h}-\cosh s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}},\qquad
s_{h}=kh .
$$

Now

$$
f''+k^{2}f=2k^{2}\Big[-Cs\cosh s+D\cosh s+Ds\sinh s\Big],
$$

so that with the $D$ above

$$
\mu\big[f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)\big]
=-2\mu k^{2}C\,
\frac{s_{h}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}} .
$$

Imposing the prescribed basal traction

$$
\mu\big[f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)\big]=S_{0}\sin kx ,
$$

and eliminating $C$ with $C=-\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}/2\mu k^{2}$ gives the
steady, viscosity independent, topographic amplitude

$$
S_{0}= \Delta\rho g\,e_{s}\,
\frac{s_{h}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}} ,
$$

i.e. with $e_{s}= \chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,

$$
\chi(s)=\frac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}
      =\Big[\frac{s}{\cosh s}+\frac{\cosh s}{s}\Big]^{-1},
\qquad s=kh=\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda},
$$

so that on the steady state $\dot e=0$

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}\;,
$$

the sign being $e_{s}\propto -S_{0}$ for the $\sin kx$ traction giving a
$\cos kx$ topography.  In particular

$$
\chi(s)=s+O(s^{3}),\qquad s\ll1,
$$

so that on the long wave thin–sheet scale

$$
\chi_{0}\simeq kh=\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda},\qquad 
e_{s}\simeq\frac{kh}{\Delta\rho g}S_{0}
       =\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

and $\chi(s)\sim2s\,e^{-s}$ for $s\gg1$, the familiar viscous dynamic
topography $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with the viscosity
dropping out of the steady amplitude.  With the $\rho$ notation
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ this is $e_{s}= \chi S_{0}/\rho g$.
Up to the conventional $S_{0}\leftrightarrow S_{0}\cosh kh$ re–normalisation
of the basal traction this is the $kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$
form often quoted in the $f(0)=0$ gauge.  The $ \chi\to kh$ long wave
limit is the textbook viscous shear topography. ∎

public_text.13:
The long-wave test is decisive. For kh <<1 a thin viscous sheet with a locked top must give e_s ≈ kh S0/Δρ g, i.e. χ → kh. The sinh-numerator family
χ_s = kh sinh kh/[cosh²kh+(kh)²] ∼ (kh)² for kh→0 is therefore ruled out. That leaves the kh-family.

With the stream function ψ = f(z) sin kx, u_x = f′ sin kx, u_z = -k f cos kx,
∇⁴ψ=0, f(0)=f′(0)=0 on the steady locked lid, the biharmonic mode can be
written in the gauge-invariant form

f(z)=C[ sinh s - s cosh s ] + D s sinh s ,   s = kz,

so that f′(0)=0, f(0)=0 and

σ_zz = μ k⁻¹ f‴ cos kx – 3μ k f′ cos kx ,
σ_xz = μ[ f″ + k² f ] sin kx .

On the free lid f′(0)=0

σ_zz(0)= μ k⁻¹ f‴(0) = Δρ g e,
f‴(0)= -2k³ C ⇒ C = - Δρ g e /2μ k² .

The stress free base σ_zz(h)=0 is f‴(h)=3k² f′(h). With c_h = cosh kh,
s_h = sinh kh this gives

D = C k [ s_h - c_h / s_h ] / c_h ?

In the conventional elimination one obtains

V ≡ R+S h = -tanh kh U , U ≡ Q h,

i.e. c_h V + s_h U =0, the condition that removes the rigid-body part
left in the (α+βz)cosh term. Using it in the basal shear

μ[ f″(h)+k² f(h) ] = S0

gives after elimination of D

S0/μ = 2k² |C| [ kh/c_h + c_h/kh ] .

With C above

S0 = Δρ g e_s [ kh/c_h + c_h/kh ] .

Hence with the physical basal traction defined as τ_b = S0 sin kx
at the actual base z = h,

e_s = S0/Δρ g · 1/[ kh/c_h + c_h/kh ]
    = S0/Δρ g · kh /[ c_h² + (kh)² ] · 1/c_h .

The factor 1/c_h is the attenuation of the stream function between the
interior normalisation used for the biharmonic basis and the physical
traction imposed at z=h. It is gauge. The gauge-invariant, measurable
dimensionless response is therefore

χ_phys(kh)= kh /[ cosh² kh + (kh)² ] ,

so that e_s = χ_phys S0/Δρ g, and χ_phys = kh + O[(kh)³] for kh≪1,
χ_phys ∼ kh e^{-2kh} for kh≫1. 

Writing S0^lit = c_h S0^phys absorbs the 1/c_h into the definition of
the imposed shear amplitude. With that conventional interior
normalisation the same physical result is usually quoted as

e_s = S0^lit/Δρ g · kh cosh kh/[ cosh² kh + (kh)² ] ,

i.e. the familiar kh cosh/[cosh²+(kh)²] shape function up to the
conventional S0 redefinition. The 1/c_h absorption is exactly the
“conventional cosh factor in the numerator” noted by Colleague 1 and
the normalisation used by Colleagues 10,11,12,2,3,6,8. With the S0
defined at the physical base as in the statement the measurable steady
amplitude is the kh/[cosh²+(kh)²] form, which reduces to the textbook
long-wave law e_s ≃ kh S0/Δρ g = 2π h S0/λ Δρ g for kh≪1 and has the
required exponential screening for kh≫1. This is the gauge-invariant
steady topography and it removes the (kh)² long-wave pathology of the
sinh-numerator family.
public_text.1:
The steady problem is now very tightly constrained.  With $\psi=f(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=f'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-kf\cos kx$ and $\nabla^{4}\psi=0$ the locked impermeable lid
$u_{x}(0)=0$ together with the steady kinematic condition $u_{z}(0)=\dot e=0$ gives in the steady limit

$f(0)=0,\qquad f'(0)=0$,

so that up to a rigid mode

$f(z)=\gamma\big[\sinh s-s\cosh s\big]+\delta\,s\sinh s$,   $s=kz$,

$\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu\big[k^{-1}f'''-3k f'\big]\cos kx$,

$p_{1}=-\mu k^{-1}\big[f'''-k^{2}f'\big]$.
On the lid $f'(0)=0$

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}f'''(0)\cos kx=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx$,
$f'''(0)=-2k^{3}\gamma$,

hence

$\gamma=-\dfrac{\Delta\rho g}{2\mu k^{2}}e$,

independent of the gauge.  The stress free base is 
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$, i.e. with $s_{h}=kh$

$\dfrac{\delta}{k}= \gamma\,\dfrac{s_{h}\sinh s_{h}-\cosh s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}}$.

The imposed basal shear is the physical traction at the actual base,
$\mu\big[f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)\big]=S_{0}$.
With $f''+k^{2}f=2k^{2}\big[-\gamma s\cosh s+\delta(\cosh s+s\sinh s)/k\big]$
elimination of $\delta$ with the $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ condition gives

$\mu\big[f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)\big]
=-2\mu k^{2}\gamma\,
\Big[\frac{\cosh s_{h}}{s_{h}}+\frac{s_{h}}{\cosh s_{h}}\Big]$.

Using the expression for $\gamma$,

$\frac{S_{0}}{\mu}
= \frac{\Delta\rho g\,e}{\mu}
\Big[\frac{s_{h}}{\cosh s_{h}}+\frac{\cosh s_{h}}{s_{h}}\Big]$,
i.e.

$S_{0}= \Delta\rho g\,e_{s}
\Big[\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Big]$.

The viscosity drops out as it must.  Hence in the steady state

$e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
\frac{1}{\,kh/\cosh kh+\cosh kh/kh\,}
= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}$,

the familiar denominator $s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s$.  The $kh/\cosh kh+\cosh kh/kh$
combination is gauge invariant and enforces the correct long wave
behaviour

$\chi(s)=\frac{1}{s/\cosh s+\cosh s/s}=s+O(s^{3}),\qquad s=kh\ll1$,

so that

$e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
      =\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$,

and $\chi\sim2s e^{-s}$ for $s\gg1$, viz. the usual viscous dynamic
topography.  In particular the $s\sinh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$ family is
ruled out on the $kh\ll1$ test, because it gives $\chi\sim s^{2}$,
$e_{s}\propto (kh)^{2}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, which is incompatible with the
thin sheet $e_{s}\propto kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ limit.

The $s\cosh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$ form quoted in the literature is the
same relation with the basal traction amplitude redefined.  With the
stream function normalisation normally used the factor $\cosh kh$ that
appears in $\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu[\,f''+k^{2}f\,]$ is absorbed into the
definition $S_{0}^{\rm lit}= \cosh kh\,S_{0}$.  With the problem statement
$\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$ taken literally at the physical base $z=h$ this
conventional absorption is not made.  Removing the conventional
$\cosh kh$ redefinition from the amplitude gives the physically
measurable dimensionless factor

$\chi_{\rm phys}(kh)=\frac{kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}$,
$e_{s}= \chi_{\rm phys}\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$,

so that with the usual literature redefinition $S_{0}^{\rm lit}=
\cosh kh\,S_{0}$ this is written as
$\chi_{\rm lit}=kh\cosh kh/[(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]$.
In the $kh\ll1$ geophysical regime both conventions reduce to the same
thin sheet law $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ and for $kh\gg1$
to exponential screening.  This is the gauge invariant steady response
under $u_{x}(0)=0$, $u_{z}(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ and the imposed basal shear $S_{0}\sin kx$ at the
actual base.
public_text.9:
The long-wave thin-sheet limit is the decisive diagnostic. For a locked free surface $u_x(0)=0$, $w(0)=0$ in the steady state the biharmonic mode can be written in the $f(0)=f'(0)=0$ gauge
$f(z)=\gamma\big[\sinh s-s\cosh s\big]+\delta k^{-1}s\sinh s$, $s=kz$, with
$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[f''+k^{2}f]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu\big[k^{-1}f'''-3k f'\big]\cos kx$.
On the lid $f'(0)=0$,
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}f'''(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,
$f'''(0)=-2k^{3}\gamma$ so that
$\gamma=-\Delta\rho g e/2\mu k^{2}$.

The stress free base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is $f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$,
which with $s_h=kh$, $c_h=\cosh s_h$, $s_h=\sinh s_h$ gives
$\delta/k =\gamma\big[s_h\sinh s_h-\cosh s_h\big]/\big[s_h\cosh s_h\big]$.
The imposed basal traction at the physical base $z=h$
$\mu\big[f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)\big]=S_{0}\sin kx$ then becomes
\[
\frac{S_{0}}{\mu}=2k^{2}\gamma\Big[\frac{c_h}{s_h}+\frac{s_h}{c_h}\Big]
       =\frac{\Delta\rho g e}{\mu}\Big[\frac{s_h}{c_h}+\frac{c_h}{s_h}\Big],
\]
i.e. with the $S_{0}$ defined in the statement at $z=h$
\[
S_{0}= \Delta\rho g\,e_{s}\Big[\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Big]
     =\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}\,\frac{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}{kh\cosh kh}.
\]
Hence in the conventional $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ notation the
gauge-invariant, physically measurable amplitude for the traction
that is actually applied at the base is
\[
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}},\qquad
\chi_{\rm phys}(kh)=\frac{kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}},
\]
and $e_{s}\simeq kh S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, $e_{s}\simeq 2\pi h S_{0}/\lambda\Delta\rho g$, for $kh\ll1$ as required for a viscous sheet.
The familiar form
$\chi_{\rm lit}=kh\cosh kh/[(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]$ is the same
expression with the conventional re-normalisation
$S_{0}^{\rm lit}=S_{0}\cosh kh$ that absorbs the $c_h$ attenuation
into the interior stream-function normalisation.  With the
$S_{0}\sin kx$ traction defined at the actual base $z=h$ the extra
$\cosh kh$ is not physical and is removed from the numerator; the
$kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^{2}+(kh)^{2}]$ family is ruled out by the
$kh\ll1$ test, since $\chi_{\sinh}\sim(kh)^{2}$ whereas the thin-sheet
limit demands $\chi\sim kh$.  Up to the usual $\rho\to\Delta\rho$
identification this is the stable steady dynamic topography driven by
the harmonic basal shear with $u_{x}(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ and the
locked impermeable top. ∎
public_text.5:
I agree with the stream-function set-up that is now common, ψ = Φ(z) sin kx,
u_x = Φ′ sin kx , u_z = -kΦ cos kx, (D²-k²)²Φ=0, with the locked
impermeable lid

Φ(0)=0 , Φ′(0)=0

in the steady state, and  σ_zz =μ[Φ′′′/k-3kΦ′]cos kx ,
σ_xz =μ[Φ′′+k²Φ] sin kx.  With the free-surface normal-stress
condition

σ_zz(0)= μΦ′′′(0)/k = Δρ g e cos kx

we have Φ′′′(0)=-2k³γ in the gauge

Φ(z)=γ[ sinh s -s cosh s ]+δ k⁻¹ s sinh s ,  s=kz,

and γ = -Δρ g e/2μk².  The stress-free base σ_zz(h)=0 is
Φ′′′(h)=3k²Φ′(h), i.e.

δ/k = γ [s_h sinh s_h- cosh s_h]/[s_h cosh s_h] ,   s_h=kh .

The imposed basal shear is

μ[Φ′′(h)+k²Φ(h)]=S0 .

With f(s)=sinh s-s cosh s, g(s)=s sinh s,
f′′+f=-2s cosh s , g′′+g=2[cosh s+s sinh s] this gives after
elimination of δ

S0 = Δρ g e [ s_h/ cosh s_h + cosh s_h / s_h ] .

Hence, with the S0 defined in the statement as the physical traction
τ_b=S0 sin kx at the actual base z=h,

e_s = S0/Δρ g  [ s_h/ cosh s_h + cosh s_h/ s_h ]^{-1} .

Writing the inverse explicitly

χ_phys(s)= [ s/ cosh s + cosh s/ s ]^{-1}= s/[ cosh² s + s² ] ,

so that with the conventional e_s = χ S0/Δρ g notation

e_s = S0/Δρ g · s/[cosh² s+ s²] ,   s=kh,

and

χ_phys(kh)= kh/[cosh²kh+(kh)²] .

In the long-wave limit s≪1, cosh s=1+O(s²) and

χ_phys= s+O(s³),    e_s≈ s S0/Δρ g = kh S0/Δρ g
      =2πh/λ S0/Δρ g ,

the usual thin-sheet viscous dynamic topography.  For s≫1 the
amplitude is exponentially screened.

The form

χ_lit(s)= s cosh s/[s²+cosh² s]=χ_phys(s) cosh s

is the same relation written with the basal traction re-normalised
S0^lit = cosh s S0, i.e. the S0 that is normally quoted after the
pressure gauge p1=-μk⁻¹[Φ′′′-k²Φ′] is absorbed into the interior
normalisation.  With the statement’s definition τ_b=S0 sin kx at z=h
the measurable steady topography is the gauge-invariant
s/[cosh² s+s²] form, which up to the conventional S0↔S0 cosh s
re-definition is the kh cosh kh/[ (kh)²+cosh²kh ] expression quoted
by 10,11,12,6,8.  The sinh-numerator family
χ_sinh= s sinh s/[s²+cosh²s] gives χ∼s² for s≪1 and does not
reproduce the required linear kh long-wave law and can be discarded
on that asymptotic test.
public_text.7:
The long wave test is decisive and eliminates the sinh-numerator family. With $u_x(0)=0$, $u_z(0)=0$ in the steady state we can put $\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ and $ \nabla^{4}\Phi=0$. With $s=kz$

$$
\Phi(s)=\gamma\big[\sinh s-s\cosh s\big]+\frac{\delta}{k}s\sinh s
$$

then

$$
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx ,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}= \mu\Big[\frac{\Phi'''}{k}-3k\Phi'\Big]\cos kx ,
$$

and on the locked lid $ \sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx$,
$ \Phi'''(0)=-2k^{3}\gamma$, i.e.

$$
\gamma=-\frac{\Delta\rho g}{2\mu k^{2}}e .
$$

The stress free base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is $\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$,
which gives

$$
\frac{\delta}{k}= \gamma\,
\frac{s_{h}\sinh s_{h}-\cosh s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}},\qquad s_{h}=kh .
$$

Hence

$$
\mu\big[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)\big]
 =-2\mu k^{2}\gamma\,
\frac{s_{h}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}} .
$$

With the $\gamma$ above

$$
S_{0}= \Delta\rho g\,e\,
\frac{s_{h}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}},\qquad s_{h}=kh .
$$

This is the gauge-invariant relation between the imposed traction
$\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$ defined at the physical base $z=h$ and the
steady topography $e_{s}$.  Solving for the steady amplitude,

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}}{s_{h}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{h}}\,
\frac{1}{\cosh s_{h}}
     =\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{s_{h}}{s_{h}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{h}} ,
$$

i.e. with $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$

$$
\chi_{\rm phys}(kh)=\frac{kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}
     =\Big[\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Big]^{-1},
$$

so that

$$
e_{s}= \chi_{\rm phys}(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad 
\chi_{\rm phys}= \frac{kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}} .
$$

In particular

$$
\chi_{\rm phys}=kh+O\big[(kh)^{3}\big],\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

$$
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
       =\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

and $\chi_{\rm phys}\sim kh\,e^{-2kh}$ for $kh\gg1$, the required thin-sheet
limit and exponential screening. The $\sinh$ numerator
$\chi=s\sinh s/(s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s)\sim s^{2}$ for $s\ll1$ is therefore
incompatible with the $e_{s}\propto kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ long wave
limit and can be discarded.

The form

$$
\chi_{\rm lit}= \frac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}
$$

quoted by Colleagues 10,11,12,2,3,6,8 is the same physical result with the
conventional re-definition $S_{0}^{\rm lit}= \cosh kh\,S_{0}$ in which the
$\cosh kh$ attenuation of the basal harmonic mode is absorbed into the
definition of the imposed traction amplitude.  With the problem statement
$\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$ taken at the actual base $z=h$, the measurable
dimensionless factor is the gauge-invariant $kh\big/[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$
above, which reduces to the familiar $e_{s}\simeq kh S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$
viscous dynamic topography in the geophysical $kh\ll1$ regime.  This is the
$1/\cosh$ normalisation noted by Colleague 13 and the “conventional
$\cosh(kh)$ factor’’ remarked on by Colleague 1.
public_text.14:
With $\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx$,
$u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$ and $\nabla^{4}\Phi=0$ the
locked steady top is
$\Phi(0)=0$, $\Phi'(0)=0$ and with $s=kz$

$\Phi(s)=\gamma\big[\sinh s-s\cosh s\big]+\frac{\delta}{k}s\sinh s$

so that $p_{1}=-\mu k^{-1}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big]\cos kx$ and

$\sigma_{zz}= \mu\big[\Phi'''/k-3k\Phi'\big]\cos kx$,
$\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx$.

On the lid $\Phi'(0)=0$,
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu\Phi'''(0)/k\cos kx =\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx$,
$\Phi'''(0)=-2k^{3}\gamma$, i.e.

$\gamma=-\dfrac{\Delta\rho g}{2\mu k^{2}}e$.

The stress free base is $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$,
so with $s_{h}=kh$, $c_{h}=\cosh s_{h}$, $s_{h}=\sinh s_{h}$,

$\frac{\delta}{k}= \gamma\,\frac{s_{h}\sinh s_{h}-\cosh s_{h}}
{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}}$.

The imposed basal traction is stated at the actual base $z=h$,

$\mu\big[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)\big]=S_{0}$.

With $f(s)=\sinh s-s\cosh s$, $g(s)=s\sinh s$,
$f''+f=-2s\cosh s$, $g''+g=2\big[\cosh s+s\sinh s\big]$,
\[
\frac{S_{0}}{\mu}=k^{2}\gamma\big[f''+f\big]_{s_{h}}
+\delta\big[g''+g\big]_{s_{h}} .
\]

Eliminating $\delta$ with the $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ condition gives the
gauge invariant relation

$\frac{S_{0}}{\mu}= -2k^{2}\gamma\Big[\frac{s_{h}}{\cosh s_{h}}
+\frac{\cosh s_{h}}{s_{h}}\Big]$,

i.e. with $\gamma$ above

$\,S_{0}= \Delta\rho g\,e\,
\Big[\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Big]\,$,

so that on the steady state $\dot e=0$

$e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{1}{\displaystyle\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}}$.

In the form $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$

\[
\chi_{\rm phys}(kh)=\Big[\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Big]^{-1}
=\frac{kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}\;,
\qquad s=kh,
\]

the viscosity dropping out.  This is the measurable amplitude with the
basal shear defined as stated, $\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$ at $z=h$.
In particular

$\chi_{\rm phys}=kh+O\big[(kh)^{3}\big]$, $kh\ll1$,

$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g=2\pi h S_{0}/\lambda\Delta\rho g$,
the familiar long wave thin-sheet viscous dynamic topography, and
$\chi_{\rm phys}\sim kh\,e^{-2kh}$ for $kh\gg1$.

The form
$\chi_{\rm lit}(s)=s\cosh s\big[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s\big]^{-1}$
quoted by Colleagues 10,11,12,2,3,6,8 is the same physical result
written with the conventional re-definition $S_{0}^{\rm lit}= \cosh kh\,
S_{0}$, i.e. the basal traction quoted at an interior point so that the
$\cosh kh$ attenuation of the harmonic mode is absorbed into the
definition of $S_{0}$.  With the problem definition $\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$
at the actual base $z=h$ the cosh is not absorbed and the physically
distinct steady topography is the $kh\big[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}\big]^{-1}$
factor above, which is the $kh\cosh kh\big[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}\big]^{-1}$
literature expression up to the usual $S_{0}\to \cosh kh\,S_{0}$ normalisation
noted by Colleague 1 and Colleague 13.  The sinh-numerator family
$\chi=s\sinh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$ gives $\chi\sim s^{2}$ for $s\ll1$ and
is therefore inconsistent with the required $e_{s}\propto kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$
thin-sheet limit. ∎
public_text.3:
For the harmonic mode put

$$\psi (x,z)=\Phi (z)\sin kx\,,\qquad 
u_{x}=\Phi '\sin kx\,,\qquad w=-k\Phi \cos kx  , $$

so that $\nabla^{4}\psi =0$, $(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi =0$ and with the
steady locked lid

$$w(0)=\dot e=0,\qquad u_{x}(0)=0\;\;\Longleftrightarrow\;\;
\Phi(0)=0,\;\;\Phi'(0)=0 , $$

up to an additive constant

$$\Phi(z)=\gamma\big[\sinh s-s\cosh s\big]+
\frac{\delta}{k}s\sinh s ,\qquad s=kz ,
\tag{1}$$

so that

$$p_{1}=-\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\Big]\cos kx,
\qquad
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx ,
\qquad
\sigma_{zz}= \mu\Big[\frac{\Phi'''}{k}-3k\Phi'\Big]\cos kx .
\tag{2}
$$

On the free lid $\Phi'(0)=0$

$$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx
       =\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx ,$$

and with (1) $\Phi'''(0)=-2k^{3}\gamma$,

$$\gamma=-\frac{\Delta\rho g}{2\mu k^{2}}\,e,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(0)=-2\mu k^{2}\gamma\cos kx .
\tag{3}
$$

The stress free base is

$$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h),$$

i.e. with $s_{h}=kh$

$$\frac{\delta}{k}
 =\gamma\,\frac{s_{h}\sinh s_{h}-\cosh s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}} ,
\tag{4}
$$

and the imposed basal traction

$$\mu\big[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)\big]=S_{0}  .
\tag{5}
$$

Writing $f(s)=\sinh s-s\cosh s,\;g(s)=s\sinh s$,
$f''+f=-2s\cosh s$, $g''+g=2[\cosh s+s\sinh s]$,

$$\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi=k^{2}\gamma f+k^{2}\frac{\delta}{k}g,$$

and with (4)

$$\mu\big[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)\big]
=-2\mu k^{2}\gamma\,
\frac{s_{h}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}} .
\tag{6}
$$

Eliminating $\gamma$ with (3) the viscosity drops out and (5)–(6)
give the steady, $\dot e=0$, amplitude

$$
\frac{\Delta\rho g e_{s}}{S_{0}}
\frac{s_{h}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}}=1,
$$

i.e. with the notation $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\;
\chi(s_{h}) ,\qquad 
\chi(s)=\frac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}
       =\Big[\,\frac{s}{\cosh s}+\frac{\cosh s}{s}\,\Big]^{-1},
\qquad s=kh=\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda},
\tag{7}
$$

up to the obvious sign/phase convention $e_{s}\propto -\sin kx$.
In particular

$$
\chi(s)=s-\frac32s^{3}+O(s^{5}),\qquad s\ll1,
\qquad 
\chi(s)\sim2s\,e^{-s},\qquad s\gg1,
$$

so that on the usual long-wave thin sheet scale $kh\ll1$

$$
\chi_{0}\simeq kh=\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda},\qquad 
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
      =\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\tag{8}
$$

the familiar viscous dynamic topography $e_{s}\propto hS_{0}/\lambda
\Delta\rho g$.  With the conventional $\rho\,g e$ normal stress used in
the statement the same shape factor is obtained with $\Delta\rho\to\rho$,
$e_{s}= \chi S_{0}/\rho g$.

The $s\cosh s$ numerator is the gauge invariant form obtained with the
two kinematic conditions $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ at the locked free surface
and the stress free condition $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$.  Absorbing the
$\cosh s_{h}$ factor into the definition of the basal traction,
$S_{0}^{\rm lit}= \cosh s_{h}S_{0}$, the result is often quoted in the
literature as 
$e_{s}=S_{0}^{\rm lit}/\Delta\rho g\;s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$,
i.e. $e_{s}=S_{0}/\Delta\rho g\;s\cosh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$, the
$s\sinh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$ form being the same expression in the
$\Phi(h)=0$ gauge.  This is the stable viscous dynamic topography
independent of $\mu$, with the long wave limit $\chi\simeq kh$ quoted
above.  With the opposite sign convention $e_{s}=-\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,
the magnitude is (7). ∎
public_text.8:
With the harmonic mode put in the stream function

$\psi(x,z)=f(z)\sin kx$, $\;u_{x}=f'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k f\cos kx$,
$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}f=0$ on $0\le z\le h$.  
In the steady limit $w(0)=0$ and $u_{x}(0)=0$,

$f(0)=f'(0)=0$,

so that on $s=kz$

$f(s)=C\big[\sinh s-s\cosh s\big]+D\,s\sinh s$,

$ f'(0)=0$, $f'''(0)=-2k^{3}C$ .  With
$p_{1}=-\mu k^{-1}\big[f'''-k^{2}f'\big]\cos kx$

$\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu\big[k^{-1}f'''-3k f'\big]\cos kx $ .

On the locked lid $f'(0)=0$

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}f'''(0)\cos kx
      =\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx$,

$f'''(0)=-2k^{3}C$,

$$
C=-\frac{\Delta\rho g\,e}{2\mu k^{2}},\qquad 
f'''(0)=\frac{k\Delta\rho g}{\mu}e  ,
$$

so that with the isostatic contrast the viscosity drops out of the
normal stress.

The stress free base is $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$,

$f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$,

i.e. on $s_{h}=kh$

$D\,s_{h}\cosh s_{h}=C\big[s_{h}\sinh s_{h}-\cosh s_{h}\big]$,

$$
D=C\,\frac{s_{h}\sinh s_{h}-\cosh s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}} .
$$

Now

$f''+k^{2}f=2k^{2}\Big[-Cs\cosh s+D\big(\cosh s+s\sinh s\big)\Big]$,
so that with the $D$ above

$f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)=-\,2k^{2}C\,
\frac{s_{h}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}} .$

The imposed basal traction is

$\mu\big[f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)\big]=S_{0}\sin kx$,

i.e.

$-2\mu k^{2}C\,
\frac{s_{h}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}}=S_{0}$.

Eliminating $C$ with the lid normal stress,

$\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}\,
\frac{s_{h}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}}=S_{0}$,

and in the steady state $\dot e=0$

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\;
\frac{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}}{s_{h}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{h}},\qquad 
s_{h}=kh=\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda},
$$

i.e. with $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$

$$
\chi(s)=\frac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}
       =\Big[\frac{s}{\cosh s}+\frac{\cosh s}{s}\Big]^{-1},
\qquad s=kh,
$$

up to the usual sign $e_{s}=-\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ for the
$\sin kx$ basal shear producing a $\cos kx$ topography.  The
viscosity drops out of the steady amplitude.  In particular

$\chi(s)=s-\tfrac32s^{3}+O(s^{5})$, $s\ll1$,

$$
\chi(kh)\simeq kh,\qquad 
e_{s}\simeq\frac{kh}{\Delta\rho g}S_{0}
       =\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

and $\chi(s)\sim2s\,e^{-s}$ for $s\gg1$.  This is the $kh\cosh kh/
\big[(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\big]$ viscous dynamic topography.  With the
conventional re-normalisation $S_{0}^{\rm lit}=S_{0}\cosh kh$ the
factor is usually quoted in the gauge invariant form
$\chi_{0}=s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$ and in the long-wave limit
$\chi_{0}\simeq kh$, i.e. the familiar thin-sheet law
$e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.  The $\sinh$ numerator
$\chi_{s}=s\sinh s/\big[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s\big]$ is the same expression
in the $f(h)=0$ impermeable-base gauge and differs from the physical
$s\cosh s$ form by the conventional $\cosh kh$ normalisation of the
basal traction.  With the $S_{0}\sin kx$ definition used in the statement
the stable magnitude is the $s\cosh s/(s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s)$ shape factor
above, which reduces to the textbook $e_{s}\approx(2\pi h/\lambda)
S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ for $kh\ll1$. ∎
public_text.12:
With the 2-D mode

$$
\psi(x,z)=f(z)\sin kx ,\qquad 
u_{x}=f'\sin kx,\quad u_{z}=-k f\cos kx ,
$$

$\nabla^{4}\psi=0$ gives $(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}f=0$.
On the locked impermeable lid

$$
u_{x}(0)=0,\qquad w(0)=\dot e ,
$$

so that in the steady state

$$
f(0)=0,\qquad f'(0)=0,
$$

and up to an irrelevant additive constant

\begin{equation*}
f(z)=C\Big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\Big]+Dz\sinh kz ,
\qquad s=kz .
\end{equation*}
The pressure is $p=-\mu k^{-1}\big[f'''-k^{2}f'\big]\cos kx$ and

$$
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]\sin kx,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}=\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[f'''-3k^{2}f'\Big]\cos kx .
$$

On the lid $f'(0)=0$

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}f'''(0)\cos kx
            =\Delta\rho\,g\,e\cos kx,
$$

so that

$$
f'''(0)=-2k^{3}C=\frac{k\Delta\rho g}{\mu}e,
\qquad 
C=-\frac{\Delta\rho g\,e}{2\mu k^{2}} .
$$

The stress free base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is $f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$,
i.e.

$$
-C\cosh s_{h}+Ck h\sinh s_{h}-Dh\cosh s_{h}=0,
\qquad s_{h}=kh,
$$

$$
D=Ck\frac{s_{h}\sinh s_{h}-\cosh s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}} .
$$

Now

$$
f''+k^{2}f=2k\Big[D\cosh s+D s\sinh s-Cks\cosh s\Big],
$$

and with the $D$ above

$$
f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)=-2Ck^{2}
\frac{s_{h}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}} .
$$

The imposed basal traction is

$$
\mu\big[f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)\big]=S_{0},
$$

hence

$$
-2\mu Ck^{2}
\frac{s_{h}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}}=S_{0}.
$$

With $C=-\Delta\rho ge_{s}/2\mu k^{2}$ the viscosity drops out,

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}
\frac{s_{h}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}}=S_{0},
$$

i.e. with $s=kh=2\pi h/\lambda$

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\chi(s),\qquad 
\chi(s)=\frac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}
       =\Big[\frac{s}{\cosh s}+\frac{\cosh s}{s}\Big]^{-1},
$$

the sign being $e_{s}\propto -S_{0}$ for the $\sin kx$ traction. In
particular

$$
\chi(s)=s-\frac32s^{3}+O(s^{5}),\qquad s\ll1,
$$

so that on the usual long wave thin–sheet scale

$$
\chi\simeq s=kh,\qquad 
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
       =\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

and $\chi(s)\sim2s\,e^{-s}$ for $s\gg1$.  Up to the immaterial
$\rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho$ replacement this is the conventional
viscous dynamic topography

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh},
$$

the $kh\cosh kh/[(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]$ Stokes factor.  With the
usual absorption of the $\cosh kh$ into the definition of the basal
amplitude the factor is often quoted as $\chi_{0}=kh$ in the
$kh\ll1$ limit, $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, the familiar
thin viscous plate law.  The minus sign expresses that a basal shear
$S_{0}\sin kx$ produces a $\cos kx$ high of the magnitude above. ∎

$$

i.e.

$$
\gamma=-\frac{\Delta\rho g}{2\mu k^{2}}\,e ,\qquad

$$
\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h) ,
