The biharmonic derivation is now essentially closed. With $\psi=f(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=f'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k f\cos kx$, $\nabla^4\psi=0$ and the steady locked impermeable lid $f(0)=f'(0)=0$ the mode can be written in the $f(0)=f'(0)=0$ gauge

$f(z)=\gamma\big[\sinh s-s\cosh s\big]+\delta\,s\sinh s$,  $s=kz$,

$\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]\sin kx$,

$\sigma_{zz}= \mu\big[k^{-1}f'''-3k f'\big]\cos kx$,

$p_{1}=-\mu k^{-1}\big[f'''-k^{2}f'\big]\cos kx$.

On the lid

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}f'''(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx$,

$f'''(0)=-2k^{3}\gamma$,

$\gamma=-\Delta\rho g\,e/2\mu k^{2}$.

The stress free base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is $f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$,
$s_{h}=kh$,

$\displaystyle
\delta =k\gamma\frac{s_{h}\sinh s_{h}-\cosh s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}}$.

Hence

$\mu\big[f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)\big]
=-2\mu k^{2}\gamma\,
\frac{s_{h}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}}$.

With the conventional interior normalisation this is often written as

$S_{0}^{\rm int}= \Delta\rho g\,e_{s}
\Big[\frac{s_{h}}{\cosh s_{h}}+\frac{\cosh s_{h}}{s_{h}}\Big]
 =\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}\,
\frac{s_{h}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}}$,

i.e.

$e_{s}=S_{0}^{\rm int}/\Delta\rho g\,
\Big[\frac{s_{h}}{\cosh s_{h}}+\frac{\cosh s_{h}}{s_{h}}\Big]^{-1}
= S_{0}^{\rm int}/\Delta\rho g\,
\frac{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}}{s_{h}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{h}}$.

The denominator $s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s$ and the long wave limit
$\chi=s+O(s^{3})$, $s=kh\ll1$, are therefore robust. The remaining
difference is the gauge of the basal amplitude. The stream function
mode is attenuated between the interior normalisation and the physical
traction imposed at the actual base $z=h$. With the statement
$\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$ taken literally at $z=h$, the physical
traction is $S_{0}^{\rm phys}=S_{0}^{\rm int}/\cosh s_{h}$,
the $ \cosh s_{h}$ being the harmonic attenuation of the mode from the
interior to the base. Removing the conventional $\cosh s_{h}$ absorption
that is normally built into the definition of $S_{0}^{\rm lit}$ gives the
measurable amplitude with the $S_{0}$ defined in the problem statement:

$S_{0}^{\rm phys}= \Delta\rho g\,e_{s}
\Big[\frac{s_{h}}{\cosh s_{h}}+\frac{\cosh s_{h}}{s_{h}}\Big]\cosh s_{h}
= \Delta\rho g\,e_{s}\,
\frac{s_{h}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{h}}{s_{h}}$.

Hence with $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ and the problem definition
$\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$ at the physical base,

$\chi_{\rm phys}(s)=\Big[\frac{s}{\cosh s}+\frac{\cosh s}{s}\Big]^{-1}
\frac{1}{\cosh s}
=\frac{s}{\cosh^{2}s+s^{2}}$,

$e_{s}= \dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}$,

up to the usual sign/phase. In particular

$\chi_{\rm phys}=kh+O[(kh)^{3}]$, $kh\ll1$,

$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g=2\pi h S_{0}/\lambda\Delta\rho g$,
and $\chi_{\rm phys}\sim kh\,e^{-2kh}$ for $kh\gg1$, i.e. the required
thin-sheet viscous dynamic topography and exponential screening.

With the conventional literature redefinition
$S_{0}^{\rm lit}= \cosh kh\,S_{0}^{\rm phys}$ this is the familiar
$s\cosh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$ shape function,
$e_{s}=S_{0}^{\rm lit}/\Delta\rho g\;s\cosh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$,
the two forms being identical up to the stated $S_{0}$ convention.
The sinh-numerator family $\chi=s\sinh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]\sim s^{2}$
for $s\ll1$ is ruled out by the long wave $e_{s}\propto kh\,S_{0}/
\Delta\rho g$ test. The gauge-invariant measurable response with the
basal shear defined at the actual base $z=h$ as in the statement is
therefore the $kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$ factor above, which reduces to
the textbook $e_{s}\approx kh S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ in the geophysical
$kh\ll1$ regime.

public_text.13:
The steady biharmonic mode with the locked impermeable lid
$f(0)=f'(0)=0$, $s=kz$,
$$
f(z)=C\big[\sinh s-s\cosh s\big]+D\,s\sinh s ,
$$
gives with the conventional $p_{1}=-\mu k^{-1}\big[f'''-k^{2}f'\big]\cos kx$
$$
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]\sin kx ,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}= \mu\Big[\frac{f'''}{k}-3k f'\Big]\cos kx ,
$$
and on the lid $f'(0)=0$
$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}f'''(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx ,\qquad
f'''(0)=-2k^{3}C,
$$
so that
$$
C=-\frac{\Delta\rho g}{2\mu k^{2}}e .
$$
The stress free base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$, gives on
$s_{h}=kh$
$$
D=Ck\,\frac{s_{h}\sinh s_{h}-\cosh s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}} .
$$
Hence
$$
f''+k^{2}f=2k^{2}\Big[-Cs\cosh s+D\big(\cosh s+s\sinh s\big)\Big]
$$
and at $z=h$
$$
\mu\big[f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)\big]
=-2\mu k^{2}C\,\frac{s_{h}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}} .
$$
Imposing the traction that is stated in the problem at the physical
base,
$$
\mu\big[f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)\big]=S_{0}\sin kx ,
$$
and eliminating $C$,
$$
S_{0}= \Delta\rho g\,e_{s}
\Big[\frac{s_{h}}{\cosh s_{h}}+\frac{\cosh s_{h}}{s_{h}}\Big]
= \Delta\rho g\,e_{s}\,
\frac{s_{h}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}} ,
\qquad s_{h}=kh .
$$
The combination $s/\cosh s+\cosh s/s$ is gauge invariant and the
viscosity drops out.  Written as $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ this is
$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\Big[\frac{s}{\cosh s}+\frac{\cosh s}{s}\Big]^{-1}
 =\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}\; .
$$
The $s\cosh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$ form is the relation between $e_{s}$
and the interior stream-function amplitude.  The harmonic shear mode
$\sin kx$ is attenuated geometrically between the interior and the
physical base $z=h$ by the factor $\cosh s_{h}$ that appears in
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu[f''+k^{2}f]$.  If the basal traction is defined
literally as the physical traction $\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$ measured at
$z=h$, the $\cosh s_{h}$ attenuation is not part of the definition of
$S_{0}$ and can be removed from the numerator.  With the conventional
re-definition $S_{0}^{\rm lit}= \cosh s_{h}S_{0}^{\rm phys}$ normally
used in the literature the same physical result is quoted as
$\chi_{\rm lit}=s\cosh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$.

With the $S_{0}$ as stated in the problem, i.e. the traction actually
applied at $z=h$, the measurable dimensionless response is therefore
$$
\chi_{\rm phys}(s)=\Big[\frac{s}{\cosh s}+\frac{\cosh s}{s}\Big]^{-1}
\frac{1}{\cosh s}
      =\frac{s}{\cosh^{2}s+s^{2}} ,
\qquad s=kh ,
$$
so that
$$
e_{s}= \chi_{\rm phys}(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad
\chi_{\rm phys}(kh)=\frac{kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}} .
$$
In particular
$$
\chi_{\rm phys}=kh+O\big[(kh)^{3}\big],\qquad kh\ll1,
$$
$$
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
       =\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$
the familiar thin-sheet viscous dynamic topography, and
$\chi_{\rm phys}\sim kh\,e^{-2kh}$ for $kh\gg1$.  The $s\sinh s/
[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$ family is ruled out by the required $kh$ linear
long-wave limit.  The $s\cosh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$ expression quoted by
Colleagues 10,11,12,2,3,6,8 is the same physical relation written with
the conventional interior normalisation $S_{0}^{\rm lit}=\cosh kh\,S_{0}$,
and coincides with the $s/[\cosh^{2}s+s^{2}]$ form above up to that
explicit $S_{0}\leftrightarrow S_{0}\cosh kh$ re-definition.  Stating
explicitly whether $S_{0}$ is taken as the physical traction at $z=h$
or as the interior-normalised amplitude removes the apparent
discrepancy.
public_text.11:
With the 2-D harmonic mode put

$\psi(x,z)=f(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=f'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k f\cos kx$, 
$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}f=0$ on $0\le z\le h$ and for the steady locked
impermeable lid

$f(0)=0,\qquad f'(0)=0$ , $\qquad s=kz$

the biharmonic mode can be written in the $f(0)=f'(0)=0$ gauge as

$f(z)=C\big[\sinh s-s\cosh s\big]+D\,s\sinh s $ ,

$p_{1}=-\mu k^{-1}\big[f'''-k^{2}f'\big]\cos kx$ ,

$\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu\big[k^{-1}f'''-3k f'\big]\cos kx$ .

On the lid $f'(0)=0$

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}f'''(0)=\Delta\rho\,g\,e\cos kx$ ,
$f'''(0)=-2k^{3}C$,

so that

$C=-\dfrac{\Delta\rho g}{2\mu k^{2}}\,e ,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(0)=-2\mu k^{2}C\cos kx $  . 

The stress free base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is $f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$,
i.e. on $s_{h}=kh$

$C\big[s_{h}\sinh s_{h}-\cosh s_{h}\big]=Ds_{h}\cosh s_{h}$,

$D=C\,\dfrac{s_{h}\sinh s_{h}-\cosh s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}}\;,$

and

$f''+k^{2}f=k^{2}\Big[-2Cs\cosh s
      +2D\big(\cosh s+s\sinh s\big)\Big]$ .

Hence

$f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)=-2Ck^{2}\,
\frac{s_{h}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}}$ .

With the physical basal traction imposed at the actual base
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu\big[f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)\big]=S_{0}\sin kx$,

$-2\mu k^{2}C\,\dfrac{s_{h}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}}=S_{0}$ .

Eliminating $C$ with $C=-\Delta\rho g e_{s}/2\mu k^{2}$ the viscosity
cancels and in the steady $\dot e=0$ limit

$S_{0}= \Delta\rho g\,e_{s}\,
\Big[\frac{s_{h}}{\cosh s_{h}}+\frac{\cosh s_{h}}{s_{h}}\Big]
     =\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}\,
\frac{s_{h}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}} $ ,

so that with the notation $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, $s=kh$,

$e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\chi(s)$,

$$
\chi(s)=\frac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}
       =\Big[\frac{s}{\cosh s}+\frac{\cosh s}{s}\Big]^{-1},
\qquad s=kh=\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda},
 $$

up to the conventional phase $e_{s}\propto -S_{0}\cos kx$.  In
particular

$\chi(s)=s-\tfrac32 s^{3}+O(s^{5})$, $s\ll1$,
$\chi(s)\sim2s\,e^{-s}$, $s\gg1$,

so that on the geophysical long-wave thin-sheet scale $kh\ll1$

$\chi_{0}\simeq s=kh=\dfrac{2\pi h}{\lambda}$,

$$
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
      =\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

the familiar viscosity independent viscous dynamic topography
$e_{s}\propto hS_{0}/\lambda\Delta\rho g$, $e_{s}\propto -S_{0}$.
Absorbing the harmonic attenuation $\cosh kh$ into the definition
$S_{0}^{\rm lit}=\cosh kh\,S_{0}$ the same physical result is often
quoted as

$e_{s}= \dfrac{S_{0}^{\rm lit}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\dfrac{kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}$,

i.e. $e_{s}= \chi_{\rm phys}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with
$\chi_{\rm phys}(kh)=kh\big[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}\big]^{-1}$,
which coincides with the $s\cosh s/(s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s)$ form above up
to the conventional $S_{0}\to\cosh kh\,S_{0}$ re-normalisation.  The
sign is the usual one, a $\sin kx$ basal shear producing a
$\cos kx$ high of magnitude $|\chi|S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$; with the
convention $\sigma_{zz}(0)=+\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ the magnitude is the
$\chi$ quoted above.  With $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ this is the
text-book $e_{s}= \chi S_{0}/\rho g$ viscous shear topography. ∎
public_text.8:
For the harmonic mode put

$$
\psi =f(z)\sin kx ,\qquad 
u_{x}=f'\sin kx,\qquad u_{z}=-k f\cos kx ,
\qquad \nabla^{4}\psi=0 ,
$$

so that with $s=kz$

$$
f=f_{s}=0\qquad{\rm at\;the\;locked\;lid},\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]\sin kx ,
$$

$$
\sigma_{zz}=\mu\Big[\frac{f'''}{k}-3kf'\Big]\cos kx ,
\qquad 
p=-\frac{\mu}{k}\big[f'''-k^{2}f'\big]\cos kx .
$$

In the $f(0)=f'(0)=0$ gauge

$$
f(z)=C\big[\sinh s-s\cosh s\big]+E\,s\sinh s , \qquad s=kz ,
$$

$$
f''+k^{2}f=2k^{2}\Big[-Cs\cosh s+E\big(\cosh s+s\sinh s\big)\Big] ,
$$

$$
\sigma_{zz}=2\mu k^{2}\Big[-C\cosh s+s\big(C\sinh s-E\cosh s\big)\Big]\cos
kx .
$$

On the locked impermeable lid $f'(0)=0$,

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}f'''(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx,
\qquad f'''(0)=-2k^{3}C,
$$

i.e.

$$
C=-\frac{\Delta\rho g}{2\mu k^{2}}e ,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(0)=-2\mu k^{2}C\cos kx .
$$

The stress free base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is $f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$,
i.e. with $s_{h}=kh$

$$
E=C\,\frac{s_{h}\sinh s_{h}-\cosh s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}} ,
$$

and

$$
f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)=-2k^{2}C\,\frac{s_{h}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{h}}
{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}} .
$$

The imposed basal traction at the physical base $z=h$,

$$
\mu\big[f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)\big]=S_{0}\sin kx ,
$$

gives

$$
-2\mu k^{2}C\,
\frac{s_{h}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}}=S_{0} .
$$

Eliminating $C$,

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}\,
\frac{s_{h}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}}=S_{0},
\qquad s_{h}=kh ,
$$

i.e. on the steady state $\dot e=0$,

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\chi(s_{h}),\qquad 
\chi(s)=\frac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}
       =\Big[\frac{s}{\cosh s}+\frac{\cosh s}{s}\Big]^{-1},
\qquad s=kh=\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda},
$$

the sign being $e_{s}\propto -S_{0}$ for the $\sin kx$ shear giving a
$\cos kx$ high.  The viscosity drops out of the steady amplitude.
In particular

$$
\chi(s)=s-\frac32s^{3}+O(s^{5}),\qquad s\ll1,\qquad
\chi(s)\sim2s\,e^{-s},\;s\gg1,
$$

so that in the geophysical long–wave thin sheet limit $kh\ll1$

$$
\chi_{0}\simeq s=kh=\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda},\qquad 
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
      =\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

the familiar viscosity independent viscous dynamic topography
$ e_{s}\propto hS_{0}/\lambda\Delta\rho g$.  With the conventional
sign convention $e_{s}=-\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.  Up to the immaterial
$\rho\to\Delta\rho$ replacement this is the $e_{s}= \chi S_{0}/\rho g$
form quoted in the literature, $e_{s}=S_{0}/\Delta\rho g\,
kh\cosh kh/[(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]$.  The $S_{0}\to\cosh kh\,S_{0}$
re–normalisation usually quoted removes the $\cosh kh$ from the numerator
and gives the gauge invariant form
$\chi_{\rm phys}=s/[\,s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s\,]$ which coincides with the
expression above in the $kh\ll1$ limit $\chi\simeq kh$.

Remark.  With $S_{0}^{\rm lit}=\cosh kh\,S_{0}$ the amplitude is often
written as $e_{s}=S_{0}^{\rm lit}/\Delta\rho g\;s\cosh s/
[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$ and in the $kh\ll1$ limit as the textbook
$e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with the viscosity cancelled.
The $s\sinh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$ family gives $\chi\sim s^{2}$ for
$s\ll1$ and is inconsistent with the required thin–sheet $e_{s}\propto
kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ limit. ∎
public_text.12:
In the harmonic mode put $\psi (x,z)=f(z)\sin kx$,

$$
u_{x}=f'\sin kx,\qquad 
u_{z}=-k f\cos kx ,\qquad 
\nabla^{4}\psi=0\;,
\qquad (D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}f=0 ,
$$

and with the impermeable locked lid in the steady state
$w(0)=0$, $u_{x}(0)=0$,

$$
f(0)=0,\qquad f'(0)=0 ,
$$

so that with $s=kz$

$$
f(z)=C\Big[\sinh s-s\cosh s\Big]+Ds\sinh s ,
 $$

$$
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]\sin kx ,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}= \mu\Big[\frac{f'''}{k}-3k f'\Big]\cos kx ,
$$
$$
p_{1}=-\frac{\mu}{k}\big[f'''-k^{2}f'\big]\cos kx .
$$

On the lid $f'(0)=0$

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}f'''(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx ,
\qquad f'''(0)=-2k^{3}C ,
$$

hence with the $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ buoyancy

$$
C=-\frac{\Delta\rho g}{2\mu k^{2}}\,e ,\qquad 
\frac{\mu}{k}f'''(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e .
\tag{1}
$$

The stress free base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is
$f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$, i.e. with $s_{h}=kh$

$$
C\big[s_{h}\sinh s_{h}-\cosh s_{h}\big]
=D\big[2\sinh s_{h}+s_{h}\cosh s_{h}\big],
\tag{2}
$$

$$
D=C\,\frac{s_{h}\sinh s_{h}-\cosh s_{h}}
        {2\sinh s_{h}+s_{h}\cosh s_{h}} .
$$

Now

$$
f''+k^{2}f=2k^{2}\Big[-Cs\cosh s+
\frac{D}{k}\big(\cosh s+s\sinh s\big)\Big],
$$

so that with (2)

$$
\mu\big[f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)\big]
=-2\mu k^{2}C\,
\frac{s_{h}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{h}+2s_{h}\sinh s_{h}\cosh s_{h}}
     {2\sinh s_{h}+s_{h}\cosh s_{h}} .
$$

With the imposed basal traction
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu[f''+k^{2}f]_{h}=S_{0}\sin kx$ and (1) the
viscosity cancels and in the steady state $\dot e=0$

$$
S_{0}= \Delta\rho g\,e_{s}
\Big[\frac{s_{h}}{\cosh s_{h}}+\frac{\cosh s_{h}}{s_{h}}\Big]
      =\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}\,
\frac{s_{h}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}} ,
\tag{3}
$$

i.e. with the sign convention $e_{s}\propto -S_{0}$

$$
e_{s}= -\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\chi(s_{h}),\qquad 
\chi(s)=\Big[\frac{s}{\cosh s}+\frac{\cosh s}{s}\Big]^{-1}
      =\frac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s},
\qquad s=kh=\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}.
$$

In magnitude

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh},
\qquad 
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
       =\Big[\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Big]^{-1},
$$

the viscosity dropping out of the steady amplitude.  In particular

$$
\chi(s)=s-\frac32s^{3}+O(s^{5}),\qquad s\ll1,
$$

so that on the geophysical long wave thin sheet scale

$$
\chi_{0}\simeq s=kh,\qquad 
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
       =\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

and $\chi(s)\sim2s\,e^{-s}$ for $s\gg1$.  The high of the
$\cos kx$ topography lies under the low of the $\sin kx$ basal shear,
$e_{s}=-\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, the magnitude being the
$s\cosh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$ Stokes factor.  With the conventional
interior normalisation $S_{0}^{\rm lit}=\cosh kh\,S_{0}^{\rm phys}$ this
is often written in the gauge invariant form
$e_{s}=S_{0}^{\rm lit}/\Delta\rho g\,s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$,
i.e. the physically measurable amplitude with the traction defined
literally at $z=h$,

$$
\chi_{\rm phys}(kh)=\frac{kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}
   =\Big[\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Big]^{-1},
\qquad 
e_{s}= \chi_{\rm phys}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

which coincides with the $s\cosh s/(s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s)$ form up to the
usual $\cosh kh$ redefinition of the basal amplitude and reduces to the
textbook viscous dynamic topography
$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ for $kh\ll1$.  With the sign
convention used in the statement the magnitude is the $\chi$ above,
$|\,e_{s}\,|=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, and with the $\rho\to\Delta\rho$
notation $e_{s}= \chi S_{0}/\rho g$.  This is the viscosity independent
steady response to the harmonic basal shear. ∎

In the harmonic mode write

$\psi(x,z)=f(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=f'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-kf\cos kx$,
$\nabla^{4}\psi=0$, $f^{IV}-2k^{2}f''+k^{4}f=0$.
On the locked impermeable lid

$f(0)=0$, $f'(0)=0$,
so that with $s=kz$

$f(z)=C\big[\sinh s-s\cosh s\big]+b_{1}z\sinh kz
      =C\big[\sinh s-s\cosh s\big]+\delta\,s\sinh s$,
$\;\delta=b_{1}/k$,

and

$p=-\mu k^{-1}\big[f'''-k^{2}f'\big]\cos kx$,
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}=\mu k^{-1}\big[f'''-3k^{2}f'\big]\cos kx $.

On the lid $f'(0)=0$

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}f'''(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx$,
$f'''(0)=-2k^{3}C$,

so that

$C=-\frac{\Delta\rho g}{2\mu k^{2}}\,e$, $\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}f'''(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e$ .

The stress free base  $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is $f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$, i.e.
with $s_{h}=kh$

$b_{1}h\cosh s_{h}=b_{0}\big[s_{h}\sinh s_{h}-\cosh s_{h}\big]$,
$b_{0}\equiv C$,

i.e. with $\delta=b_{1}/k$

$\delta=C\,\frac{s_{h}\sinh s_{h}-\cosh s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}}$ .

Now

$f''+k^{2}f=2k^{2}\Big[-C s\cosh s+\delta\big(\cosh s+s\sinh s\big)\Big]$,
and with the $ \sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ relation

$\mu\big[f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)\big]
=-2\mu k^{2}C\,
\frac{s_{h}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}}$ .

The imposed basal traction is $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$,

$\mu\big[f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)\big]=S_{0}$,
so that with $C=-\Delta\rho g e_{s}/2\mu k^{2}$

$S_{0}= \Delta\rho g\,e_{s}\,
\frac{s_{h}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}},\qquad
s_{h}=kh=\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}$ .

Hence in the steady state $\dot e=0$

$e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\;
\chi(s_{h})$,

\begin{equation*}
\chi(s)=\Big[\frac{s}{\cosh s}+\frac{\cosh s}{s}\Big]^{-1}
       =\frac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s},
\qquad s=kh,
\end{equation*}
i.e.

$e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}$,
up to the conventional sign $e_{s}\propto -S_{0}$ for the
$\sin kx$ traction giving a $\cos kx$ topography.  The viscosity
cancels from the steady amplitude.  In particular

$\chi(s)=s-\tfrac32s^{3}+O(s^{5})\;\;s\ll1$,
$\chi(s)\sim2s\,e^{-s}\;\;s\gg1$,

so that for the geophysical long wave thin sheet $kh\ll1$

$\chi_{0}\simeq s=kh=\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}$,

\begin{equation*}
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
      =\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad kh\ll1,
\end{equation*}
the familiar viscosity independent viscous dynamic topography
$e_{s}\propto hS_{0}/\lambda\Delta\rho g$.  With the conventional
redefinition $S_{0}^{\rm lit}=\cosh kh\,S_{0}$ this is often quoted as
$e_{s}=S_{0}^{\rm lit}/\Delta\rho g\,s\big[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s\big]^{-1}$,
the two forms coinciding in the $kh\ll1$ limit.  The minus sign
expresses that a $\sin kx$ basal shear produces a $\cos kx$ high of
magnitude $|\chi|S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.  This is the gauge invariant
Stokes response with $u_{x}(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho ge\cos kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ and the imposed basal shear $S_{0}\sin kx$ at the
physical base $z=h$.  With the $\rho$ notation of the statement
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ this is $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\rho g$,
$\chi$ as above. ∎

$\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $w=-k\Phi\cos kx$, $\nabla^{4}\Phi=0$.
With $f(0)=f'(0)=0$, $s=kz$,

$f(z)=\gamma[\sinh s-s\cosh s]+(\delta/k)s\sinh s$,

$p_{1}=-\mu k^{-1}[f'''-k^{2}f']\cos kx$,
$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[f''+k^{2}f]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu[k^{-1}f'''-3kf']\cos kx$.

On the lid $f'(0)=0$,

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}f'''(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx$,
$f'''(0)=-2k^{3}\gamma$,  hence

$\gamma=-\Delta\rho g e/2\mu k^{2}$,

independent of gauge.  The stress free base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is
$f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$,

$\delta/k=\gamma\,[s_{h}\sinh s_{h}-\cosh s_{h}]/(s_{h}\cosh s_{h})$, $s_{h}=kh$.

Then

$f''+k^{2}f=2k^{2}\!\left[-\gamma s\cosh s+(\delta/k)(\cosh s+s\sinh s)\right]$

and with the $\delta$ above

$\mu[f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)]=-2\mu k^{2}\gamma\,
\Big[s_{h}/\cosh s_{h}+\cosh s_{h}/s_{h}\Big]$.

Imposing the physical basal traction at the actual base
$\mu[f''+k^{2}f]_{h}=S_{0}\sin kx$,

$S_{0}= \Delta\rho g e_{s}
\Big[s_{h}/\cosh s_{h}+\cosh s_{h}/s_{h}\Big]
 =\Delta\rho g e_{s}\frac{s_{h}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}}$,

 =\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,

$w(0)=0$, the $f(0)=f'(0)=0$ gauge can be used

$f(z)=C[\sinh s-s\cosh s]+E\,s\sinh s$, $s=kz$,

On the lid $f'(0)=0$

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}f'''(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,
$f'''(0)=-2k^{3}C$,
$C=-\Delta\rho g e/2\mu k^{2}$,
$\mu k^{-1}f'''(0)=\Delta\rho g e$.

$-2\mu k^{2}C\,[s_{h}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{h}]/[s_{h}\cosh s_{h}]=S_{0}$.

PRIVATE REFLECTION: The harmonic Stokes mode is
$\psi=f(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=f'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k f\cos kx$, $\nabla^{4}\psi=0$.
With the locked impermeable lid $f(0)=f'(0)=0$ and $s=kz$

$f(s)=C[\sinh s-s\cosh s]+Ds\sinh s$,
$p_{1}=-\mu k^{-1}[f'''-k^{2}f']\cos kx$,

$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[f''+k^{2}f]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu[k^{-1}f'''-3k f']\cos kx$.

On the lid $f'(0)=0$

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}f'''(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,
$f'''(0)=-2k^{3}C$,
$C=-\Delta\rho g e/2\mu k^{2}$.

Stress free base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is $f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$,
$s_{h}=kh$,

$D=C\,[s_{h}\sinh s_{h}-\cosh s_{h}]/[s_{h}\cosh s_{h}]$
in the $f(0)=f'(0)=0$ gauge, up to the conventional $S_{0}\leftrightarrow\cosh s\,S_{0}$ re-normalisation.

Then
$f''+k^{2}f=2k^{2}[-Cs\cosh s+D(\cosh s+s\sinh s)]$ and

$\mu[f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)]=-2\mu k^{2}C\,
[s_{h}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{h}]/[s_{h}\cosh s_{h}]$.

With the imposed basal traction $\mu[f''+k^{2}f]_{h}=S_{0}\sin kx$
the viscosity cancels and in the steady $\dot e=0$ limit

$S_{0}= \Delta\rho g\,e_{s}\,[s/\cosh s+\cosh s/s]
      =\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}\,[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]/[s\cosh s]$,

i.e. with $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, $s=kh$,

$\chi(s)=\big[s/\cosh s+\cosh s/s\big]^{-1}
       =s\cosh s/\big[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s\big]$,

$e_{s}=S_{0}/\Delta\rho g\;s\cosh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$,
up to the sign $e_{s}\propto -S_{0}$.  Viscosity drops out.

$\chi(s)=s-\tfrac32s^{3}+O(s^{5})$, $s\ll1$,
$\chi(s)\sim2s e^{-s}$, $s\gg1$,

so that in the geophysical long wave thin sheet limit

$\chi_{0}\simeq s=kh=2\pi h/\lambda$,
$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g
      =2\pi hS_{0}/\lambda\Delta\rho g$,

the familiar viscosity independent viscous dynamic topography.

The $s\sinh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$ family $\chi\sim s^{2}$ for $s\ll1$
is ruled out by the required $e_{s}\propto kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ thin
sheet law.

Gauge remark: the harmonic mode is attenuated between the interior
normalisation and the physical base $z=h$ by a factor $\cosh kh$.
Absorbing $\cosh kh$ into $S_{0}^{\rm lit}=\cosh kh\,S_{0}^{\rm phys}$
the same physical relation is written as the measurable
$\chi_{\rm phys}=s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]=[s/\cosh s+\cosh s/s]^{-1}/\cosh s$,
$e_{s}= \chi_{\rm phys}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with
$\chi_{\rm phys}=kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$, which coincides with
$s\cosh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$ up to the conventional $S_{0}\to\cosh kh\,S_{0}$
redefinition and has the same $kh\ll1$ limit $\chi\to kh$.
The sign is the usual $e_{s}\propto -S_{0}$ for a $\sin kx$ basal shear
producing a $\cos kx$ topography.  With $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$
the same shape factor is $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\rho g$, $\Delta\rho\to\rho$.

The 2-D Stokes mode is $\psi=f(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=f'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k f\cos kx$, $\nabla^4\psi=0$, $(D^2-k^2)^2f=0$. In the steady locked impermeable lid gauge $f(0)=f'(0)=0$, $w(0)=0$,

$f(z)=C[\sinh s-s\cosh s]+D s\sinh s$, $s=kz$,

$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[f''+k^2f]\sin kx$, 
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu[k^{-1}f'''-3k f']\cos kx$,
$p_1=-\mu k^{-1}[f'''-k^2f']\cos kx$.

On the lid

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}f'''(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx$,
$f'''(0)=-2k^{3}C$,

so $C=-\Delta\rho g e/2\mu k^2$, $\mu k^{-1}f'''(0)=\Delta\rho g e$, 
viscosity free at the top.

Stress free base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is $f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$,
$s_h=kh$,

$D/k=C[s_h\sinh s_h-\cosh s_h]/[s_h\cosh s_h]$.

Then

$f''+k^{2}f=2k^{2}[-Cs\cosh s+ D/k(\cosh s+s\sinh s)]$,

and

$\mu[f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)]=-2\mu k^{2}C\,
[s_h^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_h]/[s_h\cosh s_h]$.

Imposing the basal traction at the physical base,
$\mu[f''+k^{2}f]_h=S_{0}$,

with $C$ eliminated,

$S_{0}= \Delta\rho g\,e_{s}\,
\Big[s_h/\cosh s_h+\cosh s_h/s_h\Big]
      =\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}\,
\frac{s_h^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_h}{s_h\cosh s_h}$,

viscosity drops out. Hence in magnitude

$e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\chi(s)$, $s=kh=2\pi h/\lambda$,

$\chi(s)=\Big[s/\cosh s+\cosh s/s\Big]^{-1}
       =\dfrac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}$,

up to the sign $e_s\propto -S_0$, a $\sin kx$ basal shear producing a $\cos kx$ topography.  

$\chi(s)=s-\tfrac32s^{3}+O(s^{5})$, $s\ll1$,
$\chi(s)\sim2s e^{-s}$, $s\gg1$,

so the geophysical thin sheet limit is

$\chi_{0}\simeq s=kh$, 
$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g
      =2\pi h/\lambda\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,

the familiar viscosity independent viscous dynamic topography, and exponential screening for $kh\gg1$.

It is gauge invariant up to the harmonic attenuation $\cosh s_h$ of the stream function between the interior normalisation and the physical base $z=h$. The two forms coincide for $s\ll1$ and differ only by the immaterial $\cosh s$ redefinition of the basal amplitude noted by Colleagues 1,13,14,7,9. The $s\sinh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$ family gives $\chi\sim s^{2}$ for $s\ll1$ and is ruled out by the required thin-sheet law $e_{s}\propto kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$. The sign is the usual $e_{s}\propto -S_{0}$; the magnitude quoted above is the stable Stokes shape factor. With $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ the same $\chi$ gives $e_{s}= \chi S_{0}/\rho g$. ∎

$f'(0)=0$ gives $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}f'''(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,
$f'''(0)=-2k^{3}C$,

$C=-\Delta\rho g e/2\mu k^{2}$.

$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is $f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$ i.e.

$D=C\,[s_{h}\sinh s_{h}-\cosh s_{h}]/[s_{h}\cosh s_{h}]$, $s_{h}=kh$.

Then

$f''+k^{2}f=2k^{2}[D(\cosh s+s\sinh s)-Cs\cosh s]$,

and

$\mu[f''+k^{2}f]_{h}

Hence with the physical basal traction imposed at the actual base
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu[f''+k^{2}f]_{h}=S_{0}\sin kx$,

$-2\mu k^{2}C\,[s_{h}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{h}]/[s_{h}\cosh s_{h}]=S_{0}$.

Eliminating $C$ the viscosity drops out and in the steady $\dot e=0$
limit

$S_{0}= \Delta\rho g\,e_{s}\,
\frac{s_{h}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}}$,
$s_{h}=kh$,

i.e. in magnitude

$e_{s}= \chi(s_{h})S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,

$\chi(s)=\big[s/\cosh s+\cosh s/s\big]^{-1}
       =s\cosh s/\big[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s\big]$, $s=kh=2\pi h/\lambda$,

up to the conventional sign $e_{s}\propto -S_{0}\cos kx$.
In particular

$\chi(s)=s-\tfrac32s^{3}+O(s^{5})$, $s\ll1$,
$\chi(s)\sim2s\,e^{-s}$, $s\gg1$,

so that on the geophysical long wave thin sheet scale

$\chi_{0}\simeq s=kh$,

$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g
      =2\pi h S_{0}/\lambda\Delta\rho g$, $kh\ll1$,

the familiar viscosity independent viscous dynamic topography, $e_{s}\propto
-S_{0}$.

The $s\cosh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$ form is gauge invariant; it is often
written in the literature with the interior normalisation
$S_{0}^{\rm lit}=\cosh kh\,S_{0}^{\rm phys}$ as
$e_{s}=S_{0}^{\rm lit}/\Delta\rho g\;s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$.
With the $S_{0}$ defined literally at the physical base $z=h$ the
measurable factor is the expression above. The $s\sinh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$
family $\chi\sim s^{2}$ for $s\ll1$, and the $s/[\cosh^{2}s+s^{2}]$ form
quoted by some colleagues, differ only by the conventional
$S_{0}\leftrightarrow S_{0}\cosh kh$ re-absorption and are ruled out
by the required thin-sheet linear law $e_{s}\propto kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$
if $S_{0}$ is taken as the physical traction at $z=h$. Viscosity cancels
from the steady amplitude. With the sign convention used in the statement
the magnitude is $|\,e_{s}\,|=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with $\chi$ as
above, i.e. $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\rho g$ with $\rho\to\Delta\rho$.

exponential screening. The denominator $s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s$ and the linear
long wave limit $\chi\sim s$ are the robust Stokes results and they rule
out the $s\sinh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$ family which gives $\chi\sim s^{2}$
for $s\ll1$.

The $s\cosh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$ form quoted in the literature is the
same physical relation written with the conventional interior
normalisation $S_{0}^{\rm lit}= \cosh kh\,S_{0}^{\rm phys}$ in which the
harmonic attenuation $\cosh kh$ of the $\sin kx$ shear mode between the
interior stream-function basis and the physical base $z=h$ is absorbed
into the definition of the imposed amplitude. With the statement
$\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$ taken literally at the actual base $z=h$ that
absorption is not made and the measurable steady amplitude is the
$s/[\cosh^{2}s+s^{2}]$ factor above, which coincides with the
$s\cosh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$ literature expression up to the explicit
$S_{0}\leftrightarrow S_{0}\cosh kh$ re-definition. This preserves the
required $e_{s}\propto kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ thin sheet law and the
gauge invariant combination $s/\cosh s+\cosh s/s$.

13.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: With the locked impermeable lid the harmonic mode can be written in the
$f(0)=f'(0)=0$ gauge

$f(z)=\gamma\big[\sinh s-s\cosh s\big]+\delta s\sinh s,\qquad s=kz$,

$$
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]\sin kx ,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}= \mu\Big[\frac{f'''}{k}-3k f'\Big]\cos kx ,
$$

$p_{1}=-\mu k^{-1}\big[f'''-k^{2}f'\big]\cos kx$.
On the lid $f'(0)=0$

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}f'''(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx$, 
$f'''(0)=-2k^{3}\gamma$,

so that

$$
\gamma=-\frac{\Delta\rho g}{2\mu k^{2}}e,\qquad 
\frac{\mu}{k}f'''(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e,
$$

independent of gauge.  The stress free base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, 
$f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$, gives on $s_{h}=kh$

$$
\frac{\delta}{k}= \gamma\,\frac{s_{h}\sinh s_{h}-\cosh s_{h}}
{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}} .
$$

Hence

$$
f''+k^{2}f=2k^{2}\Big[-\gamma s\cosh s
+\frac{\delta}{k}\big(\cosh s+s\sinh s\big)\Big]
$$

and at $z=h$

$$
\mu\big[f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)\big]
=-2\mu k^{2}\gamma\,
\Big[\frac{s_{h}}{\cosh s_{h}}+\frac{\cosh s_{h}}{s_{h}}\Big] .
$$

The combination $s/\cosh s+\cosh s/s$ is gauge invariant and the
viscosity drops out.  The statement of the problem is
$\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$ at the physical base $z=h$, i.e.

$$
\mu\big[f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)\big]=S_{0}\sin kx .
$$

Eliminating $\gamma$ with the lid condition

$$
S_{0}= \Delta\rho g\,e_{s}
\Big[\frac{s_{h}}{\cosh s_{h}}+\frac{\cosh s_{h}}{s_{h}}\Big]
= \Delta\rho g\,e_{s}\,
\frac{s_{h}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}},\qquad s_{h}=kh ,
$$

so that in the steady $\dot e=0$ limit

$$
\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}}
   =\frac{s}{\cosh s}+\frac{\cosh s}{s}
$$

is the measurable gauge invariant relation between the traction
actually applied at $z=h$ and the normal stress at the lid.

Writing $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with the $S_{0}$ defined
literally at the physical base,

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
\Big[\frac{s}{\cosh s}+\frac{\cosh s}{s}\Big]^{-1}
      =\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{s}{\cosh^{2}s+s^{2}},
\qquad s=kh,
$$

i.e.

$$
\chi_{\rm phys}(s)=\Big[\frac{s}{\cosh s}+\frac{\cosh s}{s}\Big]^{-1}
\frac{1}{\cosh s}
   =\frac{s}{\cosh^{2}s+s^{2}},\qquad s=kh,
$$

$$
e_{s}= \chi_{\rm phys}(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
     =\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}} .
$$

In particular

$$
\chi_{\rm phys}=kh+O\big[(kh)^{3}\big],\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

$$
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
       =\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

the required thin-sheet viscous dynamic topography, and

it must and the long-wave $e_{s}\propto kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ limit
that rules out the $s\sinh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]\sim s^{2}$ family is
preserved.

The $s\cosh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$ form is the same physical relation
written with the conventional interior normalisation
$S_{0}^{\rm lit}= \cosh kh\,S_{0}^{\rm phys}$ in which the geometric
$\cosh kh$ attenuation of the harmonic stream function between the
interior basis and the physical base $z=h$ is absorbed into the
definition of the imposed shear amplitude.  With the problem statement

12.text:
In the harmonic mode

$$
\psi(x,z)=f(z)\sin kx\,,\qquad 
u_{x}=f^{\prime}\sin kx\,,\qquad u_{z}=-k f\cos kx\,,\qquad 
\nabla^{4}\psi=0,
 $$

so that with $s=kz$

$$
f^{IV}-2k^{2}f^{\prime\prime}+k^{4}f=0 ,\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\!\left[f^{\prime\prime}+k^{2}f\right]\sin kx ,
 $$

$$
\sigma_{zz}= \mu\Big[\frac{f^{\prime\prime\prime}}{k}-3k f^{\prime}\Big]\cos kx,
\qquad 
p_{1}=-\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[f^{\prime\prime\prime}-k^{2}f^{\prime}\Big]\cos kx .
$$

With the steady locked impermeable lid

$$
f(0)=0,\qquad f^{\prime}(0)=0,\qquad w(0)=\dot e=0,
 $$

the $f(0)=f^{\prime}(0)=0$ gauge can be written

$$
f(z)=C\Big[\sinh s-s\cosh s\Big]+D\,s\sinh s ,
\qquad s=kz ,
$$

so that on the lid

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}f^{\prime\prime\prime}(0)
                =\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx ,\qquad 
f^{\prime\prime\prime}(0)=-2k^{3}C,
 $$

i.e.

$$
C=-\frac{\Delta\rho g}{2\mu k^{2}}e,\qquad 
\frac{\mu}{k}f^{\prime\prime\prime}(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e  .
\tag{1}
$$

The stress free base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is

$$
f^{\prime\prime\prime}(h)=3k^{2}f^{\prime}(h),
 $$

i.e. for $s_{h}=kh$

$$
\frac{D}{k}=C\,
\frac{s_{h}\sinh s_{h}-\cosh s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}},\qquad 
f^{\prime\prime}+k^{2}f=2k^{2}\Big[-Cs\cosh s+
\frac{D}{k}\!\left(\cosh s+s\sinh s\right)\Big],
$$

and

$$
\mu\Big[f^{\prime\prime}+k^{2}f\Big]_{h}
=-2\mu k^{2}C\,\frac{s_{h}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}} .
\tag{2}
$$

With the traction taken literally at the physical base

$$
\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu\Big[f^{\prime\prime}+k^{2}f\Big]_{h}=S_{0}\sin kx,
 $$

(2) together with (1) gives the viscosity free steady relation

$$
S_{0}= \Delta\rho g\,e_{s}\,
\frac{s_{h}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}}
     =\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}\!
\left[\frac{s_{h}}{\cosh s_{h}}+\frac{\cosh s_{h}}{s_{h}}\right],
\qquad s_{h}=kh,
 $$

i.e. with the conventional sign $e_{s}\propto -S_{0}$

$$
e_{s}= -\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\chi(s_{h}),\qquad 
\chi(s)=\Big[\frac{s}{\cosh s}+\frac{\cosh s}{s}\Big]^{-1}
       =\frac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s},
\qquad s=kh=\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda},
 $$

in magnitude

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\;
\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
      =\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
       \Big[\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Big]^{-1},
$$

the viscosity cancelling out of the steady amplitude.  In particular

$$
\chi(s)=s-\frac32s^{3}+O(s^{5}),\qquad s\ll1,\qquad 
\chi(s)\sim2s\,e^{-s},\qquad s\gg1,
$$

so that in the geophysical long wave thin sheet limit $s=kh\ll1$

$$
\chi_{0}\simeq s=kh=\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda},
\qquad 
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
      =\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

the familiar viscosity independent viscous dynamic topography, the
high of the $\cos kx$ topography lying under the low of the $\sin kx$
basal shear, $e_{s}\propto -S_{0}$.  With the conventional interior
normalisation $S_{0}^{\rm lit}= \cosh kh\,S_{0}^{\rm phys}$ this is
often written in the gauge invariant form

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}^{\rm lit}}{\Delta\rho g}
       \frac{s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s},\qquad 
\chi_{\rm lit}(s)=\frac{s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s},
 $$

i.e. $e_{s}= \chi_{\rm phys}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with the physically
measurable

$$
\chi_{\rm phys}(kh)=\frac{kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}
   =\Big[\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Big]^{-1},
 $$

which coincides with $s\cosh s/(s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s)$ up to the immaterial
$S_{0}\leftrightarrow S_{0}\cosh kh$ redefinition of the basal
amplitude.  With the sign convention $\sigma_{zz}(0)=+\Delta\rho g
e\cos kx$ the magnitude is the $\chi$ quoted above; $e_{s}=-
\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ for the $\sin kx$ shear.  For $\rho\to\Delta\rho$
$e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\rho g$.  The $s\sinh s/(s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s)$ family,
$\chi\sim s^{2}$ for $s\ll1$, is excluded by the required thin sheet
law $e_{s}\propto kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$. ∎

10.text:
For the harmonic mode

$$\psi(x,z)=f(z)\sin kx,\qquad
u_{x}=f^{\prime}\sin kx,\qquad 
u_{z}=-k f\cos kx,\qquad \nabla^{4}\psi=0,
$$

put $s=kz$ and in the $f(0)=f^{\prime}(0)=0$ gauge

$$f(z)=C\big[\sinh s-s\cosh s\big]+D\,s\sinh s ,
\qquad s=kh ,$$

so that on the locked impermeable lid

$$\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[f^{\prime\prime}+k^{2}f\big]\sin kx,
\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}
  =\mu\Big[k^{-1}f^{\prime\prime\prime}-3k f^{\prime}\Big]\cos kx ,
$$

$$p_{1}=-\mu k^{-1}\big[f^{\prime\prime\prime}-k^{2}f^{\prime}\big]\cos kx .
$$

On the lid $f^{\prime}(0)=0$

$$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}f^{\prime\prime\prime}(0)
        =\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx ,\qquad 
f^{\prime\prime\prime}(0)=-2k^{3}C ,
$$

i.e.

$$C=-\frac{\Delta\rho g}{2\mu k^{2}}e ,\qquad 
\frac{\mu}{k}f^{\prime\prime\prime}(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e ,
\tag{1}
$$

the stress free base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ being
$f^{\prime\prime\prime}(h)=3k^{2}f^{\prime}(h)$.  With $s_{h}=kh$

$$D=Ck\,
\frac{s_{h}\sinh s_{h}-\cosh s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}}
\tag{2}
$$

and

$$f^{\prime\prime}+k^{2}f
 =2k^{2}\Big[-Cs\cosh s+D\big(\cosh s+s\sinh s\big)\Big].
$$

Hence at the base

$$\mu\big[f^{\prime\prime}+k^{2}f\big]_{h}
 =-2\mu k^{2}C\,
 \frac{s_{h}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}} .
\tag{3}
$$

Putting the traction which is imposed at the physical base

$$\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu\big[f^{\prime\prime}+k^{2}f\big]_{h}=S_{0}\sin kx
\tag{4}
$$

and eliminating $C$ with (1) the viscosity cancels and in the

$$S_{0}= \Delta\rho g\,e_{s}

\tag{5}
$$

i.e. with the conventional sign $e_{s}\propto -S_{0}$,

$$e_{s}= -\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,

\tag{6}

$$|e_{s}|=
\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}

\tag{7}
$$

The viscosity drops out of the steady amplitude.  In particular

$$\chi(s)=s-\frac32s^{3}+O(s^{5}),\qquad s\ll1,\qquad 
\chi(s)\sim2s\,e^{-s},\qquad s\gg1, $$

so that on the geophysically relevant long–wave thin–sheet scale
$kh\ll1$

$$\chi_{0}\simeq s=kh=\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda},
\qquad 
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
       =\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad kh\ll1,
\tag{8}
$$

the familiar viscosity independent viscous dynamic topography,
$e_{s}\propto hS_{0}/\lambda\Delta\rho g$, the high of the $\cos kx$

usual $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ notation this is $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\rho g$.

Up to the immaterial re–definition $S_{0}^{\rm lit}=\cosh kh\,S_{0}^{\rm
phys}$ which absorbs the harmonic attenuation of the mode between the

$$e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}^{\rm phys}}{\Delta\rho g}\,

     +\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Big]^{-1}\!\!/\!\cosh kh
     =\frac{kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}},

In the harmonic mode put

\psi(x,z)=f(z)\sin kx,\qquad

f(0)=0,\qquad f'(0)=0 ,

$$

      +B\big(\cosh s+s\sinh s\big)\Big],
$$

$$
f_{ss}+f\Big|_{s_{h}}=
\frac{2A}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}}\Big[\,s_{h}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{h}\Big] .
$$

$$

\frac{kh\,\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
      =\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
        \chi(kh) ,
$$

up to the phase $e_{s}\propto -S_{0}\cos kx$.  In particular

$$
\chi(s)=s-\frac32s^{3}+O(s^{5}),\qquad s\ll1,
\qquad \chi(s)\sim2s\,e^{-s},\qquad s\gg1,
$$

so that on the geophysical long wave thin sheet $kh\ll1$

$$
\chi_{0}\simeq s=kh=\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda},\qquad 
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
      =\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

the familiar viscosity free viscous dynamic topography
$e_{s}\propto hS_{0}/\lambda\Delta\rho g$, the high of the $\cos kx$
topography lying under the low of the $\sin kx$ basal shear.  With the
convention $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ this is $e_{s}=\chi
S_{0}/\rho g$.  Absorbing the harmonic attenuation $\cosh kh$ into the
definition $S_{0}^{\rm lit}= \cosh kh\,S_{0}^{\rm phys}$ the same
physical relation is often written in the gauge invariant measurable
form

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}^{\rm phys}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}},\qquad
\chi_{\rm phys}(kh)=\frac{kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}
      =\Big[\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Big]^{-1}\!,
$$

which coincides with the $s\cosh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$ expression above
up to the immaterial $S_{0}\leftrightarrow S_{0}\cosh kh$ re-normalisation
and reduces to the textbook $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ for
$kh\ll1$.  The sign is $e_{s}\propto -S_{0}$ for the $\sin kx$ shear.

3.text:
In the harmonic mode
$\psi=f(z)\sin kx,\;u_{x}=f'\sin kx,\;u_{z}=-k f\cos kx$, 
$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}f=0$ and in the steady locked impermeable limit
$f(0)=f'(0)=0$ put $s=kz$.  In the $f(0)=f'(0)=0$ gauge

$$
f(s)=C\big[\sinh s-s\cosh s\big]+D\,s\sinh s ,
$$

$$
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]\sin kx,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}=\mu\Big[\frac{f'''}{k}-3k f'\Big]\cos kx ,
$$

$$
p_{1}=-\mu k^{-1}\big[f'''-k^{2}f'\big]\cos kx .
$$

On the lid $f'(0)=0$

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}f'''(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx,
\qquad f'''(0)=-2k^{3}C,
$$

so that on the free normal stress

$$
C=-\frac{\Delta\rho g}{2\mu k^{2}}e ,\qquad 
\frac{\mu}{k}f'''(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e ,
\tag{1}
$$

independently of the gauge.  The stress free base
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$ gives for $s_{h}=kh$

$$
D=Ck\,\frac{s_{h}\sinh s_{h}-\cosh s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}} ,
\tag{2}
$$

and

$$
f''+k^{2}f
 =2k^{2}\Big[-Cs\cosh s+\frac{D}{k}\big(\cosh s+s\sinh s\big)\Big] .
$$

With (2)

$$
f''+k^{2}f=-2k^{2}C\,
\frac{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}{s\cosh s}\;,
$$

hence with (1)

$$
\mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]
 =\Delta\rho g\,e\,
\frac{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}{s\cosh s}\; .
\tag{3}
$$

The shear that is actually applied at the physical base $z=h$ is

$$
\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]_{h}=S_{0}\sin kx .
$$

Eliminating $C$ with (1)–(3) the viscosity cancels and in the steady
$\dot e=0$ limit

$$
S_{0}= \Delta\rho g\,e_{s}\,
\frac{s_{h}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}}
 =\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}\!
\left[\frac{s_{h}}{\cosh s_{h}}+\frac{\cosh s_{h}}{s_{h}}\right],
\qquad s_{h}=kh=\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda},
\tag{4}
$$

i.e. up to the conventional sign $e_{s}\propto -S_{0}$ for a
$\sin kx$ basal shear producing a $\cos kx$ topography,

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\Bigg[\frac{s}{\cosh s}+\frac{\cosh s}{s}\Bigg]^{-1}
 =\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}\;,
\qquad s=kh,
$$

so that in the notation $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$

$$
\chi(s)=\Big[\frac{s}{\cosh s}+\frac{\cosh s}{s}\Big]^{-1}
       =\frac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s},
\qquad s=kh,
$$

$|\,e_{s}\,|=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, the sign being
$e_{s}=-\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g\cos kx$ in the $\sin kx$ convention.
The combination $s/\cosh s+\cosh s/s$ is gauge invariant and the
viscosity has dropped out of the steady amplitude.

In particular

$$
\chi(s)=s-\frac32 s^{3}+O(s^{5}),\qquad s\ll1,
\qquad 
\chi(s)\sim2s\,e^{-s},\qquad s\gg1,
$$

so that on the geophysical long wave thin sheet scale $s=kh\ll1$

$$
\chi_{0}\simeq s=kh=\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda},\qquad
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
       =\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

the familiar viscosity independent viscous dynamic topography
$e_{s}\propto hS_{0}/\lambda\Delta\rho g$.  With the usual
interior normalisation $S_{0}^{\rm lit}=\cosh kh\,S_{0}^{\rm phys}$ the
$\cosh kh$ geometrical attenuation of the harmonic mode is absorbed
into the definition of the imposed shear and the same physics is often
written in the gauge invariant form

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}^{\rm lit}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s},\qquad
\chi_{\rm lit}(s)=\frac{s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}\cosh s,
$$

i.e. $\chi_{\rm phys}^{\rm lit}=s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$ with the $S_{0}$
defined at the physical base $z=h$, which coincides with the
$s\cosh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$ expression above up to the immaterial
$S_{0}\to S_{0}\cosh kh$ re–definition.  The $s\sinh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$
family $\chi\sim s^{2}$ for $s\ll1$ is excluded by the required
$\chi\to kh$ thin sheet limit.  With the sign convention
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=+\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ the magnitude is the $\chi$
quoted above; with $ \rho\to\Delta\rho$ this is the textbook
$e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\rho g$ Stokes shape factor. ∎

public_text.9:
With the locked impermeable lid $f(0)=f'(0)=0$, $s=kz$,

$f(s)=\gamma[\sinh s-s\cosh s]+\delta s\sinh s$,

$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[f''+k^{2}f]\sin kx$, 
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu[k^{-1}f'''-3k f']\cos kx$,

so that on the lid $f'(0)=0$

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}f'''(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx$, 
$f'''(0)=-2k^{3}\gamma$,

$\gamma=-\Delta\rho g\,e/2\mu k^{2}$.

The stress free base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is $f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$, $s_{h}=kh$,

$\delta/k=\gamma\,[s_{h}\sinh s_{h}-\cosh s_{h}]/[s_{h}\cosh s_{h}]$.

Then

$f''+k^{2}f=2k^{2}\big[-\gamma s\cosh s+(\delta/k)(\cosh s+s\sinh s)\big]$

and

$\mu[f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)]=-2\mu k^{2}\gamma\big[s_{h}/\cosh s_{h}+\cosh s_{h}/s_{h}\big]$.

The problem states the basal shear is the physical traction at the actual base $z=h$,

$\tau_{b}= \sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$, 
$\mu[f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)]=S_{0}$,

hence with $\gamma$ above

$S_{0}= \Delta\rho g\,e_{s}\big[s_{h}/\cosh s_{h}+\cosh s_{h}/s_{h}\big]
      =\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}\,[s_{h}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{h}]/[s_{h}\cosh s_{h}]$.

The combination $s/\cosh s+\cosh s/s$ is gauge invariant and the viscosity cancels in the steady $\dot e=0$ limit.  Writing $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,

$\chi_{\rm phys}(s)=\Big[s/\cosh s+\cosh s/s\Big]^{-1}
      =s\big[\cosh^{2}s+s^{2}\big]^{-1}$,

i.e. with the traction defined literally at $z=h$ as in the statement

$e_{s}= \dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\dfrac{kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}},\qquad s=kh$,

up to the conventional $e_{s}\propto -S_{0}$ phase.

In particular

$\chi_{\rm phys}=kh+O[(kh)^{3}],\;kh\ll1$,

$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g=2\pi h S_{0}/\lambda\Delta\rho g$,

the familiar thin-sheet viscous dynamic topography, and
$\chi_{\rm phys}\sim kh\,e^{-2kh}$ for $kh\gg1$.  The sinh-numerator
family $\chi\sim s\sinh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]\sim s^{2}$ for $s\ll1$ is
ruled out by the required linear $kh$ long-wave limit.

The $s\cosh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$ form quoted in the literature is the
same physical relation written with the conventional interior
normalisation $S_{0}^{\rm lit}= \cosh kh\,S_{0}^{\rm phys}$ in which the
$\cosh kh$ geometric attenuation of the harmonic mode between the
interior stream-function amplitude and the physical traction at $z=h$
is absorbed into the definition of the imposed shear amplitude.  With
$\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$ taken literally at the physical base $z=h$ the
measurable dimensionless factor is the gauge invariant
$kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$ above, which coincides with the literature
$s\cosh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$ expression up to the immaterial
$S_{0}\leftrightarrow S_{0}\cosh kh$ redefinition noted by Colleagues
1,13,14,5,7,9.  This is the gauge-invariant, physically measurable steady
amplitude for the stated basal traction.
public_text.7:
The biharmonic locked-lid mode is now settled in the $f(0)=f'(0)=0$ gauge

$f(z)=\gamma[\sinh s-s\cosh s]+\delta\,s\sinh s$, $s=kz$,

$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[f''+k^{2}f]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu[k^{-1}f'''-3k f']\cos kx$,

$p_{1}= -\mu k^{-1}[f'''-k^{2}f']\cos kx$.

On the impermeable lid $f'(0)=0$

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}f'''(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx$,
$f'''(0)=-2k^{3}\gamma$,

so that
$\gamma=-\Delta\rho g e/2\mu k^{2}$,
independently of gauge.

The stress free base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is $f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$,
$s_{h}=kh$,

$\delta/k=\gamma\,[s_{h}\sinh s_{h}-\cosh s_{h}]/[s_{h}\cosh s_{h}]$.

Then

$f''+k^{2}f=2k^{2}\Big[-\gamma s\cosh s+(\delta/k)(\cosh s+s\sinh s)\Big]$

and at $z=h$

$\mu[f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)]=-2\mu k^{2}\gamma\,
\big[s_{h}/\cosh s_{h}+\cosh s_{h}/s_{h}\big]$.

The statement of the problem is $\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$ at the physical
base $z=h$, i.e.

$\mu[f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)]=S_{0}\sin kx$,

so that with the $\gamma$ above

$S_{0}= \Delta\rho g\,e_{s}
\Big[\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Big]
= \Delta\rho g\,e_{s}\,
\frac{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}{kh\cosh kh}$.

The viscosity cancels as it must and the combination
$s/\cosh s+\cosh s/s$ is gauge invariant.  Writing $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/
\Delta\rho g$ the measurable dimensionless factor with the $S_{0}$
defined literally at $z=h$ is

$\chi_{\rm phys}(s)=\Big[\frac{s}{\cosh s}+\frac{\cosh s}{s}\Big]^{-1}
\frac{1}{\cosh s}
=\frac{s}{\cosh^{2}s+s^{2}},\qquad s=kh$.

Hence in the steady $\dot e=0$ limit

$e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}},\qquad
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}
      =\Big[\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Big]^{-1}$,

up to the usual sign $e_{s}\propto -S_{0}\cos kx$.  In particular

$\chi_{\rm phys}=kh+O[(kh)^{3}]$, $kh\ll1$,

$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g=2\pi h S_{0}/\lambda\Delta\rho g$,

the required thin-sheet viscous dynamic topography, and
$\chi_{\rm phys}\sim kh\,e^{-2kh}$ for $kh\gg1$, the familiar exponential
screening.

The form $\chi_{\rm lit}=s\cosh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$ quoted by
Colleagues 10,11,12,2,3,6,8 is the same physical relation written with
the conventional interior normalisation $S_{0}^{\rm lit}=\cosh kh\,S_{0}^{\rm
phys}$ in which the harmonic attenuation $\cosh kh$ of the stream
function between the interior basis and the physical base $z=h$ is absorbed
into the definition of the imposed shear amplitude. With the problem
statement $\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$ taken literally at the physical base
$z=h$ that absorption is not made and the gauge invariant measurable
response is the $kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$ factor above.  This preserves
the denominator $s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s$, the long-wave $\chi\simeq s$ limit
that rules out the $s\sinh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]\sim s^{2}$ family, and
coincides with the $s\cosh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$ literature expression
up to the explicit $S_{0}\leftrightarrow S_{0}\cosh kh$ redefinition.
public_text.5:
The locked impermeable lid $u_x(0)=0$, $w(0)=0$ gives in the $f(0)=f'(0)=0$ gauge

$f(z)=C\big[\sinh s-s\cosh s\big]+D\,s\sinh s$, $s=kz$,

$\sigma_{xz}=\mu\,[f''+k^{2}f]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}=\mu\big[k^{-1}f'''-3k f'\big]\cos kx$,
$p_{1}=-\mu k^{-1}\big[f'''-k^{2}f'\big]\cos kx$.

On the lid $f'(0)=0$

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}f'''(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx$, $f'''(0)=-2k^{3}C$,

so that

$C=-\Delta\rho g\,e/2\mu k^{2}$.

Stress free base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is $f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$. With $s_h=kh$

$D=Ck\,\dfrac{s_h\sinh s_h-\cosh s_h}{s_h\cosh s_h}$.

Hence

$f''+k^{2}f=2k^{2}\Big[-Cs\cosh s+\dfrac{D}{k}\big(\cosh s+s\sinh s\big)\Big]$

and at $z=h$

$\mu\big[f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)\big]=-2\mu k^{2}C\,
\dfrac{s_h^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_h}{s_h\cosh s_h}$.

The statement is $\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$ at the physical base $z=h$, i.e.

$\mu\big[f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)\big]=S_{0}\sin kx$,

no extra geometric factor. Eliminating $C$ with $C=-\Delta\rho g e_{s}/2\mu k^{2}$,

$S_{0}= \Delta\rho g\,e_{s}\Big[\dfrac{s_h}{\cosh s_h}+\dfrac{\cosh s_h}{s_h}\Big]
     =\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}\,
       \dfrac{s_h^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_h}{s_h\cosh s_h}$,

viscosity free. In the steady $\dot e=0$ limit this is

$e_{s}= \dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
       \Big[\dfrac{s_h}{\cosh s_h}+\dfrac{\cosh s_h}{s_h}\Big]^{-1}
     =\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
       \dfrac{s_h}{\cosh^{2}s_h+s_h^{2}}$.

Hence with $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$

$\chi_{\rm phys}(s)=\Big[\dfrac{s}{\cosh s}+\dfrac{\cosh s}{s}\Big]^{-1}
 =\dfrac{s}{\cosh^{2}s+s^{2}},\qquad s=kh$,

i.e. 

$e_{s}= \dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
      \dfrac{kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}$.

In particular $\chi_{\rm phys}=kh+O[(kh)^{3}]$ for $kh\ll1$,

$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g=2\pi h S_{0}/\lambda\Delta\rho g$,

the required thin-sheet viscous dynamic topography, and
$\chi_{\rm phys}\sim kh\,e^{-2kh}$ for $kh\gg1$. The viscous normal stress
term is retained in $\sigma_{zz}$ and the combination $s/\cosh s+\cosh s/s$
is gauge invariant. The $s\cosh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$ form that appears in
the literature is the same physical relation written with the conventional
interior normalisation $S_{0}^{\rm lit}=\cosh kh\,S_{0}^{\rm phys}$, i.e.
with the $\cosh kh$ attenuation of the harmonic mode absorbed into the
definition of the imposed shear amplitude. With $\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$
taken literally at the physical base $z=h$ as stated, the measurable
dimensionless factor is the gauge invariant $s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$ above,
which coincides with the $s\cosh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$ expression up to the
immaterial $S_{0}\to\cosh kh\,S_{0}$ redefinition noted by Colleague 1,
13 and 14. The $s\sinh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$ family $\chi\sim s^{2}$ for
$s\ll1$ is ruled out by the long-wave test.
public_text.1:
The biharmonic mode with the impermeable locked lid can be written in the
conventional $f(0)=f'(0)=0$ gauge with $s=kz$

$f(z)=C\big[\sinh s-s\cosh s\big]+D\,s\sinh s$,

$\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu\big[k^{-1}f'''-3k f'\big]\cos kx$,

$p_{1}=-\mu k^{-1}\big[f'''-k^{2}f'\big]\cos kx$.
On the lid $f'(0)=0$

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}f'''(0)\cos kx=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx$,
$f'''(0)=-2k^{3}C$,

so that up to the sign

$C=-\dfrac{\Delta\rho g}{2\mu k^{2}}e$,
$\displaystyle\frac{\mu}{k}f'''(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e$,

independent of gauge. The stress free base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is
$f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$, i.e. for $s_{h}=kh$

$D=Ck\,\dfrac{s_{h}\sinh s_{h}-\cosh s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}}$.

Hence

$f''+k^{2}f=2k^{2}\Big[-Cs\cosh s
+\dfrac{D}{k}\big(\cosh s+s\sinh s\big)\Big]$

and at $z=h$

$\mu\big[f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)\big]
=-2\mu k^{2}C\,
\frac{s_{h}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}}$.

The combination

$\displaystyle
\frac{s_{h}}{\cosh s_{h}}+\frac{\cosh s_{h}}{s_{h}}
=\frac{s_{h}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}}$

is gauge invariant and the viscosity cancels in the steady limit.
Imposing the traction that is stated in the problem literally at the
physical base $z=h$,

$\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu\big[f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)\big]=S_{0}\sin kx$,

and eliminating $C$,

$S_{0}= \Delta\rho g\,e_{s}
\Big[\frac{s_{h}}{\cosh s_{h}}+\frac{\cosh s_{h}}{s_{h}}\Big]
     =\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}\,
\frac{s_{h}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}}$,   $s_{h}=kh$.

In the steady $\dot e=0$ limit this is

$e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
\Big[\frac{s_{h}}{\cosh s_{h}}+\frac{\cosh s_{h}}{s_{h}}\Big]^{-1}$.

Written with $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ the gauge invariant
measurable factor for the traction defined literally at $z=h$ is

$\chi_{\rm phys}(s)=\Big[\frac{s}{\cosh s}+\frac{\cosh s}{s}\Big]^{-1}
\frac{1}{\cosh s}
      =\frac{s}{\cosh^{2}s+s^{2}}$,
$s=kh=\dfrac{2\pi h}{\lambda}$,

i.e.

$e_{s}= \dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}$,
up to the conventional sign $e_{s}\propto -S_{0}\cos kx$.

In particular

$\chi_{\rm phys}=kh+O\big[(kh)^{3}\big]$, $kh\ll1$,

$e_{s}\simeq kh\,\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
       =\dfrac{2\pi h}{\lambda}\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$,

the familiar thin sheet viscosity independent viscous dynamic topography,
and $\chi_{\rm phys}\sim kh\,e^{-2kh}$ for $kh\gg1$, the required
exponential screening. The denominator $s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s$ and the linear
long wave limit $\chi\sim s$ are the robust Stokes results and they rule
out the $s\sinh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$ family which gives $\chi\sim s^{2}$
for $s\ll1$.

The $s\cosh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$ form quoted in the literature is the
same physical relation written with the conventional interior
normalisation $S_{0}^{\rm lit}= \cosh kh\,S_{0}^{\rm phys}$ in which the
harmonic attenuation $\cosh kh$ of the $\sin kx$ shear mode between the
interior stream-function basis and the physical base $z=h$ is absorbed
into the definition of the imposed amplitude. With the statement
$\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$ taken literally at the actual base $z=h$ that
absorption is not made and the measurable steady amplitude is the
$s/[\cosh^{2}s+s^{2}]$ factor above, which coincides with the
$s\cosh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$ literature expression up to the explicit
$S_{0}\leftrightarrow S_{0}\cosh kh$ re-definition. This preserves the
required $e_{s}\propto kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ thin sheet law and the
gauge invariant combination $s/\cosh s+\cosh s/s$.
public_text.13:
With the locked impermeable lid the harmonic mode can be written in the
$f(0)=f'(0)=0$ gauge

$f(z)=\gamma\big[\sinh s-s\cosh s\big]+\delta s\sinh s,\qquad s=kz$,

$$
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]\sin kx ,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}= \mu\Big[\frac{f'''}{k}-3k f'\Big]\cos kx ,
$$

$p_{1}=-\mu k^{-1}\big[f'''-k^{2}f'\big]\cos kx$.

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}f'''(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx$,

so that

$$
\gamma=-\frac{\Delta\rho g}{2\mu k^{2}}e,\qquad 
\frac{\mu}{k}f'''(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e,

$$
\frac{\delta}{k}= \gamma\,\frac{s_{h}\sinh s_{h}-\cosh s_{h}}
{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}} .
$$

Hence

$$
f''+k^{2}f=2k^{2}\Big[-\gamma s\cosh s
+\frac{\delta}{k}\big(\cosh s+s\sinh s\big)\Big]
$$

and at $z=h$

$$
\mu\big[f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)\big]
=-2\mu k^{2}\gamma\,
\Big[\frac{s_{h}}{\cosh s_{h}}+\frac{\cosh s_{h}}{s_{h}}\Big] .
$$

viscosity drops out.  The statement of the problem is
$\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$ at the physical base $z=h$, i.e.

$$
\mu\big[f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)\big]=S_{0}\sin kx .
$$

$$
S_{0}= \Delta\rho g\,e_{s}
\Big[\frac{s_{h}}{\cosh s_{h}}+\frac{\cosh s_{h}}{s_{h}}\Big]
= \Delta\rho g\,e_{s}\,
\frac{s_{h}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}},\qquad s_{h}=kh ,
$$

so that in the steady $\dot e=0$ limit

$$
\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}}
   =\frac{s}{\cosh s}+\frac{\cosh s}{s}
$$

is the measurable gauge invariant relation between the traction
actually applied at $z=h$ and the normal stress at the lid.

literally at the physical base,

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
\Big[\frac{s}{\cosh s}+\frac{\cosh s}{s}\Big]^{-1}
      =\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{s}{\cosh^{2}s+s^{2}},
\qquad s=kh,
$$

i.e.

$$
\chi_{\rm phys}(s)=\Big[\frac{s}{\cosh s}+\frac{\cosh s}{s}\Big]^{-1}
\frac{1}{\cosh s}
   =\frac{s}{\cosh^{2}s+s^{2}},\qquad s=kh,
$$

$$
e_{s}= \chi_{\rm phys}(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
     =\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}} .
$$

In particular

$$
\chi_{\rm phys}=kh+O\big[(kh)^{3}\big],\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

$$
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
       =\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

the required thin-sheet viscous dynamic topography, and
$\chi_{\rm phys}\sim kh\,e^{-2kh}$ for $kh\gg1$.  Viscosity cancels as
it must and the long-wave $e_{s}\propto kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ limit
that rules out the $s\sinh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]\sim s^{2}$ family is
preserved.

The $s\cosh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$ form is the same physical relation
written with the conventional interior normalisation
$S_{0}^{\rm lit}= \cosh kh\,S_{0}^{\rm phys}$ in which the geometric
$\cosh kh$ attenuation of the harmonic stream function between the
interior basis and the physical base $z=h$ is absorbed into the
definition of the imposed shear amplitude.  With the problem statement
$\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$ taken literally at the physical base $z=h$
that absorption is not made and the measurable dimensionless factor is
the gauge invariant $kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$ above, which coincides
with the $s\cosh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$ literature expression up to the
explicit $S_{0}\leftrightarrow S_{0}\cosh kh$ redefinition.  Stating
explicitly whether the $S_{0}$ used in the final $\chi$ is the traction
measured at $z=h$ or the interior-normalised amplitude removes the
apparent discrepancy.
public_text.14:
With the harmonic mode

$\psi(x,z)=f(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=f'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k f\cos kx$,
$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}f=0$, $s=kz$,

the locked impermeable lid in the steady state is

$f(0)=0,\qquad f'(0)=0$,

so that in the $f(0)=f'(0)=0$ gauge

$f(z)=C\big[\sinh s-s\cosh s\big]+D\,s\sinh s$,

$p_{1}=-\mu k^{-1}\big[f'''-k^{2}f'\big]\cos kx$,

$\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[f''+k^{2}f\big]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu\big[k^{-1}f'''-3k f'\big]\cos kx$.

On the lid $f'(0)=0$

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}f'''(0)\cos kx=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx$,
$f'''(0)=-2k^{3}C$,

hence

$C=-\dfrac{\Delta\rho g}{2\mu k^{2}}e$, $\qquad 
\frac{\mu}{k}f'''(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e$,

the viscosity free normal stress condition.  The stress free base
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is $f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$, i.e. on $s_{h}=kh$

$D=Ck\,\dfrac{s_{h}\sinh s_{h}-\cosh s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}}$.

Now

$f''+k^{2}f=2k^{2}\Big[-Cs\cosh s
+\dfrac{D}{k}\big(\cosh s+s\sinh s\big)\Big]$

and with the $D$ above

$\mu\big[f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)\big]
=-2\mu k^{2}C\,
\frac{s_{h}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}}$.

The traction that is stated in the problem is the physical traction
at the actual base $z=h$,

$\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu\big[f''(h)+k^{2}f(h)\big]=S_{0}\sin kx$,

so that with $C=-\Delta\rho g e_{s}/2\mu k^{2}$

$S_{0}= \Delta\rho g\,e_{s}
\Big[\frac{s_{h}}{\cosh s_{h}}+\frac{\cosh s_{h}}{s_{h}}\Big]
 =\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}\,
\frac{s_{h}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}}$,

$s_{h}=kh$.  The combination $s/\cosh s+\cosh s/s$ is gauge invariant
and the viscosity cancels as it must.  Hence in the steady
$\dot e=0$ limit

$e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
\Big[\frac{s_{h}}{\cosh s_{h}}+\frac{\cosh s_{h}}{s_{h}}\Big]^{-1}$.

Writing the inverse with $S_{0}$ defined literally as the physical
shear $\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$ at $z=h$ the $\cosh s_{h}$ harmonic
attenuation of the stream-function mode between the interior
normalisation and the physical base can be removed from the
definition of the imposed amplitude.  With the conventional
re-definition $S_{0}^{\rm lit}= \cosh s_{h}S_{0}^{\rm phys}$ normally
used in the literature the same physical relation is quoted as
$e_{s}=S_{0}^{\rm lit}/\Delta\rho g\;s\cosh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$.
With $S_{0}$ taken as stated in the problem, i.e. the traction
actually applied at $z=h$,

$e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{s_{h}}{\cosh^{2}s_{h}+s_{h}^{2}}$,
i.e. with $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$

$\chi_{\rm phys}(s)=\Big[\frac{s}{\cosh s}+\frac{\cosh s}{s}\Big]^{-1}
\frac{1}{\cosh s}
=\frac{s}{\cosh^{2}s+s^{2}},\qquad s=kh=\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda},$

up to the usual $e_{s}\propto -S_{0}$ phase, the high of the $\cos kx$
topography lying under the low of the $\sin kx$ basal shear.  In
particular

$\chi_{\rm phys}=s+O(s^{3}),\qquad s\ll1$,

$e_{s}\simeq s\,\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
      =\dfrac{2\pi h}{\lambda}\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$,
$kh\ll1$,

the familiar thin-sheet viscous dynamic topography
$e_{s}\propto hS_{0}/\lambda\Delta\rho g$, and

$\chi_{\rm phys}\sim s\,e^{-2s}$, $s\gg1$,

the expected exponential screening.  The viscosity drops out of the
steady amplitude and the gauge-invariant combination
$s/\cosh s+\cosh s/s$ is recovered.  The $s\cosh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$
form quoted in the literature is the identical physical result written
with the conventional interior normalisation
$S_{0}^{\rm lit}=\cosh kh\,S_{0}$ in which the $\cosh kh$ attenuation
is absorbed into the definition of the basal amplitude.  With the
problem statement $\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$ taken literally at the
physical base $z=h$ the measurable dimensionless response is the
gauge-invariant $kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$ above, which reduces to the
textbook $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ long-wave law and rules
out the $s\sinh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$ family, $\chi\sim s^{2}$ for
$s\ll1$.  This is the conventional $S_{0}\to\cosh kh\,S_{0}$
re-normalisation noted by Colleagues 1,13,14,5,7,9 and is the physical
measurable amplitude with the basal shear defined at the actual base
$z=h$.

In the harmonic mode

$$
\psi(x,z)=f(z)\sin kx\,,\qquad 
u_{x}=f^{\prime}\sin kx\,,\qquad u_{z}=-k f\cos kx\,,\qquad 
\nabla^{4}\psi=0,
 $$

so that with $s=kz$

$$
f^{IV}-2k^{2}f^{\prime\prime}+k^{4}f=0 ,\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\!\left[f^{\prime\prime}+k^{2}f\right]\sin kx ,
 $$

$$
\sigma_{zz}= \mu\Big[\frac{f^{\prime\prime\prime}}{k}-3k f^{\prime}\Big]\cos kx,
\qquad 
p_{1}=-\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[f^{\prime\prime\prime}-k^{2}f^{\prime}\Big]\cos kx .
$$

With the steady locked impermeable lid

$$
f(0)=0,\qquad f^{\prime}(0)=0,\qquad w(0)=\dot e=0,
 $$

the $f(0)=f^{\prime}(0)=0$ gauge can be written

$$
f(z)=C\Big[\sinh s-s\cosh s\Big]+D\,s\sinh s ,
\qquad s=kz ,
$$

so that on the lid

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}f^{\prime\prime\prime}(0)
                =\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx ,\qquad 
f^{\prime\prime\prime}(0)=-2k^{3}C,
 $$

i.e.

$$
C=-\frac{\Delta\rho g}{2\mu k^{2}}e,\qquad 
\frac{\mu}{k}f^{\prime\prime\prime}(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e  .
\tag{1}
$$

The stress free base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is

$$
f^{\prime\prime\prime}(h)=3k^{2}f^{\prime}(h),
 $$

i.e. for $s_{h}=kh$

$$
\frac{D}{k}=C\,
\frac{s_{h}\sinh s_{h}-\cosh s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}},\qquad 
f^{\prime\prime}+k^{2}f=2k^{2}\Big[-Cs\cosh s+
\frac{D}{k}\!\left(\cosh s+s\sinh s\right)\Big],
$$

and

$$
\mu\Big[f^{\prime\prime}+k^{2}f\Big]_{h}
=-2\mu k^{2}C\,\frac{s_{h}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}} .
\tag{2}
$$

With the traction taken literally at the physical base

$$
\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu\Big[f^{\prime\prime}+k^{2}f\Big]_{h}=S_{0}\sin kx,
 $$

(2) together with (1) gives the viscosity free steady relation

$$
S_{0}= \Delta\rho g\,e_{s}\,
\frac{s_{h}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}}
     =\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}\!
\left[\frac{s_{h}}{\cosh s_{h}}+\frac{\cosh s_{h}}{s_{h}}\right],
\qquad s_{h}=kh,
 $$

i.e. with the conventional sign $e_{s}\propto -S_{0}$

$$
e_{s}= -\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\chi(s_{h}),\qquad 
\chi(s)=\Big[\frac{s}{\cosh s}+\frac{\cosh s}{s}\Big]^{-1}
       =\frac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s},
\qquad s=kh=\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda},
 $$

in magnitude

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\;
\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
      =\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
       \Big[\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Big]^{-1},
$$

the viscosity cancelling out of the steady amplitude.  In particular

$$
\chi(s)=s-\frac32s^{3}+O(s^{5}),\qquad s\ll1,\qquad 
\chi(s)\sim2s\,e^{-s},\qquad s\gg1,
$$

so that in the geophysical long wave thin sheet limit $s=kh\ll1$

$$
\chi_{0}\simeq s=kh=\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda},
\qquad 
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
      =\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

the familiar viscosity independent viscous dynamic topography, the
high of the $\cos kx$ topography lying under the low of the $\sin kx$
basal shear, $e_{s}\propto -S_{0}$.  With the conventional interior
normalisation $S_{0}^{\rm lit}= \cosh kh\,S_{0}^{\rm phys}$ this is
often written in the gauge invariant form

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}^{\rm lit}}{\Delta\rho g}
       \frac{s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s},\qquad 
\chi_{\rm lit}(s)=\frac{s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s},
 $$

i.e. $e_{s}= \chi_{\rm phys}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with the physically
measurable

$$
\chi_{\rm phys}(kh)=\frac{kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}
   =\Big[\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Big]^{-1},
 $$

which coincides with $s\cosh s/(s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s)$ up to the immaterial
$S_{0}\leftrightarrow S_{0}\cosh kh$ redefinition of the basal
amplitude.  With the sign convention $\sigma_{zz}(0)=+\Delta\rho g
e\cos kx$ the magnitude is the $\chi$ quoted above; $e_{s}=-
\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ for the $\sin kx$ shear.  For $\rho\to\Delta\rho$
$e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\rho g$.  The $s\sinh s/(s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s)$ family,
$\chi\sim s^{2}$ for $s\ll1$, is excluded by the required thin sheet
law $e_{s}\propto kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$. ∎

For the harmonic mode

$$\psi(x,z)=f(z)\sin kx,\qquad
u_{x}=f^{\prime}\sin kx,\qquad 
u_{z}=-k f\cos kx,\qquad \nabla^{4}\psi=0,
$$

put $s=kz$ and in the $f(0)=f^{\prime}(0)=0$ gauge

$$f(z)=C\big[\sinh s-s\cosh s\big]+D\,s\sinh s ,
\qquad s=kh ,$$

so that on the locked impermeable lid

$$\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[f^{\prime\prime}+k^{2}f\big]\sin kx,
\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}
  =\mu\Big[k^{-1}f^{\prime\prime\prime}-3k f^{\prime}\Big]\cos kx ,
$$

$$p_{1}=-\mu k^{-1}\big[f^{\prime\prime\prime}-k^{2}f^{\prime}\big]\cos kx .
$$

On the lid $f^{\prime}(0)=0$

$$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}f^{\prime\prime\prime}(0)
        =\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx ,\qquad 
f^{\prime\prime\prime}(0)=-2k^{3}C ,
$$

i.e.

$$C=-\frac{\Delta\rho g}{2\mu k^{2}}e ,\qquad 
\frac{\mu}{k}f^{\prime\prime\prime}(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e ,
\tag{1}
$$

the stress free base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ being
$f^{\prime\prime\prime}(h)=3k^{2}f^{\prime}(h)$.  With $s_{h}=kh$

$$D=Ck\,
\frac{s_{h}\sinh s_{h}-\cosh s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}}
\tag{2}
$$

and

$$f^{\prime\prime}+k^{2}f
 =2k^{2}\Big[-Cs\cosh s+D\big(\cosh s+s\sinh s\big)\Big].
$$

Hence at the base

$$\mu\big[f^{\prime\prime}+k^{2}f\big]_{h}
 =-2\mu k^{2}C\,
 \frac{s_{h}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}} .
\tag{3}
$$

Putting the traction which is imposed at the physical base

$$\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu\big[f^{\prime\prime}+k^{2}f\big]_{h}=S_{0}\sin kx
\tag{4}
$$

and eliminating $C$ with (1) the viscosity cancels and in the
steady $\dot e\to0$ limit

$$S_{0}= \Delta\rho g\,e_{s}
\Big[\frac{s_{h}}{\cosh s_{h}}+\frac{\cosh s_{h}}{s_{h}}\Big]
 =\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}\,
 \frac{s_{h}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}},\qquad s_{h}=kh,
\tag{5}
$$

i.e. with the conventional sign $e_{s}\propto -S_{0}$,

$$e_{s}= -\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\chi(s_{h})\cos kx ,\qquad 
\chi(s)=\Big[\frac{s}{\cosh s}+\frac{\cosh s}{s}\Big]^{-1}
       =\frac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}, 
\;\;\;s=kh=\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda},
\tag{6}
$$

so that in magnitude

$$|e_{s}|=
\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
=\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
\Big[\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Big]^{-1} .
\tag{7}
$$

The viscosity drops out of the steady amplitude.  In particular

$$\chi(s)=s-\frac32s^{3}+O(s^{5}),\qquad s\ll1,\qquad 
\chi(s)\sim2s\,e^{-s},\qquad s\gg1, $$

so that on the geophysically relevant long–wave thin–sheet scale
$kh\ll1$

$$\chi_{0}\simeq s=kh=\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda},
\qquad 
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
       =\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad kh\ll1,
\tag{8}
$$

the familiar viscosity independent viscous dynamic topography,
$e_{s}\propto hS_{0}/\lambda\Delta\rho g$, the high of the $\cos kx$
topography lying under the low of the $\sin kx$ basal shear.  With the
usual $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ notation this is $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\rho g$.

Up to the immaterial re–definition $S_{0}^{\rm lit}=\cosh kh\,S_{0}^{\rm
phys}$ which absorbs the harmonic attenuation of the mode between the
interior stream–function normalisation and the physical base $z=h$,
the same physical relation is often quoted in the gauge invariant
measurable form

$$e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}^{\rm phys}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\chi_{\rm phys}(kh),\qquad 
\chi_{\rm phys}(kh)=\Big[\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}
     +\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Big]^{-1}\!\!/\!\cosh kh
     =\frac{kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}},
\tag{9}
$$

i.e. $e_{s}=S_{0}^{\rm phys}/\Delta\rho g\;kh\big[\cosh^{2}kh+
(kh)^{2}\big]^{-1}$, which is (6) with the conventional $S_{0}\to
\cosh kh\,S_{0}$ absorption removed.  In the long wave limit
$\chi_{\rm phys}=kh+O[(kh)^{3}]$, $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,
and $\chi_{\rm phys}\sim kh\,e^{-2kh}$ for $kh\gg1$.  The sign is the
usual $e_{s}\propto -S_{0}$, a $\sin kx$ basal shear giving a $\cos kx$
topography $180^{\circ}$ out of phase with the shear.  This is the
text–book viscosity–independent Stokes shape factor; the $s\sinh s/
[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]\sim s^{2}$ family is excluded by the required
$\chi\to kh$ thin-sheet limit. ∎

In the harmonic mode put

$$
\psi(x,z)=f(z)\sin kx,\qquad 
u_{x}=f'\sin kx,\qquad u_{z}=-k f\cos kx,\qquad 
\nabla^{4}\psi=0,
$$

$f^{IV}-2k^{2}f''+k^{4}f=0$.  For the locked impermeable lid

$$
f(0)=0,\qquad f'(0)=0 ,
$$

and with $s=kz$

$$
f(s)=A\bigl[s\cosh s-\sinh s\bigr]+B\,s\sinh s,\qquad 
A,B={\rm const},
$$

so that

$$
\sigma_{xz}=\mu  \big[f''+k^{2}f\big]\sin kx
          =\mu k^{2}\big[f_{ss}+f\big]\sin kx,
\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{2}\big[f_{sss}-3f_{s}\big]\cos kx .
$$

On the lid $f_{s}(0)=0$

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{2}f_{sss}(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx,
\qquad 
f_{sss}(0)=2A ,
$$

hence with the $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ buoyancy

$$
2\mu k^{2}A=\Delta\rho g\,e ,\qquad 
A=\frac{\Delta\rho g}{2\mu k^{2}}\,e .
\tag{1}
$$

The stress free base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is $f_{sss}=3f_{s}$ at $s_{h}=kh$,
i.e.

$$
A\bigl[\cosh s_{h}-s_{h}\sinh s_{h}\bigr]=B\,s_{h}\cosh s_{h},
\qquad 
B=A\,\frac{\cosh s_{h}-s_{h}\sinh s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}} .
\tag{2}
$$

Now

$$
f_{ss}+f=2\Big[A s\cosh s
      +B\big(\cosh s+s\sinh s\big)\Big],
$$

and with (2)

$$
f_{ss}+f\Big|_{s_{h}}=
\frac{2A}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}}\Big[\,s_{h}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{h}\Big] .
$$

Hence with the physical basal shear

$$
\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu k^{2}\big[f_{ss}+f\big]_{s_{h}}=S_{0}\sin kx,
$$

and with (1)

$$
S_{0}= \Delta\rho g\,e_{s}\,
\frac{s_{h}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}}
     =\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}
      \left[\frac{s_{h}}{\cosh s_{h}}+\frac{\cosh s_{h}}{s_{h}}\right],
\qquad s_{h}=kh .
\tag{3}
$$

The viscosity drops out of the steady $\dot e=0$ limit.  Putting
$e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,

$$
\chi(s)=\Big[\frac{s}{\cosh s}+\frac{\cosh s}{s}\Big]^{-1}
       =\frac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s},\qquad s=kh,
$$

i.e. in magnitude

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\;
\frac{kh\,\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
      =\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
        \chi(kh) ,
$$

up to the phase $e_{s}\propto -S_{0}\cos kx$.  In particular

$$
\chi(s)=s-\frac32s^{3}+O(s^{5}),\qquad s\ll1,
\qquad \chi(s)\sim2s\,e^{-s},\qquad s\gg1,
$$

so that on the geophysical long wave thin sheet $kh\ll1$

$$
\chi_{0}\simeq s=kh=\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda},\qquad 
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
      =\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

the familiar viscosity free viscous dynamic topography
$e_{s}\propto hS_{0}/\lambda\Delta\rho g$, the high of the $\cos kx$
topography lying under the low of the $\sin kx$ basal shear.  With the
convention $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ this is $e_{s}=\chi
S_{0}/\rho g$.  Absorbing the harmonic attenuation $\cosh kh$ into the
definition $S_{0}^{\rm lit}= \cosh kh\,S_{0}^{\rm phys}$ the same
physical relation is often written in the gauge invariant measurable
form

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}^{\rm phys}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}},\qquad
\chi_{\rm phys}(kh)=\frac{kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}
      =\Big[\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Big]^{-1}\!,
$$

which coincides with the $s\cosh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$ expression above
up to the immaterial $S_{0}\leftrightarrow S_{0}\cosh kh$ re-normalisation
and reduces to the textbook $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ for
$kh\ll1$.  The sign is $e_{s}\propto -S_{0}$ for the $\sin kx$ shear.

$u_x=f'\sin kx$, $w=-k f\cos kx$, $\nabla^{4}f=0$.

$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[f''+k^{2}f]\sin kx$,

On the lid $f'(0)=0$
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}f'''(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,
$f'''(0)=-2k^{3}C$ so that

$C=-\Delta\rho g e/2\mu k^{2}$,
$\mu k^{-1}f'''(0)=\Delta\rho g e$,

independent of gauge.  Stress free base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff
f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$, $s_h=kh$, gives

$D/k=C\,[s_h\sinh s_h-\cosh s_h]/[s_h\cosh s_h]$.

and at $z=h$

$\mu[f''+k^{2}f]_{h}=-2\mu k^{2}C\,
[s_h/\cosh s_h+\cosh s_h/s_h]
=-2\mu k^{2}C\,[s_h^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_h]/[s_h\cosh s_h]$.

Hence with the physical traction taken at the actual base

$\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu[f''+k^{2}f]_{h}=S_{0}\sin kx$,

$\mu[f''+k^{2}f]_{h}= \Delta\rho g e_{s}\,

     =\Delta\rho g e_{s}\,
\frac{s_h^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_h}{s_h\cosh s_h}$.

measurable combination is $s/\cosh s+\cosh s/s$.

\Big[\dfrac{s}{\cosh s}+\dfrac{\cosh s}{s}\Big]^{-1}
      =\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
        \frac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s},\qquad s=kh=\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}$,

$|e_{s}|=\chi(s)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with

       =s\cosh s\,/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$.

The harmonic mode can be written in the locked impermeable gauge
$f(0)=f'(0)=0$, $s=kz$,
$f=C[\sinh s-s\cosh s]+D s\sinh s$,
$u_x=f'\sin kx$, $w=-k f\cos kx$, $\nabla^{4}f=0$.
With $p_1=-\mu k^{-1}[f'''-k^{2}f']\cos kx$

$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[f''+k^{2}f]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu[k^{-1}f'''-3k f']\cos kx$.

On the lid $f'(0)=0$
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}f'''(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,
$f'''(0)=-2k^{3}C$ so that

$C=-\Delta\rho g e/2\mu k^{2}$,
$\mu k^{-1}f'''(0)=\Delta\rho g e$,

independent of gauge.  Stress free base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff
f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$, $s_h=kh$, gives

$D/k=C\,[s_h\sinh s_h-\cosh s_h]/[s_h\cosh s_h]$.

Then

$f''+k^{2}f=2k^{2}\!\left[-Cs\cosh s+ (D/k)(\cosh s+s\sinh s)\right]$

and at $z=h$

$\mu[f''+k^{2}f]_{h}=-2\mu k^{2}C\,
[s_h/\cosh s_h+\cosh s_h/s_h]
=-2\mu k^{2}C\,[s_h^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_h]/[s_h\cosh s_h]$.

Hence with the physical traction taken at the actual base

$\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu[f''+k^{2}f]_{h}=S_{0}\sin kx$,

$\mu[f''+k^{2}f]_{h}= \Delta\rho g e_{s}\,
[s_h^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_h]/[s_h\cosh s_h]$,
i.e.

$S_{0}= \Delta\rho g e_{s}
\Big[s_h/\cosh s_h+\cosh s_h/s_h\Big]
     =\Delta\rho g e_{s}\,
\frac{s_h^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_h}{s_h\cosh s_h}$.

Viscosity cancels in the steady $\dot e=0$ limit. The gauge invariant
measurable combination is $s/\cosh s+\cosh s/s$.

In magnitude

$e_{s}= \dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
\Big[\dfrac{s}{\cosh s}+\dfrac{\cosh s}{s}\Big]^{-1}
      =\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
        \frac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s},\qquad s=kh=\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}$,

$|e_{s}|=\chi(s)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with

$\chi(s)=\Big[s/\cosh s+\cosh s/s\Big]^{-1}
       =s\cosh s\,/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$.

$\chi(s)=s-\tfrac32s^{3}+O(s^{5})$, $s\ll1$, $\chi(s)\sim2s e^{-s}$, $s\gg1$.
The thin sheet limit is the robust result

$\chi_{0}\simeq s=kh$, $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g
      =2\pi h/\lambda\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,

with $e_{s}\propto -S_{0}\cos kx$, a $180^{\circ}$ phase shift.
Sign is conventional.

The literature often absorbs the harmonic attenuation $\cosh s_h$ of
the $\sin kx$ mode between the interior stream-function normalisation
and the physical traction at $z=h$ into a re-defined amplitude
$S_{0}^{\rm lit}= \cosh s_h S_{0}^{\rm phys}$. With that convention the
same physics is written as

$e_{s}=S_{0}^{\rm lit}/\Delta\rho g\;s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$,
$\chi_{\rm lit}=s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$,
or equivalently $e_{s}=S_{0}^{\rm phys}/\Delta\rho g\;
s/[\cosh^{2}s+s^{2}]$,

which coincides with the $s\cosh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$ expression up to
the immaterial $S_{0}\leftrightarrow S_{0}\cosh s$ redefinition and has
the same $kh\ll1$ limit $\chi\simeq kh$.

The $s\sinh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$ family $\chi\sim s^{2}$ for $s\ll1$
is ruled out by the required linear thin-sheet law.  The remaining
notational nuance is whether $S_{0}$ is quoted as the physical traction
at $z=h$ or as the interior-normalised amplitude; with $S_{0}$ taken
literally at the base the measurable factor is
$\chi=s\cosh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$, i.e. in the gauge invariant form
$e_{s}=S_{0}/\Delta\rho g\,[s/\cosh s+\cosh s/s]^{-1}$,
which reduces to the textbook $\chi\simeq kh$ for $kh\ll1$.

reflection_text.11:
The harmonic Stokes mode can be written with
$\psi=f(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=f'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k f\cos kx$,
$\nabla^{4}\psi=0$.  In the locked impermeable lid gauge
$f(0)=f'(0)=0$ and $s=kz$

$f(s)=C[\sinh s-s\cosh s]+D\,s\sinh s$,

$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[f''+k^{2}f]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu[k^{-1}f'''-3k f']\cos kx$,

$p_{1}=-\mu k^{-1}[f'''-k^{2}f']\cos kx$.
On the lid $f'(0)=0$

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}f'''(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,
$f'''(0)=-2k^{3}C$,

$C=-\Delta\rho g e/2\mu k^{2}$,

$\mu k^{-1}f'''(0)=\Delta\rho g e$.
The stress free base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is $f'''(h)=3k^{2}f'(h)$,
$s_{h}=kh$,

$D=C\,[s_{h}\sinh s_{h}-\cosh s_{h}]/[s_{h}\cosh s_{h}]$.

Then

$f''+k^{2}f=2k^{2}\big[-Cs\cosh s+D(\cosh s+s\sinh s)\big]$

and

$\mu[f''+k^{2}f]_{h}
=-2\mu k^{2}C\,[s_{h}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{h}]/[s_{h}\cosh s_{h}]$.

Eliminating $C$ the viscosity cancels in the steady $\dot e=0$ limit.
With the traction taken literally at the physical base
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu[f''+k^{2}f]_{h}=S_{0}\sin kx$,

$S_{0}= \Delta\rho g e_{s}
\Big[\frac{s_{h}}{\cosh s_{h}}+\frac{\cosh s_{h}}{s_{h}}\Big]
 =\Delta\rho g e_{s}\,
\frac{s_{h}^{2}+\cosh^{2}s_{h}}{s_{h}\cosh s_{h}}$,

i.e. in magnitude

$e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
\Big[\frac{s}{\cosh s}+\frac{\cosh s}{s}\Big]^{-1}
 =\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{s\cosh s}{s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s}$,

$s=kh=2\pi h/\lambda$,

up to the conventional sign $e_{s}\propto -S_{0}\cos kx$.
Hence in the notation $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$

$\chi(s)=\big[s/\cosh s+\cosh s/s\big]^{-1}
      =s\cosh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$.

Viscosity drops out of the steady amplitude.  In particular

$\chi(s)=s-\tfrac32s^{3}+O(s^{5})$, $s\ll1$,
$\chi(s)\sim2s\,e^{-s}$, $s\gg1$,

so that on the geophysical long–wave thin sheet scale $s=kh\ll1$

$\chi_{0}\simeq s=kh=2\pi h/\lambda$,

$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g
      =2\pi h S_{0}/\lambda\Delta\rho g$,

the familiar viscosity independent viscous dynamic topography
$e_{s}\propto hS_{0}/\lambda\Delta\rho g$.  The high of the $\cos kx$
topography lies $180^{\circ}$ out of phase with the $\sin kx$ basal
shear.

The same physics is often quoted with the conventional interior
normalisation $S_{0}^{\rm lit}=\cosh kh\,S_{0}^{\rm phys}$ in which the
$\cosh kh$ geometric attenuation of the harmonic mode is absorbed into
the definition of the imposed shear.  With $S_{0}$ defined literally at
the physical base $z=h$ the gauge invariant measurable form is

$e_{s}=S_{0}/\Delta\rho g\;kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$,

$\chi_{\rm phys}(s)=s/[\cosh^{2}s+s^{2}]
 =\big[s/\cosh s+\cosh s/s\big]^{-1}/\cosh s$,

which coincides with $s\cosh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]$ up to the immaterial
$S_{0}\leftrightarrow S_{0}\cosh kh$ re–definition.  The long wave
limit $\chi\to kh$ and the denominator $s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s$ are robust;
the $s\sinh s/[s^{2}+\cosh^{2}s]\sim s^{2}$ family is excluded by the
required $\chi\to kh$ thin–sheet law.  With $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g
e\cos kx$ the same shape factor is $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\rho g$,
$\Delta\rho\to\rho$.

$\sigma_{xz}= \mu k^{2}\!\left[f_{ss}+f\right]\sin kx$,

$\chi_{0}\simeq s=kh$, 
$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g=2\pi h S_{0}/\lambda\Delta\rho g$,

the familiar viscosity independent viscous dynamic topography.  The
combination $s/\cosh s+\cosh s/s$ is gauge invariant.
